questionsEn.q: International organisations (IOs) have an irreplaceable and diverse role in resolving international conflict, acting as key arenas for diplomacy, mediation, and humanitarian intervention. States can communicate, make treaties, and resolve conflicts without resorting to violence in neutral environments provided by organisations such as the United Nations (UN), regional organisations like the African Union (AU), and specialist organisations. In order to stabilise unstable areas, IOs regularly dispatch peacekeeping operations to monitor ceasefires, protect people, and aid in post-conflict reconstruction. They also serve to enforce international law and human rights, making states accountable for their behaviour and encouraging peaceful coexistence norms. Though their potential is undermined by geopolitical competition, veto powers, and resource constraints, IOs are indispensable for organising multilateral actions to confront complex emergencies, mobilising collective action to avert escalation, reduce suffering, and lay the foundations for sustainable peace in an increasingly interdependent world. To limit communication between conflicting states

questionsEn.q: In addition to the historical taboo that often silenced discussions of psychological well-being, mental health awareness has evolved into an essential part of contemporary society. Creating a culture that is supportive and understanding starts with recognizing that mental health is on par with bodily health. questionsEn.q: Online purchasing, which combines unmatched ease with a distinct set of disadvantages, has completely changed how consumers behave. Accessibility is its main benefit; customers may explore and buy things from almost anywhere at any time, and there is frequently a greater selection than in physical stores. Important lures include competitive pricing, made possible by internet retailers' reduced overhead, and the simplicity of comparing prices from several providers. However, there are significant drawbacks to online shopping's virtual nature. Delivery-related discontent may result from the inability to personally inspect things before purchase. Concerns over shipping delays, unstated expenses, and the effects of packaging and transportation on the environment are becoming more widespread. Additionally, the individualised customer service experience may be weakened by a lack of human interaction. What is the primary advantage of online purchasing according to the text?
o: It allows for in-person inspection of products
It provides easy access to a wider selection of items from anywhere at any time
It offers higher prices than physical stores
It eliminates the need for shipping
questionsEn.s: The passage explicitly states that accessibility is the primary benefit of online shopping, noting specifically that **customers may explore and buy things from almost anywhere at any time, and there is frequently a greater selection than in physical stores.**

questionsEn.q: The idea of progress has always gone hand in hand with the evolution of human beings and the invention of technology. Each technological revolution has unearthed revolutionary changes that have rewritten the human experience in the past. From the invention of the printing press to the invention of the internet, technological breakthroughs have shaped the manner in which we live, work, and communicate. But with our arrival in an age of artificial intelligence, automation, and biotechnology comes a growing paradox: while these technologies offer unparalleled convenience and power, they also undermine tried-and-true social forms and erode the very notion of what it means to be human. Technological advances, first of all, have provided standards of living much better. Medical advances like gene editing and precision medicine hold the promise to cure diseases that were once thought incurable. Communication technology has made the world think alike in ways that people could not have imagined a couple of decades ago, with people able to work together across borders and cultures with relative ease. But the same technology has profound implications. Automation is taking away jobs for millions of people, particularly where human labor can be automated. The speed of innovation has left millions behind, and with it there is a feeling of disconnection, fear for the future. Secondly, our dependence on technology is creating basic questions regarding privacy, security, and freedom. As we introduce AI into everyday life, do we have to sit back and ask ourselves: are we Master of Technology, or is technology the master of us? The paradox of progress, then, is in its double-edged nature. On one hand, technology comes bearing answers to some of humankind's biggest problems, yet it also brings new issues that human beings must resolve in order to make progress mean a more just and sustainable tomorrow. What is the main paradox introduced in the passage regarding technological advancements?
o: Technology always improves the quality of life
Technology eliminates all forms of labor
Technology offers convenience but also undermines social structures and the notion of being human
Technology solves all human problems without consequences
questionsEn.s: The passage explicitly states the core paradox: while these technologies offer unparalleled convenience and power, they also undermine tried-and-true social forms and erode the very notion of what it means to be human. This directly points to the third option.

questionsEn.q: The explosive integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the workplace represents a tangled web of ethical issues that need to be carefully addressed. While AI holds out the potential for increased productivity, mechanisation of routine tasks, and new opportunities for economic development, it raises to its highest power fundamental questions regarding job loss, algorithmic bias, and the redefinition of human work. Strong retraining initiatives and proactive legislative responses are necessary to counteract social disruption in the face of the possibility of widespread job losses, particularly in repetitive and predictable tasks. More dangerously, AI programs that learn from historical data have the potential to reinforce and even magnify prevailing cultural biases, leading to biassed performance evaluations or discriminatory hiring practices. This creates issues of fairness and equity in a more automated world. In addition, as AI fills increasing numbers of decision-making positions, the accountability issue is at the forefront: who is accountable when an AI system commits a critical mistake or inflicts harm? Strong retraining initiatives and proactive legislative responses are necessary to counteract social disruption in the face of the possibility of widespread job losses, particularly in repetitive and predictable tasks. What is one of the main ethical concerns related to the integration of AI into the workplace?
o: Increased job opportunities in all sectors

Improved decision-making in human resource management
Reduction in the use of technology in decision-making
questionsEn.s: The passage explicitly states that AI programs have the potential to **reinforce and even magnify prevailing cultural biases,** which is highlighted as a dangerous ethical concern.

questionsEn.q: Mandala art, a term derived from the Sanskrit word for **circle,**.Mandalas are mathematical and metaphorical works of art that have captivated people for ages. In essence, a mandala is a circle pattern that represents the cosmos and the individual's journey. The genesis of everything, one's identity, or a heavenly essence are all represented by the design's centre. Complex and often symmetrical patterns spread forth from this hub representing the universe's growth and the continuous flow of life. Mandalas, which have their roots in both Buddhism and Hinduism, are powerful instruments for spiritual ritual and meditation. In order to symbolise the fleeting nature of life and the rejection of earthly possessions, monks painstakingly create these elaborate patterns out of coloured sand, only to brush them away when finished. Making a mandala has therapeutic benefits in addition to its religious significance. Drawing its geometric patterns in a methodical and repeated manner helps to reduce tension, improve focus, and calm the mind. The act of creating is a form of active meditation that allows the artist to concentrate and attain inner peace. What does the term **mandala** mean in Sanskrit?
questionsEn.s: The passage explicitly states in the first sentence that **Mandala art** is a term derived from the Sanskrit word for **circle**. Thus, **Circle** is the precise and correct answer.

questionsEn.q: In the contemporary corporate milieu, women occupying the echelons of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Technology Officer (CTO) roles have increasingly disrupted the traditionally male-dominated paradigm. Despite systemic impediments such as gender bias and glass ceilings, a growing cohort of women leaders is redefining organizational dynamics through innovative leadership and technological acumen. The ascendancy of women CEOs and CTOs is emblematic of progressive shifts in societal and corporate ethos, fostering inclusivity and diversity at strategic decision-making levels. Their leadership is often characterized by a collaborative approach, emotional intelligence, and resilience, which synergize effectively with technological innovation and business strategy. However, these trailblazing women frequently confront challenges including unequal access to mentorship, networking opportunities, and unconscious biases embedded within corporate cultures. The persistence of such barriers underscores the necessity for institutional reforms aimed at amplifying female representation in executive roles. Moreover, the integration of technology with visionary leadership by women CTOs has catalyzed transformative advancements across sectors, underscoring the symbiotic relationship between gender diversity and technological progress. This paradigm not only enhances organizational performance but also fosters sustainable development goals aligned with equity. In essence, the emergence of women as CEOs and CTOs heralds a nuanced reconfiguration of power structures within the corporate sphere, delineating a future where gender parity and innovation coalesce to propel economic and social progress. In the sentence, "The persistence of such barriers underscores the necessity for institutional reforms aimed at amplifying female representation in executive roles," the phrase **aimed at amplifying female representation** is:
o: an absolute phrase modifying the entire sentence
questionsEn.s: The phrase **aimed at amplifying female representation** begins with the past participle **aimed** and functions as an adjective to describe the noun immediately preceding it, which is **reforms**.

questionsEn.q: The mounting reality of climate migration represents a deep and vexing challenge to confront the ethical and planning paradigms of global society. As melting polar ice, desertification, and violent weather patterns make large areas unhabitable, millions are already being forced off their land, in the process creating a new generation of forced migrants who now have no official legal status as **climate refugees.** The issue now is no longer whether this will occur, but how countries ought to act together and fairly. A thorough solution calls for a multi-faceted strategy: first, the creation of new international humanitarian and legal protocols to acknowledge and safeguard climate migrants and shift away from the present, limited definition of refugees. Second, it requires proactive, not reactive, policy, such as the establishment of legal and safe channels of resettlement, strong humanitarian assistance for uprooted persons, and serious investment in building climate resilience among those who are likely to be vulnerable, so that they are not displaced in the first place. It puts in sharp relief the hard question of how the burden is to be shared. A strong case, based on the issue of climate justice, places the main burden on the industrialised world. They have been the biggest per-capita producers of greenhouse gases throughout history, something that is directly associated with the scale of the climate crisis. Their prosperity was primarily developed through carbon-polluting industries, and those are the same conditions responsible for destroying the least-developed countries, which have contributed minimal input to the crisis. Hence, an ethical and equitable response requires that these industrialized countries take the lead with both financial and logistical assistance. They must be leading the line in supporting adaptation projects in developing nations and having the resources necessary for the resettlement and integration of climate migrants. The international community has to eventually realize that the responsibility of climate change is not equally shared, and an equitable solution must involve people who caused the problem taking the initiative to mitigate the most destructive humanitarian effects of the problem. According to the passage, what is the primary ethical dilemma posed by climate migration?
o: Whether migrants should be allowed to resettle
How the burden of climate migration should be shared
Whether climate change is a natural occurrence
How to prevent future climate change
questionsEn.s: The passage explicitly states that the situation **puts in sharp relief the hard question of how the burden is to be shared,** highlighting this as the primary ethical and logistical challenge for global society.

questionsEn.q: Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it: The fundamental and existential threat posed by the unparalleled proliferation of digital surveillance capabilities to democracy's foundational tenets is a clear contradiction between the demands of modern security and the ideals of individual liberty. It is now concretely known whether these technologies are compromising civil freedoms, rather than just an abstract theory. Facial recognition, bulk collection of data, and algorithmic tracking of online activity give governments and corporations the ability to exercise constant, detailed surveillance over the lives of citizens. All-encompassing surveillance has the potential to have a "chilling effect", - where citizens, aware of being spied upon, might censor themselves, restrict their activism, and refrain from articulating dissenting views, thus suppressing the very dissent and freedom of expression that are core to a healthy democracy. The possibility of using these tools for political repression, social control, and targeting marginalised communities poses a sinister downward slide toward a surveillance state where the assumption of innocence gives way to an assumption of suspicion. The underlying conflict, then, is how to balance personal privacy against national security. Although there is a genuine need for governments to employ sophisticated technologies to respond to terrorism, organised crime, and other grave dangers, this must not be at the cost of the basic right to privacy. A good balance is a strong and open legal regime that subjects surveillance activities to rigorous judicial supervision and public accountability. Since technologies like end-to-end encryption are essential for protecting private communication, they should be supported and encouraged rather than compromised. In order to establish clear red lines—what data can be gathered, under what conditions, and for how long—societies must also participate in a continuous and collaborative public discussion. Whether freedom endures in the age of the internet depends upon our capacity to construct a system in which security is not a zero-sum affair with liberty but a system of confidence in which technology serves to safeguard citizens, not continually watch them. What is the central contradiction discussed in the passage regarding digital surveillance?
o: The need for transparency vs. secrecy
The conflict between technological progress and personal privacy
The desire for security vs. the rights of corporations
The trade-off between national security and individual freedom
questionsEn.s: The passage clearly states the contradiction is "between the demands of modern security and the ideals of individual liberty." This directly matches option (d). Option (b) mentions "technological progress," which is not the focus. Option (a) about transparency vs. secrecy is not the central theme. Option (c) about rights of corporations is not discussed as a central contradiction.

Facial recognition, bulk collection of data, and algorithmic tracking of online activity give governments and corporations the ability to exercise constant, detailed surveillance over the lives of citizens. All-encompassing surveillance has the potential to have a "chilling effect", - where citizens, aware of being spied upon, might censor themselves, restrict their activism, and refrain from articulating dissenting views, thus suppressing the very dissent and freedom of expression that are core to a healthy democracy. The possibility of using these tools for political repression, social control, and targeting marginalised communities poses a sinister downward slide toward a surveillance state where the assumption of innocence gives way to an assumption of suspicion. The underlying conflict, then, is how to balance personal privacy against national security. Although there is a genuine need for governments to employ sophisticated technologies to respond to terrorism, organised crime, and other grave dangers, this must not be at the cost of the basic right to privacy. A good balance is a strong and open legal regime that subjects surveillance activities to rigorous judicial supervision and public accountability. Since technologies like end-to-end encryption are essential for protecting private communication, they should be supported and encouraged rather than compromised. In order to establish clear red lines—what data can be gathered, under what conditions, and for how long—societies must also participate in a continuous and collaborative public discussion. Whether freedom endures in the age of the internet depends upon our capacity to construct a system in which security is not a zero-sum affair with liberty but a system of confidence in which technology serves to safeguard citizens, not continually watch them. How does the passage describe the use of surveillance technologies by governments and corporations?
o: A beneficial tool for national security only
A means of societal control and political repression
A tool for promoting freedom of expression
A neutral force that has no impact on privacy
questionsEn.s: The passage states: "The possibility of using these tools for political repression, social control, and targeting marginalised communities poses a sinister downward slide toward a surveillance state." This directly describes surveillance as a means of societal control and political repression, matching option (b). Options (a), (c), and (d) contradict the passage's negative portrayal.

questionsEn.q: Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it: One of the biggest ethical dilemmas of the twenty-first century is brought up by the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into modern combat, particularly in the form of autonomous weapons systems (AWS). The promise of strategic advantage is pitted against fundamental ethical principles in the fiercely debated issue of whether or not such "killer robots" should be allowed in combat. Supporters contend that autonomous weapons might decrease the loss of human life, since they do not fear, become tired, or suffer the emotional stress that can cause human mistakes in combat. They also might be able to operate with more accuracy and rapidity in an unpredictable environment, which could decrease civilian casualties. The ethical arguments are serious, nonetheless. The most compelling argument is the transfer of the life-and-death decision-making from a human to a machine. Opponents contend that a computer, however sophisticated, could never have the moral calculus, compassion, or comprehension of human dignity to make such judgments. This creates an important question of accountability: in the event that an autonomous weapon kills without authorisation, who has the moral and legal culpability? Is it the programmer who wrote the algorithm, the commander who sent the system out, or the state that legitimised its use? The secrecy of AI's decision-making process, commonly known as a "black box," also adds to the difficulty in assigning blame. This built-in absence of clear moral and legal norms tests the very foundations of the international laws of armed conflict. Essentially, the debate about autonomous weapons puts us in a position of considering not only the technology but also human responsibility, judgment, and the ethical limits we are prepared to place on the waging of war. Which of the following is the most compelling ethical argument against autonomous weapons in combat?
o: The potential for increased civilian casualties
The speed at which autonomous weapons operate
The transfer of life-and-death decision-making to machines
The lack of accountability in AI decisions
questionsEn.s: The passage explicitly states that "the most compelling argument is the transfer of the life-and-death decision-making from a human to a machine." Therefore, option (c) is correct.

questionsEn.q:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. She poured the hot liquid into her favourite mug.
Q. A downpour had started raining hard, beating against the windowpanes in steady rhythm.
R. The kitchen was filled with the scent of cinnamon and cloves, a comforting and warm smell.
S. It was a fantastic night to have a mug of hot cider.
questionsEn.s: First comes the rainy setting (Q), then the general conclusion (S), then the action of pouring cider (R and P fit as description and action). The best coherent sequence is **QSRP**.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following questions: India’s tryst with chess is deeply interwoven with its cultural heritage, for the game itself originally known as "chaturanga" emerged on the subcontinent over a millennium ago. Initially conceived as a strategic simulation of warfare, "chaturanga" evolved into shatranj under Persian influence before migrating westward, ultimately becoming modern chess. In the contemporary era, India’s prominence on the global chess stage began with the meteoric ascent of Viswanathan Anand in the late 20th century. Anand’s fluid playing style, amalgamating tactical precision with positional depth, earned him the World Chess Championship title multiple times and inspired a generation of players. His success catalysed institutional investment in chess, leading to an upsurge in tournaments, academies, and grassroots initiatives across the country. The 21st century has witnessed the emergence of prodigies such as Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa, D. Gukesh, and Nihal Sarin, whose exploits in international arenas have positioned India as a formidable force in team events like the Chess Olympiad. Digital platforms have further accelerated talent development, enabling young aspirants to spar with grandmasters worldwide, thus refining their strategic acumen from an early age. Today, India stands not merely as the cradle of chess’s origins but as an influential power shaping its future. This continuity from ancient invention to modern innovation underscores the nation’s enduring legacy in the chess world. The phrase "enabling young aspirants to spar with grandmasters worldwide" functions as:
questionsEn.s: The phrase begins with the present participle **enabling** and modifies the preceding idea about digital platforms, so it functions as a participle phrase.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following questions: The evolution of artificial lighting has been a remarkable journey from primitive illumination to sophisticated, energy-efficient systems. Early humans relied on rudimentary sources such as torches and oil lamps, which, though limited in luminosity, extended productive hours beyond daylight. The invention of the incandescent bulb in the late 19th century, pioneered by Thomas Edison and others, heralded a transformative era, delivering consistent brightness through electrically heated filaments. This innovation was soon succeeded by fluorescent lighting, which employed gas discharge to produce light more efficiently, albeit with a colder hue. The 20th century also witnessed the rise of halogen lamps, prized for their compact size and enhanced brightness. However, the most significant leap emerged with the advent of Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs). LEDs combine minimal energy consumption with exceptional longevity, revolutionising residential, commercial, and public lighting. Modern developments have expanded beyond mere illumination. Smart lighting systems integrate with digital networks, allowing remote control, colour customisation, and adaptive brightness. These technologies not only optimise energy usage but also contribute to mood enhancement and architectural aesthetics. From the flicker of a primitive flame to the programmable glow of smart LEDs, lighting has evolved into a convergence of science, design, and sustainability—an indispensable facet of contemporary life. The phrase "allowing remote control, colour customisation, and adaptive brightness" functions as:
questionsEn.s: The phrase begins with the present participle **allowing** and modifies the preceding clause about smart lighting systems, so it functions as a participle phrase.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following questions: In modern households, electrical devices are as common as furniture. From refrigerators and washing machines to smart televisions and microwave ovens, these appliances have transformed domestic life. However, their increasing presence has also heightened the risks, particularly for children, whose natural curiosity often overrides caution. Electrical devices operate on currents that can cause severe injury or even death if mishandled. Young children, unaware of these dangers, may insert fingers or objects into sockets, tug at dangling cords, or attempt to open appliance panels. Such actions can result in shocks, burns, or mechanical harm. Even low voltage devices, if defective or poorly maintained, can be hazardous. The responsibility for preventing accidents rests largely with adults. Installing socket covers, keeping cords out of reach, and unplugging appliances when not in use are basic precautions. More advanced measures include using Residual Current Devices (RCDs), which automatically cut off power during faults, and ensuring all wiring complies with safety standards. Regular inspection of devices is equally critical, as frayed wires or exposed components can turn everyday items into hidden threats. Education plays a vital role. Teaching children the "look, don't touch" rule, explaining the dangers of electricity in age-appropriate terms, and supervising them around devices are all effective strategies. Safety is not merely a matter of physical barriers but also of fostering awareness. Ultimately, a home equipped with electrical conveniences need not be a danger zone. Through vigilant supervision, proper maintenance, and informed habits, families can enjoy technology while safeguarding their youngest members. "Families can enjoy technology while safeguarding their youngest members." Rewrite the above sentence in passive voice.
o: Technology can be enjoyed by families while their youngest members are safeguarded.
Technology is enjoyed by families while safeguarding their youngest members.
Technology will be enjoyed by families while their youngest members safeguard them.
Technology has been enjoyed by families while safeguarding their youngest members.
questionsEn.s: The active sentence "Families can enjoy technology..." becomes passive as "Technology can be enjoyed by families...". The clause "while safeguarding their youngest members" is best rendered as "while their youngest members are safeguarded."

The policy replaces the 10+2 structure with a new 5+3+3+4 system, which focuses on the foundational stage and encourages critical thinking from an early age. One of the key effects of the NEP is the emphasis on mother tongue or regional language as the medium of instruction at the primary level. This has generated both appreciation and concern. While experts believe it will strengthen children's roots and understanding, some worry about challenges in implementation and the impact on English language proficiency. Furthermore, the NEP promotes vocational education, digital literacy, and interdisciplinary studies. It aims to reduce rote learning and exams-centric approaches by encouraging practical knowledge and creativity. If implemented effectively, the NEP could reshape India's educational landscape for generations to come. Which of the following words from the passage is a gerund?
questionsEn.s: A gerund is a verb form ending in "-ing" that functions as a noun. In the passage, "learning" in "rote learning" acts as a noun. "Reshape" and "replace" are base verbs, while "emphasis" is a noun.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following questions: In contemporary India, the accounting profession, particularly Chartered Accountants (CAs), is witnessing an alarming surge in fatalities attributed primarily to excessive work-related stress. The profession's demanding nature—characterized by protracted hours, stringent deadlines, and intense mental exertion—has precipitated grave health repercussions. Despite being pivotal to the country's financial ecosystem, many CAs endure chronic sleep deprivation and psychological strain, culminating in life-threatening conditions such as cardiac arrests and strokes. The deleterious effects of incessant work pressures are exacerbated during the fiscal year-end and tax filing seasons, where the workload intensifies manifold. The compulsion to deliver flawless outputs within unforgiving timeframes frequently compels professionals to forsake personal well-being. Moreover, the COVID-19 pandemic further aggravated these conditions by transitioning most work to virtual platforms, blurring the boundaries between professional and personal life, and extending working hours indefinitely. Compounding this predicament is the societal stigma attached to seeking psychological assistance, which dissuades many from obtaining necessary mental health support. The regulatory bodies and firms, albeit cognizant of this crisis, have been slow to implement effective measures to mitigate occupational hazards. In essence, the burgeoning mortality among Indian CAs is a clarion call for systemic reforms, encompassing workload management, mental health awareness, and institutional accountability, to safeguard the professionals who underpin India's economic stability. Identify the voice of the verb phrase in the sentence: "The compulsion to deliver flawless outputs within unforgiving timeframes frequently compels professionals to forsake personal well-being."
questionsEn.s: The subject "The compulsion..." performs the action "compels", so the verb phrase is in active voice. Passive voice would show the subject receiving the action. "Causative" and "subjunctive mood" do not apply here.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following questions:** In an era where urban dwellers frequently lament their paucity of time, cultivating plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles. Certain species, endowed with remarkable resilience, can subsist with negligible intervention, thereby mitigating the anxieties often concomitant with horticulture. The snake plant (Sansevieria trifasciata), for instance, is virtually indomitable. It thrives in variegated light conditions and can endure erratic watering schedules without forfeiting its structural elegance. Likewise, the pothos (Epipremnum aureum), with its luxuriant, trailing foliage, adapts to both dimly lit corners and well-illuminated spaces, performing photosynthesis with an almost stoic persistence. Another exemplar is the aloe Vera, whose succulent leaves serve as reservoirs of moisture, rendering frequent irrigation superfluous. Beyond its ornamental utility, aloe Vera confers medicinal benefits, its gel being esteemed for dermal amelioration. Even the ZZ plant (Zamioculcas zamiifolia), seemingly sculpted from emerald wax, flourishes in neglect, tolerating prolonged droughts and low luminosity without capitulating to decay. The allure of such flora lies not merely in their aesthetic contribution but in their implicit lesson: resilience is as captivating as fragility. In cultivating them, one engages in a quiet partnership where human oversight is ancillary, and nature's intrinsic mechanisms orchestrate survival with effortless grace. **"plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles." Convert the sentence into Interrogative sentence.**
o: plants that demand minimal vigilance have not become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
Is plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
Why plants that demand minimal vigilance have become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
Have plants that demand minimal vigilance become almost axiomatic for those seeking verdant comfort within their domiciles?
questionsEn.s: This question tests the conversion of an assertive sentence into an interrogative sentence. The original sentence is in present perfect tense with "have become." To convert it into an interrogative sentence, we use the auxiliary verb "Have" at the beginning. Option (d) is correct because it follows the structure: Have + subject + verb. Option (a) is incorrect because it only adds a question mark without changing the structure. Option (b) is wrong due to incorrect subject-verb agreement ("Is plants"). Option (c) creates a "why" question, which changes the meaning completely.

questionsEn.q: Plastic surgery has become increasingly common in recent years, with millions of people opting for cosmetic procedures to enhance their physical appearance. questionsEn.q: The debate over whether working from home is better than working from the office has intensified, especially after the global shift during the pandemic. While remote work offers flexibility and saves commuting time, many experts argue that office work remains more effective for several reasons. Offices provide a structured environment where employees can separate personal and professional lives. Face to face interactions promote quick problem-solving, spontaneous discussions, and stronger teamwork elements often difficult to replicate virtually. Being in an office also helps maintain discipline and reduces distractions common at home, such as chores or family interruptions. Another important factor is the psychological impact. For many, the daily routine of getting ready, commuting, and working with colleagues boosts motivation and creates a sense of belonging. It also helps prevent the isolation that remote workers sometimes experience. While technology enables virtual collaboration, human connection and workplace culture often thrive better in physical spaces. In-person environments support relationship-building and allow managers to observe and support employees more effectively. Therefore, while remote work has advantages like flexibility and comfort, the traditional office still plays a key role in productivity, mental well-being, and professional development. A balanced approach, blending remote and in-office work might offer the best of both worlds, catering to different needs while preserving efficiency and connection. In the sentence: "While remote work offers flexibility and saves commuting time, many experts argue that working from the office remains more effective for several reasons." questionsEn.s: **Flexibility** names a quality or state, so it is a **noun**. It is the object of the verb “offers” in the sentence.

questionsEn.q: Despite significant progress in mental health awareness, visiting a psychiatrist remains a taboo for many people in India. questionsEn.q: Old age is often described as a period of reflection, wisdom, and sometimes, unexpected emotional turbulence. Experts suggest that emotional wellbeing in old age largely depends on supportive relationships and a sense of purpose. Engaging in hobbies, maintaining friendships, and feeling valued by younger generations can significantly uplift an elderly person’s mood and outlook on life. Sadly, in many societies, older individuals are not given the attention and respect they deserve, which can intensify their feelings of despair. Younger generations should respect older individuals. questionsEn.q: In India's fiscal architecture, taxation constitutes a cardinal instrument for resource mobilisation and equitable wealth distribution. Broadly bifurcated into direct and indirect levies, the system encompasses a complex interplay of statutory provisions, administrative machinery, and compliance frameworks. Direct taxes, exemplified by income tax and corporate tax, are levied directly on individuals or entities based on their earnings or profits. These imposts embody the principle of progressive taxation, wherein higher income brackets attract proportionately higher rates, ostensibly promoting distributive justice. Indirect taxes, conversely, are imposed on goods and services, with the burden ultimately borne by the end consumer. The advent of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in 2017 subsumed a plethora of erstwhile levies such as excise duty, service tax, and value-added tax, creating a unified national market. While GST has streamlined compliance and reduced cascading effects, debates persist regarding its impact on small enterprises and revenue buoyancy. In addition, India imposes ancillary duties such as customs duty on imports, intended both to generate revenue and to protect domestic industries. The overall tax regime, though intricate, is pivotal for financing public infrastructure, social welfare programmes, and defence expenditure, thereby underpinning the nation’s developmental trajectory. The clause "wherein higher income brackets attract proportionately higher rates" is:
questionsEn.s: The clause beginning with **wherein** describes the noun phrase **the principle of progressive taxation** by explaining what it involves. Therefore, it functions as an **adjective clause**.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following questions: In an economy increasingly defined by automation and volatile market dynamics, the pertinence of skill-based education has never been more conspicuous. Traditional pedagogy, with its emphasis on rote memorisation and theoretical abstraction, often fails to equip learners with the pragmatic competencies demanded by contemporary industries. This schism between academic instruction and workplace exigencies has engendered a workforce proficient in qualifications but deficient in adaptability. Skill-based education, conversely, prioritises applied learning, fostering dexterity in problem-solving, communication, and technological fluency. Apprenticeships, vocational training, and project-based curricula immerse students in authentic scenarios where knowledge is not merely recited but operationalized. Such experiential learning cultivates not only technical acumen but also critical soft skills indispensable in collaborative environments. Furthermore, skill-oriented systems encourage a mind-set of lifelong learning, essential in an era where obsolescence can render a profession archaic within a decade. They democratise opportunity by enabling individuals from diverse socio-economic backgrounds to access employment through demonstrable capability rather than academic prestige alone. Ultimately, integrating skill-based frameworks into mainstream education is not a peripheral reform but a systemic imperative. It reconciles the persistent dichotomy between learning and livelihood, ensuring that education is not an inert archive of facts but a dynamic instrument for personal agency and national progress. The phrase "where knowledge is not merely recited but operationalized" functions as:
questionsEn.s: The clause begins with "where" and describes "authentic scenarios." Since it modifies a noun phrase, it functions as an adjective clause, not a noun clause or an absolute phrase.

questionsEn.q:
World Handloom Day, observed every year on 7th August, commemorates the launch of the Swadeshi Movement in

1905. It highlights the importance of India’s handloom industry, which represents not just craftsmanship but also cultural identity and self-reliance. India is home to over 43 lakh handloom weavers, many of them women in rural communities. Each region contributes a unique weaving style: such as Chanderi, Pochampally Ikat, and Kanjeevaram, reflecting the stories, rituals, and environments of its people. Despite its rich legacy, the handloom sector faces significant challenges. With rising demand for machine-made fabrics, traditional weavers are struggling to sustain their livelihoods. Government efforts, like the India Handloom Brand, aim to revive interest and increase the visibility of hand-woven products. However, access to modern markets and digital platforms remains limited for many artisans. World Handloom Day is more than symbolic. It reminds us that promoting handlooms supports sustainable fashion, local economies, and ecological balance. As consumer awareness grows around eco-friendly choices, handloom garments offer a natural alternative to fast fashion. By supporting handloom products, we are not only preserving a centuries-old tradition but also empowering artisans and encouraging environmentally conscious living. 1905. It highlights the importance of India’s handloom industry, which represents not just craftsmanship but also cultural identity and self-reliance. India is home to over 43 lakh handloom weavers, many of them women in rural communities. Each region contributes a unique weaving style: such as Chanderi, Pochampally Ikat, and Kanjeevaram, reflecting the stories, rituals, and environments of its people. Despite its rich legacy, the handloom sector faces significant challenges. With rising demand for machine-made fabrics, traditional weavers are struggling to sustain their livelihoods. Government efforts, like the India Handloom Brand, aim to revive interest and increase the visibility of hand-woven products. However, access to modern markets and digital platforms remains limited for many artisans. World Handloom Day is more than symbolic. It reminds us that promoting handlooms supports sustainable fashion, local economies, and ecological balance. As consumer awareness grows around eco-friendly choices, handloom garments offer a natural alternative to fast fashion. By supporting handloom products, we are not only preserving a centuries-old tradition but also empowering artisans and encouraging environmentally conscious living. What does "ecological balance" most likely refer to in this sentence? "It reminds us that promoting handlooms supports sustainable fashion, local economies, and ecological balance."
o: Stability and health of the environment
questionsEn.s: **Ecological balance** means the healthy and stable functioning of the natural environment. In the passage, it connects handlooms with eco-friendly and sustainable living.

questionsEn.q: In the realm of childhood development, certain games transcend mere amusement, functioning instead as potent instruments for cognitive enhancement. Unlike passive entertainment, these activities engage neural circuits, fostering memory retention, logical reasoning, and adaptive problem solving. Classic strategy games such as chess compel young players to anticipate consequences several moves ahead, refining both foresight and decision-making acuity. Similarly, puzzles ranging from jigsaw assemblies to three-dimensional brainteasers demand spatial awareness and pattern recognition, skills transferable to mathematics and science. Even word-based games, including crosswords and Scrabble, enrich vocabulary and linguistic dexterity, thereby strengthening communicative competence. Digital platforms, when judiciously curated, can also serve as catalysts for mental growth. Educational video games that simulate problem scenarios encourage children to synthesise information rapidly and experiment with multiple solutions, enhancing cognitive flexibility. Importantly, these benefits are maximised when gameplay is balanced with real-world interaction, mitigating the risks of social isolation and sedentary behaviour. Furthermore, such games cultivate patience, perseverance, and a tolerance for delayed gratification traits that underpin academic resilience. By embedding complex mental tasks within an enjoyable framework, they transform learning into an intrinsically motivating pursuit rather than an externally imposed obligation. Ultimately, games that stimulate the intellect are not trivial diversions but dynamic tools, shaping neural architecture in ways that can confer lasting academic and personal advantages. In the sentence "Digital platforms, when judiciously curated, can also serve as catalysts for mental growth.", the phrase "when judiciously curated" functions as:
questionsEn.s: The phrase begins with "when" and tells under what time/condition the main clause applies. It functions as an adverbial clause of time.

questionsEn.q: In today’s technology-centric era, electronic devices have become indispensable to modern life. From smartphones and laptops to home appliances, the demand for newer and faster gadgets continues to escalate. However, this increasing dependence has brought about a critical challenge electronic waste, commonly known as e-waste. E-waste refers to discarded electrical or electronic equipment that is obsolete or non-functional. Unlike regular waste, it contains hazardous substances such as lead, mercury, and cadmium. Improper disposal of e-waste allows these toxins to seep into soil and water bodies, causing severe environmental degradation and posing long-term health risks. Developing nations are particularly vulnerable, as they often receive large volumes of e-waste from wealthier countries. In many cases, informal recycling sectors handle this waste without adequate safety measures. Workers, including children, dismantle devices manually, exposing themselves to toxic chemicals and dangerous working conditions. On the brighter side, responsible recycling of e-waste enables the recovery of valuable materials like copper, gold, and high-quality plastics. This not only mitigates environmental harm but also reduces the strain on natural resources. Governments and environmental agencies are advocating for sustainable practices such as repairing old devices, donating functional electronics, and following safe recycling methods. Public awareness, coupled with stringent regulations, is vital for tackling this escalating problem. In conclusion, managing e-waste effectively demands both individual accountability and collective efforts. Adopting eco-friendly habits can lead us toward a cleaner, safer, and more sustainable future. Identify the type of the following sentence and justify your answer. "Improper disposal of e-waste allows these toxins to seep into soil and water bodies, causing severe environmental degradation and posing long-term health risks."
questionsEn.s: This is a simple sentence because it contains one main clause, though it includes participial phrases like “causing...” and “posing...”. These do not make it compound or complex.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following question: Over the past century, the world has witnessed a remarkable evolution in girls' education. In many parts of the world, especially during the early 1900s, girls were often denied access to schools or allowed only basic literacy. Deeprooted social norms and economic barriers restricted girls to household roles, and their potential to contribute equally to society remained untapped. Gradually, global awareness about gender equality and human rights began to change this scenario. International organisations and local governments worked together to launch initiatives aimed at increasing female literacy rates, building safe schools, and encouraging families to send their daughters to study. Campaigns highlighting the importance of girls' education brought hope to millions. Despite significant progress, challenges still persist in several developing nations, where poverty, early marriage, and cultural resistance continue to keep girls away from classrooms. However, the success stories of educated women who have become leaders, scientists, and change makers inspire others to break barriers. The evolution of girls' education proves that empowering women through knowledge benefits entire communities and fuels sustainable development. Complete the sentence with the most appropriate preposition: International organisations worked together to launch initiatives aimed ___ increasing female literacy rates.
questionsEn.s: The correct collocation is "aimed at." It means directed toward a specific objective, here increasing female literacy rates.

questionsEn.q: Hospitals operate around the clock, and so do the people who work within them. From doctors and nurses to cleaning staff, lab technicians, and administrative workers, every hospital employee plays a critical role in keeping the system functioning smoothly. While the public often sees doctors as the face of healthcare, the tireless contributions of other workers often go unnoticed. The life of a hospital employee is marked by long hours, high stress, and emotional strain. Nurses may have to attend to critical patients for entire shifts without rest, while housekeeping staff ensure that hygiene standards are maintained to prevent infections. Hospital employees handle hundreds of samples daily with precision, and emergency ward staff often face life-or-death situations multiple times a day. What makes their jobs even more challenging is the emotional burden. Hospital employees witness suffering, grief, and loss more frequently than most people do in a lifetime. Yet, despite the psychological weight, many remain committed to their work out of a deep sense of duty and compassion. In recent years, especially after the COVID-19 pandemic, awareness about the importance of every hospital worker has grown. However, proper recognition, mental health support, and fair working conditions are still essential to ensure the well-being of those who care for others. Which sentence from the passage is written in the present perfect tense?
o: Every hospital employee plays a critical role.
Many remain committed to their work.
Awareness about the importance of every hospital worker has grown.
questionsEn.s: The present perfect tense uses "has/have + past participle." In option (d), "has grown" is in the present perfect tense.

questionsEn.q: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:** Engineering was once considered one of the most prestigious and secure career choices in India. questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following question(s): Himachal Pradesh, renowned for its pristine natural beauty and ecological diversity, is presently confronting an unprecedented wave of environmental degradation. The rampant deforestation, exacerbated by unregulated urban expansion and burgeoning tourism, has precipitated a critical decline in the region's biodiversity. Once dense forests, which acted as vital carbon sinks and habitats for myriad species, are now alarmingly fragmented, undermining ecological balance. The overexploitation of natural resources, especially timber and water, compounded by erratic weather patterns attributed to climate change, further exacerbates the fragile ecosystem's vulnerability. The proliferation of construction activities along riverbanks and hill slopes has triggered soil erosion and heightened the risk of landslides, endangering both human settlements and wildlife habitats. Additionally, the indiscriminate dumping of waste, including plastic, in ecologically sensitive zones aggravates pollution levels and jeopardizes aquatic life. Another pivotal reason behind this environmental deterioration is the inadequacy of stringent environmental policies and their enforcement. Despite awareness campaigns, local governance often succumbs to developmental pressures, sidelining sustainability considerations. The nexus between economic growth and environmental neglect is glaring, necessitating immediate remedial measures. In summation, Himachal Pradesh's environmental crisis is a multifaceted problem, rooted in anthropogenic activities and climatic disturbances. Concerted efforts encompassing policy reform, community engagement, and scientific interventions are imperative to restore the state's ecological sanctity. In the sentence, "The proliferation of construction activities along riverbanks and hill slopes has triggered soil erosion," identify the type of noun "proliferation" is:
questionsEn.s: "Proliferation" refers to a process or state of rapid increase, which is an idea rather than a tangible object. Therefore, it is an abstract noun.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following questions:** Salt, a ubiquitous yet often underappreciated mineral, manifests in myriad forms, each possessing distinctive characteristics shaped by geological provenance and processing methods. Common table salt, the most prevalent variety, undergoes extensive refinement, wherein impurities are eliminated and iodine is often infused to combat endemic deficiencies. Its crystalline uniformity and rapid solubility make it indispensable in both culinary and industrial contexts. In contrast, sea salt is derived through the gradual evaporation of seawater, a process that preserves trace minerals such as magnesium and potassium, thereby imparting subtle variations in flavour and hue. Gourmet enthusiasts often extol its coarse granules for the nuanced crunch they confer to dishes. Himalayan pink salt, quarried from ancient seabeds in the Punjab region, owes its blush to iron oxide deposits. Advocates claim it offers health benefits beyond mere sodium intake, though empirical substantiation remains contested within scientific circles. Black salt, or kala namak, prevalent in South Asian gastronomy, emanates a sulphurous aroma attributable to its volcanic origins, lending complexity to traditional savouries. "Fleur de sel", literally "flower of salt," represents the zenith of artisanal salt production, hand-harvested from the delicate crust forming on salt pans. Prized for its rarity and textural delicacy, it is more an embellishment than a staple seasoning. Thus, while chemically unified by their sodium chloride essence, salts diverge in sensory appeal, mineral composition, and cultural significance, rendering them as much a subject of connoisseurship as of necessity. **Identify the correct transformation of the sentence below into the passive voice without altering its meaning.** Original sentence from the passage: "Gourmet enthusiasts often extol its coarse granules for the nuanced crunch they confer to dishes."
o: Its coarse granules are often extolled by gourmet enthusiasts for the nuanced crunch they confer to dishes.
Its coarse granules confer the nuanced crunch often extolled by gourmet enthusiasts to dishes.
The nuanced crunch is often extolled by gourmet enthusiasts for its coarse granules.
The coarse granules confer the nuanced crunch often praised by gourmet enthusiasts.
questionsEn.s: The correct passive transformation is option (a). The active sentence has "gourmet enthusiasts" as the subject performing the action "extol." In passive voice, "its coarse granules" become the subject and "are extolled" is the passive verb. The meaning and tense are preserved. Option (b) changes the structure incorrectly. Option (c) changes the focus. Option (d) is not passive. Mastering passive voice transformations is important for varied sentence construction and emphasis.

questionsEn.q:
Read the passage and answer the following question(s): The events in Rajamahendravaram in Andhra Pradesh involving the mass poisoning of consumers by milk contaminated with ethylene glycol sound a regulatory alarm. As of March 8, the death toll was 11, with approximately 20 other people, including infants, hospitalised. Milk is a staple in Indian households and contamination by an industrial compound already infamous in India for its lethality carries the potential to trigger a crisis of confidence in local, unbranded milk supplies. Children and the elderly are most affected by ethylene glycol poisoning due to their higher metabolic sensitivity and lower renal reserves, respectively. This could push people towards pasteurised milk from regulated cooperatives such as Amul or Vijaya, which seems desirable, but a large share of milk is also distributed in India through small vendors. Food-safety compliance is as much about punishing bad actors as about reducing the cost of doing the right thing. In the informal supply chain, cold-chain monitoring and hygiene inspections are almost entirely absent, leaving room for contamination. Subsidised testing kits and cooperative chilling facilities can thus reduce the risk at small dairies. Regulators may also consider safe-harbour provisions that ease penalties for dairy operators who report contamination at their facilities; this could also encourage early disclosure, giving authorities time to save lives. (Source: Bitter milk: On the Rajamahendravaram milk adulteration case - The Hindu, March

10) According to the passage, why are the elderly specifically more vulnerable to ethylene glycol poisoning?
o: Due to their lower renal reserves.
Due to their higher metabolic sensitivity.
Because they consume more unbranded milk than infants.
Because they lack access to regulated cooperatives.
questionsEn.s: The passage states the elderly are most affected due to “lower renal reserves.” Learning points: Answer must be lifted from the given line; “respectively” links elderly → lower renal reserves; avoid outside assumptions; identify cause-and-effect words in comprehension; locate the exact supporting sentence before selecting.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following question(s): The story "The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse" is a pleasant and interesting one that highlights the purity of youthfulness and the strong moral values of the Armenian Garoghlanian tribe. The story revolves around the lives of two cousins, Aram and Mourad, who belong to a poor family but are known for their honest nature. Early one morning, Aram is amazed to see his cousin Mourad riding a beautiful white horse. As the boys could not afford such a horse, Aram suspects that the horse could have been ridden without permission, but his excitement to ride the horse makes him forget his suspicion momentarily. The two boys spend a few days secretly enjoying the rides and feel a deep connection with the animal. However, when they meet the horse's owner, John Byro, and hear his sad story, they feel a sense of guilt. Though Byro recognizes his horse, he is too impressed by the tribe's reputation to accuse the boys. His faith in silence is deeply touching for the boys. Finally, Mourad decides to secretly return the horse to its proper stable. The story beautifully depicts how good values and a high moral standard can direct young hearts in the right direction. Why was Aram surprised when he first saw Mourad in the morning?
o: Because Mourad was leaving the village
Because Mourad was riding a beautiful white horse
Because Mourad had bought a new bicycle
Because Mourad was moving to another town

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the questions: The metamorphosis of a butterfly epitomizes one of nature’s most intricate and captivating transformations. The life cycle initiates with the deposition of fragile eggs, often hidden on the underside of leaves, ensuring immediate access to nourishment upon hatching. Once emerged, the larva — or caterpillar — enters a phase of relentless consumption, devouring foliage to fuel its rapid growth. During this stage, it undergoes multiple molts, shedding its rigid exoskeleton to accommodate its expanding form. This insatiable feeding period is essential for amassing the energy required for the subsequent, dramatic metamorphosis. The transition into the pupal stage, encapsulated within a chrysalis, marks an extraordinary biological phenomenon. Inside, the caterpillar’s structures are enzymatically dismantled and reconstructed into entirely new forms — wings, antennae, and compound eyes emerge through a sophisticated process known as histogenesis. Upon completing this hidden transformation, the adult butterfly struggles free, its crumpled wings needing to be inflated with hemolymph and dried before flight is possible. Once airborne, the butterfly’s existence centres on reproduction, perpetuating the species before its ephemeral life concludes. Though often romanticized, the butterfly’s life cycle underscores a rigorous narrative of survival, adaptation, and evolutionary precision, offering profound insights into the fragile balance of ecosystems. Identify the sentence from the passage which is in the **passive voice**:
o: "The metamorphosis of a butterfly epitomizes transformation."
"The butterfly inflates its wings with hemolymph."
questionsEn.s: The passive voice is formed when the subject receives the action. In option (c), "The caterpillar’s structures are enzymatically dismantled," the structures are receiving the action, so it is passive. The other options are in active voice because the subject performs the action.

questionsEn.q:
Read the passage and answer the questions: The annals of mountaineering history are adorned with figures whose daring transcended mere athleticism, embodying philosophical quests for transcendence against Earth's most formidable landscapes. Each mountaineer — whether treading the snows of Everest, the granite of Patagonia, or the arid heights of the Atlas Mountains — etched a distinct narrative of audacity and introspection. “Tenzing Norgay” and “Sir Edmund Hillary’s” epochal

1953 Everest ascent immortalized human perseverance, but figures such as “Reinhold Messner” redefined the boundaries further. Rejecting supplemental oxygen, Messner’s minimalist ethos emphasized purity over conquest, portraying mountains not as trophies but as sentient entities commanding reverence. Similarly, “Junko Tabei”, the first woman to summit Everest, symbolized the intersection of resilience and quiet defiance in an era resistant to female adventurers. The ethos of mountaineering diversified through the late 20th and early 21st centuries. Climbers like “Kilian Jornet”, blending ultra-marathon endurance with technical ascents, and “Nirmal Purja”, whose record-breaking summits shattered temporal assumptions, reveal a contemporary paradigm: mountains as arenas of rapid, almost transcendental athleticism. Meanwhile, indigenous climbers, long relegated to footnotes in expedition histories, increasingly assert their rightful place as stewards of sacred peaks. Thus, the saga of mountaineering resists reduction to mere feats of strength. It weaves a tapestry of cultures, philosophies, and personal odysseys — each ascent a dialectic between human fragility and the immutable majesty of the mountains. In the sentence: "The annals of mountaineering history are adorned with figures whose daring transcended mere athleticism..."? What is the grammatical role of the clause "whose daring transcended mere athleticism"
o: Noun clause acting as the subject
questionsEn.s: The clause **"whose daring transcended mere athleticism"** describes **"figures"**, so it works as a relative or adjective clause. It gives more information about the noun **figures**. It is not adverbial, not a noun clause, and not just a phrase.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following question(s): A passage is given with five questions following it. Read the passage carefully and select the best answer to each question out of the given four alternatives. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into decision-making systems raises profound ethical dilemmas. Unlike humans, AI lacks consciousness or moral intent, yet it increasingly influences areas such as hiring, law enforcement, and healthcare. When algorithms are trained on biased data, they may perpetuate systemic inequalities under the guise of neutrality. Moreover, responsibility becomes diffuse—if an AI-driven system causes harm, who is accountable: the programmer, the user, or the company? Transparency, often lacking in proprietary models, further complicates public trust. Ethical AI development must therefore go beyond functionality; it requires fairness audits, explainability, and robust oversight mechanisms. Without these, we risk embedding opaque biases into institutions that shape human lives. The dilemma is not merely technical but philosophical—can machines, devoid of values, make morally sound choices, or are we outsourcing ethical responsibility to lines of code? What is the central ethical concern raised in the passage?
o: Lack of data for AI training
Delegating moral responsibility to non-conscious systems
AI replacing engineers in key jobs
questionsEn.s: The passage focuses on the ethical problem of AI making influential decisions despite lacking consciousness or moral intent, which amounts to shifting ethical responsibility onto systems that cannot truly bear it.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following question(s): Once relegated to the peripheries of legitimate professional discourse, **YouTube content creation** has metamorphosed into a formidable and highly nuanced career avenue. Far beyond the superficial glitz of viral videos, contemporary content creators must navigate a labyrinthine ecosystem encompassing algorithmic unpredictability, audience analytics, intellectual property considerations, and brand partnership intricacies. The platform's democratized nature ostensibly offers an egalitarian promise — anyone with a camera and an idea can, theoretically, ascend to prominence. However, the reality is far more Darwinian. Success on YouTube today demands not only creative ingenuity but also a keen acumen in digital marketing, search engine optimization (SEO), and an ever-evolving understanding of platform-specific trends. Consistency in output, meticulous engagement with viewer communities, and adaptability to sudden policy shifts have become indispensable skills. Moreover, the psychological ramifications of tethering one's livelihood to fluctuating view counts and algorithmic favor should not be underestimated. Burnout, imposter syndrome, and a precarious sense of self-worth plague many full-time creators. Unlike traditional careers, YouTube offers no institutional safety nets; creators must independently negotiate contracts, secure health benefits, and plan for financial volatility. Nonetheless, for those who can master this digital alchemy, the rewards are substantial — both financially and creatively. questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the following question(s): The genesis of railway transportation marks one of humanity's most transformative engineering feats, profoundly reshaping industrial, social, and economic landscapes. Early prototypes, such as horse-drawn wagonways in 16th-century Europe, represented rudimentary precursors to modern trains, utilizing wooden rails to minimize friction and facilitate the movement of goods across short distances. The true revolution, however, ignited in the early 19th century with the advent of steam locomotives. Pioneers like George Stephenson, whose famous "Rocket" epitomized technological prowess, demonstrated the unprecedented potential of steam power to move both people and cargo efficiently. This innovation catalyzed the Industrial Revolution, knitting distant regions into cohesive economic fabrics and accelerating urbanization at an unparalleled pace. Throughout the 20th century, the ascendancy of diesel and electric locomotives superseded steam technology, offering greater efficiency, reliability, and environmental benefits. Bullet trains, inaugurated in Japan as the Shinkansen in 1964, redefined expectations regarding speed, safety, and technological sophistication, inspiring global high-speed rail networks. In the contemporary era, magnetic levitation (maglev) trains and hyperloop prototypes promise to further erode the barriers of distance and time, potentially rendering conventional rail obsolete. Yet, amid this rapid evolution, trains remain emblematic not merely of mechanical ingenuity but of societal progression — testaments to human ambition to connect, accelerate, and transcend physical limitations. The trajectory of railway innovation encapsulates a narrative of relentless adaptation, one wherein each epochal shift reflects broader socio-technological metamorphoses. Identify the tense and voice used in the sentence: "Early prototypes, such as horse-drawn wagon ways in 16th-century Europe, represented rudimentary precursors to modern trains..."
questionsEn.s:
The verb is "represented", which is the simple past form of "represent", so the tense is Simple Past.
The subject "Early prototypes" performs the action (it represented...), so the voice is Active.
Hence, the sentence is in Simple Past Active.

questionsEn.q: Read the cloze passage and answer the following questions: Indian classical music is one of the oldest musical traditions in the world, deeply _____(3) with the cultural and spiritual heritage of the country. It is broadly divided into two major systems: Hindustani music of the North and Carnatic music of the South. While both share ancient roots, they have evolved distinct styles, instruments, and performance techniques. Central to Indian classical music is the concept of the raga, a melodic framework that defines the mood, emotion, and time of performance. Each raga _____(4) like a musical personality, guiding the artist's improvisation and expression. Equally important is tala, the rhythmic cycle that provides structure and momentum to the composition. Together, raga and tala create an (2) intricate balance of melody and rhythm. Performances often begin with an alap, a slow and _____(5) introduction where the artist explores the raga without percussion. Gradually, the tempo increases, and the music builds into complex improvisations, engaging both the artist and the audience in a shared emotional journey. Instruments such as the sitar, sarod, veena, tabla, and mridangam, as well as vocal renditions, all play vital roles in conveying the depth of this art form. More than mere entertainment, Indian classical music is regarded as a form of meditation and storytelling. Its (1) enduring appeal lies in its ability to connect the listener to timeless emotions, bridging the ancient and the contemporary with grace and precision. In the passage, what does "Intricate" most nearly mean?
questionsEn.s:
Correct option (b)

The correct answer is 'complex'.

Key Points

• "Intricate" means something that is very detailed and complicated, or complex.

• In the passage, "an intricate balance of melody and rhythm" refers to the detailed and complex structure of Indian classical music.

• Other options ("simple", "ordinary", "weak") do not convey the intended meaning of "intricate".

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.

Usage Example: The artist created an intricate pattern, meaning the design was highly detailed and complex.

Additional Information

• Simple: Incorrect, as it is the opposite of "intricate".

• Ordinary: Incorrect, as it means common or usual.

• Weak: Incorrect, as it means lacking strength and does not relate to complexity.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the question.** Novels are a diverse and expansive category of fiction characterized by lengthy narratives that explore various themes, characters, and plots. Among the many types of novels, certain genres stand out due to their popularity and distinctive features. The mystery novel centers on a crime committed at the beginning of the story, usually a murder or theft. The narrative unfolds as characters seek to discover who committed the crime. In contrast, thriller novels focus on preventing a future crime, building suspense as protagonists race against time to stop devastating events. Both genres intrigue readers but from different narrative perspectives. The romance novel is dedicated to exploring the development of a romantic relationship. Typically, the story involves obstacles that lovers must overcome to reach a happy or emotionally satisfying ending. The science fiction novel transports readers to futuristic or imaginative worlds, incorporating advanced technology, space exploration, or alien life forms to explore human experience in speculative contexts. Other types include the psychological novel, which delves into the mental and emotional states of characters, often highlighting internal conflicts intertwined with thriller elements. The proletarian novel represents the working class's daily life, offering social or moral commentary without fantasy elements. Each novel type serves a unique purpose, catering to diverse reader interests and reflecting different aspects of human nature and society. **Identify the voice of the sentence.** "The narrative unfolds as characters seek to discover who committed the crime."
questionsEn.s: The sentence is in active voice because the subject “The narrative” performs the action “unfolds.” Passive voice would require a form like “is unfolded,” which is not used here. Causative voice involves making someone do something (have/get + object + past participle), and reflexive voice involves the subject acting on itself (using reflexive pronouns like “himself”). Learning points: active voice = subject does action; passive voice = subject receives action; intransitive verbs like “unfold” often appear naturally in active form; voice questions focus on verb form and subject-object relation; identify the main verb (“unfolds”) and its doer.

questionsEn.q: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:** 'The Movement' group was formed against the elitism of The Bloomsbury and Bohemia groups. These poets wrote ironical verses that celebrated the idea of English identity and were often immersed with nostalgia. The group included the novelist Kingsley Amis, the poet-novelist John Wain, poet-critic Donald Davie, poets Elizabeth Jennings, Thom Gunn, John Wain, D. J. Enright and Robert Conquest. The title 'the Movement' was coined by J. D. Scott, literary editor of The Spectator. This group shared antipathy towards the cultural pretensions of the Bohemian and the Bloomsbury group and in general, they had the disapproval of the elitism of the modernist writings. The writers of this group were identified by their class Origins, beer-drinking and pipe smoking habits. What were the reasons for the establishment of 'The Movement' group in Britain?
o: The oppositions were against the cultural pretensions and elitism of the Bloomsbury and Bohemian groups
Modernist elitism was advocated, and experimental writing styles were in the limelight
Romantic ideals were revived, and irony in poetry was completely rejected
Avant-garde art and radical political movements were encouraged instead
questionsEn.s: The passage explicitly says the group was formed “against the elitism” of the Bloomsbury and Bohemia groups and shared antipathy toward their cultural pretensions, so (a) matches directly. (b) is the opposite of the passage (they disapproved modernist elitism). (c) is wrong because the poets wrote “ironical verses” and were nostalgic. (d) is not stated; the passage does not emphasize avant-garde encouragement. Learning points: in RC, prefer options that restate exact passage ideas; watch for opposites/negations; identify the main purpose/formation reason; avoid choices adding new themes not mentioned; quote-based matching is safest.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the question.** In the annals of human achievement, the development of the spaceship stands as a monumental testament to the ingenuity and perseverance of scientists. Unlike any other invention, spaceships have revolutionized our understanding of the cosmos, allowing us to venture beyond Earth's atmosphere and unlock the mysteries of the universe. These vehicles are not merely mechanical constructs but intricate systems composed of advanced technology, engineering precision, and sheer human determination. Spaceships require a confluence of various scientific disciplines. Aerospace engineers meticulously design the structure, ensuring the spacecraft can withstand the extreme conditions of space, including vacuum, radiation, and temperature fluctuations. Astrophysicists provide crucial insights into celestial bodies and cosmic phenomena, guiding mission trajectories and objectives. Meanwhile, biologists study how living organisms can survive and adapt to the hostile environment beyond our planet, which is crucial for manned missions. Scientists who work on spaceship development often grapple with challenges that extend beyond terrestrial experiences. The absence of gravity affects both the mechanical operations of the spacecraft and the physiological well-being of astronauts. Communication delays, sometimes spanning minutes, complicate real-time decision-making. Despite these formidable obstacles, the collective efforts of multidisciplinary teams have repeatedly demonstrated triumph over adversity, pushing the very boundaries of human exploration. As humanity stands on the cusp of deeper interstellar journeys, the collaboration between centers of research, innovation, and space agencies worldwide is more vital than ever. These centers not only foster technological advancements but also cultivate the next generation of scientists who will carry the beacon of space exploration forward. **Choose the option that correctly fills in the blank in the sentence below.** "Scientists who work on spaceship development often ____ with challenges that extend beyond terrestrial experiences."
questionsEn.s: The subject “Scientists” is plural and the sentence is in present simple (general truth), so the base verb “grapple” is correct: “Scientists ... often grapple ...” (a) is past tense, (b) is a participle/gerund requiring an auxiliary, and (d) is singular present (“grapples”) which would match “A scientist,” not “Scientists.” Learning points: (1) “Often” commonly signals present simple for habits/general statements. (2) Plural subject takes base verb in present simple. (3) Verb forms: grapple (V1), grappled (V2/V3), grappling (V-ing). (4) Subject–verb agreement is essential in blanks.
