test.title: Word Usage

questionsEn.q: Choose the right collocation: The article offers a ______ critique of contemporary educational paradigms.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'thorough going'.

Key Points

• The phrase "thorough going" is a correct collocation and is used to describe something that is done thoroughly or comprehensively.

• It is commonly used in formal contexts, such as academic or critical writing, to emphasize the depth or completeness of an analysis or critique.

• Option 2: "through-going" and Option 3: "thorough-go" are incorrect as they are not standard collocations in the English language.

• Option 4: "go-through" is incorrect as it is not appropriate in the given context.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Complete Sentence: "The article offers a thorough going critique of contemporary educational paradigms."

Additional Information

• Option 2: "through-going" is not a valid English expression.

• Option 3: "thorough-go" is not used in English as a collocation or phrase.

• Option 4: "go-through" refers to the act of reviewing or examining something, which is unrelated to the intended meaning in this context.

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: The physician spoke ___, avoiding technical jargon so patients could understand.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'perspicuously'.

Key Points

• The word "perspicuously" means "clearly and understandably," which fits the context of a physician speaking in a way that avoids technical jargon.

• Perspicaciously (Option 2) refers to being insightful or having a keen understanding, which does not match the context of the sentence.

• Perspicuity (Option 3) is a noun and cannot grammatically fit in the blank.

• Perspiringly (Option 4) refers to sweating, which is irrelevant to the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Complete Sentence: "The physician spoke perspicuously, avoiding technical jargon so patients could understand."

Additional Information

• Option 2: "perspicaciously" is incorrect because the word means "insightfully" and does not fit the context of simplifying speech for patients.

• Option 3: "perspicuity" is a noun and cannot be used where an adverb is required.

• Option 4: "perspiringly" is unrelated to the context as it refers to sweating.

questionsEn.q: Choose the option that will replace the error highlighted in bold. Cassius spoke to Brutus under so influence of jealousy and pride.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is Option 3 — the.

The phrase “under the influence of” is the correct fixed expression. “So influence” is grammatically incorrect because so cannot be used as the determiner before the noun “influence” in this construction.

Correct sentence: Cassius spoke to Brutus under the influence of jealousy and pride.

questionsEn.q: Select the sentence with correct use of article 'the.'
o: Dr. Johnson met the Shakespeare in England.
Kalidas is the Shakespeare of India.
Dr. Johnson saw the Shakespeare acting in King Lear.
Dr. Johnson had instructed the Shakespeare to write The Tempest.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is Option 2.

Key Points

• In Option 2, the use of the article "the" is appropriate because the sentence compares Kalidas to Shakespeare, emphasizing his stature as the Shakespeare of India.

• Other options incorrectly use "the" before "Shakespeare" when referring to the historical figure or a specific instance, which is not grammatically correct.

• For instance, in Option 1, "the Shakespeare" implies a specific Shakespeare, which is incorrect as "Shakespeare" is a proper noun and does not need an article in this context.

• Option 3 and Option 4 also misuse "the Shakespeare" in contexts where it is not required or appropriate.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Correct Sentence: "Kalidas is the Shakespeare of India."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Dr. Johnson met the Shakespeare in England." – Incorrect because "Shakespeare" as a proper noun does not require "the" in this context.

• Option 3: "Dr. Johnson saw the Shakespeare acting in King Lear." – Incorrect because "the Shakespeare" implies a specific Shakespeare, which is not appropriate in this context.

• Option 4: "Dr. Johnson had instructed the Shakespeare to write The Tempest." – Incorrect because "the Shakespeare" is not the correct usage here when referring to the historical figure.

• Option 2: "Kalidas is the Shakespeare of India." – Correct because the comparison requires the definite article to indicate Kalidas's equivalence to Shakespeare in literary stature.

questionsEn.q: Choose the sentence which uses the adjective/adverb in its superlative degree correctly.
o: My uncle goes to that shop mostly frequently.
My uncle goes to that shop the more frequently.
My uncle goes to that shop very most frequently.
My uncle goes to that shop most frequently
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is Option 4.

Key Points

• The superlative degree of an adjective or adverb is used to compare three or more things or actions.

• In this question, the adverb "most frequently" is used to express the highest degree of frequency among possible comparisons.

• Option 4, "My uncle goes to that shop most frequently," uses the superlative degree correctly and is grammatically accurate.

• Options 1, 2, and 3 are either grammatically incorrect or do not use the superlative degree properly.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Correct Sentence: "My uncle goes to that shop most frequently."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "mostly frequently" is incorrect because "mostly" and "frequently" cannot be used together.

• Option 2: "the more frequently" is in the comparative degree, not the superlative degree.

• Option 3: "very most frequently" is incorrect because "very" is redundant and unnecessary in this context.

• Option 4: "most frequently" is correct and uses the superlative degree appropriately.

questionsEn.q: Which among the following sentences uses the article (if required) before the word 'honour' correctly?
o: It is the honour to be here.
It is an honour to be here.
It is honour to be here.
It is a honour to be here.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. It is an honour to be here.

Key Points

• The word 'honour' begins with a silent 'h', which makes it phonetically start with a vowel sound ('onour').

• When a word starts with a vowel sound, the article 'an' is used before it instead of 'a'.

• Option 2, 'It is an honour to be here,' correctly follows this rule.

Correct sentence: It is an honour to be here.

Additional Information

• Other options are incorrect:

• Option 1: 'the honour' is inappropriate here because 'the' is used for something specific or already mentioned.

• Option 3: 'honour' without an article is grammatically incomplete.

• Option 4: 'a honour' is incorrect because 'a' cannot precede words with vowel sounds.

questionsEn.q: Which among the following sentences uses adjective with correct degree of comparison.
o: New Delhi is more hotter to Chandigarh.
New Delhi is more hotter than Chandigarh.
New Delhi is hotter to Chandigarh.
New Delhi is hotter than Chandigarh
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. New Delhi is hotter than Chandigarh .

Key Points

• The question requires identifying the correct use of the 'degree of comparison' in a sentence.

• The adjective "hot" is used to compare two places: New Delhi and Chandigarh.

• The correct structure for comparing two entities is: Subject + comparative adjective (-er form or 'more' before the adjective) + than + object.

• In this case, the correct comparison is "hotter than" because "hotter" is the comparative form of "hot."

Correct sentence: New Delhi is hotter than Chandigarh.

Additional Information

• Explanation of incorrect options:

• Option 1: "New Delhi is more hotter to Chandigarh" is incorrect because "more" and "hotter" cannot be used together. Only one comparative form should be used.

• Option 2: "New Delhi is more hotter than Chandigarh" is incorrect for the same reason as Option 1--redundant use of "more."

• Option 3: "New Delhi is hotter to Chandigarh" is incorrect because "to" is not the correct preposition for comparison. The correct preposition is "than."

questionsEn.q: Choose the sentence with correct collocation for the word 'pattern'
o: The chef has arranged the cherries by a pattern.
The chef has arranged the cherries of a pattern.
The chef has arranged the cherries with a pattern.
The chef has arranged the cherries in a pattern.

questionsEn.q: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
o: He went to college in a train.
He went to college with a train.
He went to college by a train.
He went to college on a train.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is Option 4.

Key Points

• The usage of prepositions is crucial for conveying the correct meaning in sentences.

• The preposition "on" is used to indicate a mode of transportation like a train, bus, or plane.

• In contrast, prepositions such as "in" or "with" are incorrect in this context.

• The phrase "by a train" is grammatically incorrect because "by" is generally used without an article when referring to modes of transport (e.g., "by train").

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Correct Sentence: "He went to college on a train."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "He went to college in a train." - This is incorrect because "in" is not used for this mode of transportation.

• Option 2: "He went to college with a train." - This is incorrect as "with" implies accompaniment, which is not applicable here.

• Option 3: "He went to college by a train." - This is incorrect because "by" does not require an article for modes of transport (e.g., "by train").

test.title: Phrasal Verbs

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: The journalist refused to ___ her sources despite repeated legal threats.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. give away.

Key Points

• The sentence refers to a journalist refusing to reveal or disclose the identity of her sources. The correct phrasal verb is "give away", which can mean to reveal or disclose something that is intended to remain secret.

• The meanings of the options are as follows:

• Give away: To reveal or disclose a secret or information. This is the correct answer.

• Give out: To distribute, issue, or announce something; it does not fit the context as precisely as 'give away'.

• Give over: To hand something over or stop an activity; it does not fit the context.

• Give up: To surrender, abandon, or stop doing something; it does not fit the context.

• Therefore, "give away" is the most appropriate phrasal verb in this sentence.

Correct sentence: The journalist refused to give away her sources despite repeated legal threats.

Additional Information

• Give away is commonly used when someone unintentionally or deliberately reveals a secret, clue, or information.

• Example: She refused to give away the details of the investigation.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The issue was so delicate that she chose to ____ it altogether.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. shy away from .

Key Points

• The phrasal verb "shy away from" means to avoid something because of fear, discomfort, or reluctance.

• In the given sentence, the issue is described as delicate, implying it required careful handling or avoidance. The phrase "shy away from" is the most appropriate choice to convey this meaning.

• Other options such as "brush aside", "walk into", or "lean over" do not fit the context of deliberately avoiding a sensitive issue.

Correct sentence: The issue was so delicate that she chose to shy away from it altogether.

Additional Information

• Brush aside: Means to dismiss something as unimportant or irrelevant.

• Walk into: Refers to entering or encountering something, often unexpectedly.

• Lean over: Indicates bending the upper body forward or sideways.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The scientist was unable to _____ a definitive conclusion from the data.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. arrive at .

Key Points

• The phrase "arrive at" is commonly used to indicate reaching a conclusion or decision after careful consideration or analysis.

• In the given sentence, the scientist was trying to come to a definitive conclusion based on the data, making "arrive at" the most appropriate choice.

• Other options like "draw out," "bring up," and "make over" do not fit the context or meaning required in the sentence.

Correct sentence: The scientist was unable to arrive at a definitive conclusion from the data.

Additional Information

• Usage of Phrasal Verbs:

• Draw out: To extract information or to prolong something (e.g., "The teacher tried to draw out answers from the students.").

• Bring up: To mention or introduce a topic (e.g., "She brought up the issue during the meeting.").

• Make over: To change or improve something (e.g., "The house was made over completely.").

questionsEn.q: Select the correct phrasal verb: We need to ____ the old files before moving the new ones.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. clean out.

Key Points

• The word "clean out" means to remove everything from inside a space or container, typically to tidy it up or make room for something else. (अंदर से साफ करना)

• Example: I need to clean out my closet to make space for new clothes.

• In the given sentence, "We need to ____ the old files before moving the new ones," the correct word is "clean out" because it involves removing old files completely to make way for the new ones. (अंदर से साफ करना)

• Example: Before the new project begins, the team has to clean out the old documents.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 - clean out.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

• Clear off (हटा देना): To leave a place quickly or to remove something from a surface.

• Example: The teacher told the students to clear off their desks before the exam.

• Wipe over (साफ़ करना): To clean a surface quickly and lightly, usually with a cloth.

• Example: She wiped over the kitchen counter after cooking dinner.

• Go over (जांच करना): To review or examine something carefully.

• Example: Let's go over the presentation one more time before the meeting.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the right phrasal verb: The investigation was ____ after new evidence emerged.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. 'taken up'.

Key Points

• The phrasal verb Taken up means to start or resume an activity or investigation. (शुरू करना या फिर से आरंभ करना)

• Example: The case was taken up again after fresh complaints were filed.

• In the sentence new evidence suggests that the investigation was started again or resumed.

• Hence taken up fits correctly in the blank according to meaning and grammar.

Therefore the correct answer is taken up

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings

• Called off (रद्द करना): To cancel something.

• Picked up (उठाना या सुधार होना): To collect or improve but not suitable in this context.

• Revived up This is grammatically incorrect the correct phrase is revived.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The professor asked the student to ____ her thesis argument.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'expand on'.

Key Points

• The phrasal verb "expand on" means to provide more details or elaborate on a specific topic.

• In the context of the sentence, the professor is asking the student to elaborate on her thesis argument, which aligns with the meaning of "expand on."

• Options 1, 3, and 4 do not fit the context as they do not convey the intended meaning of elaborating or providing additional details.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Complete Sentence: "The professor asked the student to expand on her thesis argument."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "follow up" is incorrect because it means to check on or continue something, which is unrelated to elaborating on an argument.

• Option 3: "point out" is incorrect because it means to indicate or highlight something, not to elaborate on it.

• Option 4: "call for" is incorrect because it means to demand or require something, which does not fit the context.

questionsEn.q: Select the correct phrasal verb: He finally ____ to the pressure and resigned.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. gave in .

Key Points

• The phrasal verb "gave in" means to yield or surrender to pressure, force, or persuasion. It fits the context of the sentence where the individual succumbs to pressure and resigns.

• The other options do not convey the correct meaning in this context:

• "gave up": Means to stop trying or to quit, but it does not fit this context of yielding to pressure.

• "gave out": Refers to distributing or exhausting, which is unrelated to the sentence.

• "gave over": Means to transfer responsibility or stop doing something, but it is incorrect for this context.

• Thus, "gave in" is the correct choice for the blank.

Correct sentence: He finally gave in to the pressure and resigned.

Additional Information

• Phrasal Verbs: Phrasal verbs are multi-word expressions that combine a verb with a preposition or adverb to create a meaning different from the individual words.

• Examples of Common Phrasal Verbs:

• Break down: To stop working (e.g., "The car broke down").

• Carry on: To continue (e.g., "Please carry on with your work").

• Run out of: To exhaust a supply (e.g., "We ran out of milk").

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: The department was asked to ____ the outdated protocol.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is: Option 1 (phase out).

Key Points

• The phrasal verb "phase out" means to gradually stop using or doing something, especially in a systematic or planned way. (क्रमिक रूप से समाप्त करना)

• Example: The company decided to phase out the production of its older models to focus on new technology.

• The word "phase out" is appropriate for situations where something outdated or no longer useful is being removed step by step. (पुराने या अनुपयोगी चीज़ को धीरे-धीरे समाप्त करना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (phase out).

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

• Hand off (सौंपना): To give responsibility or control of something to someone else.

• Example: The manager decided to hand off the project to a more experienced team.

• Come across (सामना करना): To find or meet something or someone by chance.

• Example: While cleaning the attic, I came across my grandmother’s old letters.

• Play down (महत्त्व कम करना): To minimize the importance of something.

• Example: She tried to play down the significance of her achievements, but everyone knew how hard she worked.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: After months of negotiation, the two sides finally _____ an agreement acceptable to both parties.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'arrived at'.

Key Points

• The phrasal verb "arrived at" is used to indicate reaching a conclusion, decision, or agreement.

• In the given sentence, the context involves reaching an agreement after negotiations, making "arrived at" the correct choice.

• Options 1, 3, and 4 are incorrect because they are not idiomatically used for reaching an agreement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Complete Sentence: "After months of negotiation, the two sides finally arrived at an agreement acceptable to both parties."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "arrived to" is incorrect as it is not idiomatically used in English for reaching an agreement or conclusion.

• Option 3: "arrived on" is incorrect; it is typically used with physical locations or dates, not agreements.

• Option 4: "arrived with" is incorrect because it implies bringing something physically, which does not fit the context.

questionsEn.q: Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence. Radium ________ rays that can damage the eyes.
questionsEn.s:
“Give off” means to emit or release, especially heat, light, gas, or radiation. Radium emits rays, so “gives off” is the correct phrasal verb. “Gives over” means stop or hand over, “gives up” means surrender, and “gives away” means donate or reveal.
Learning points:
- “Give off” = emit
- “Give up” = quit/surrender
- “Give away” = donate/reveal
- Scientific contexts often use “emit” or “give off”

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: She was so overwhelmed with tasks that she had to ___ some responsibilities to her assistant.
questionsEn.s: The phrasal verb **hand over** means to delegate or pass responsibility to someone else. This perfectly fits the context of an overwhelmed person giving tasks to an assistant for completion.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: The investigation team will ___ every detail before concluding the report.
questionsEn.s: The phrasal verb **go through** means to examine or review something carefully and methodically. This perfectly fits the context of an investigation team meticulously analyzing every detail before finalizing a report.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: The startup failed to _____ the expectations it had generated among investors.
questionsEn.s: "Live up to" means to meet expectations or standards. Hence it fits the sentence correctly.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: The spokesperson tried to _____ the media frenzy by issuing a calm, factual statement.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: She always _____ her failures to bad luck rather than taking ownership.
questionsEn.s: "Put down to" means to attribute something to a particular cause. Here she attributes her failures to bad luck. "Turns out" means proves to be, "breaks into" means enters suddenly or starts abruptly, and "boils down" means reduces to the essence.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: The deal fell through because the parties couldn't ______ on the terms.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: When the scandal broke, the minister tried to _____ responsibility and blame his aides.
questionsEn.s: "Pass the buck" means shift responsibility to someone else. That fits the idea of blaming aides instead of accepting fault.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate phrasal verb: Her speech was so moving that it ______ strong emotions in the audience.
questionsEn.s: **Stirred up** means aroused or provoked emotions. That fits the meaning best. “Brought out” can mean reveal, but “stirred up emotions” is the standard expression.

questionsEn.q: Improve the sentence using the correct phrasal verb of the underlined words. The thieves managed to **get off** the police during the chase.
questionsEn.s: "Get away from" means escape from someone, which fits the context of a chase. "Get off" is incorrect here. The other phrasal verbs mean maintain good relations, recover from something, and finish or make contact, none of which fit the sentence.

questionsEn.q: Improve the sentence using the correct phrasal verb of the underlined words. The thieves managed to get off the police during the chase.
questionsEn.s: “Get away from” means escape from someone, which fits the context of thieves escaping the police. “Get off the police” is incorrect.

questionsEn.q: Improve the following sentence by replacing the underlined words with the correct phrasal verb. After months of training, she was ready **to go through** the final exam.
questionsEn.s: "Go in for" means to appear for or participate in an examination, which fits the sentence. "Go through" is incorrect in this sense.

questionsEn.q: Improve the following sentence by replacing the underlined words with the correct phrasal verb. After months of training, she was ready **to go through** the final exam.
questionsEn.s: **Go in for** can mean to appear for or take part in something like an examination. **Go through** means experience or examine, which is not suitable here. The other options do not fit the meaning.

questionsEn.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She didn’t want to talk about it, but he kept _____ the topic.
questionsEn.s: "Bringing up" means introducing a topic into conversation. The sentence requires that meaning.

questionsEn.q: Improve the sentence using the correct phrasal verb of the underlined word. You must not **fall out** your parents, no matter how angry you are.
questionsEn.s: The correct phrasal verb is "fall out with someone," meaning to quarrel with someone. So the sentence should read: "You must not fall out with your parents..."

questionsEn.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I can't believe you ______ that old trick!
questionsEn.s: "Fell for" means to be deceived by or believe a trick. It fits the context perfectly.

questionsEn.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He was late because he _______ heavy traffic on the way to work.
questionsEn.s:
"Ran into" means “met/encountered unexpectedly,” so it fits the sentence:
He was late because he ran into heavy traffic on the way to work.
Other options do not fit the meaning here:
- looked into = investigated
- got through = managed to finish / contacted by phone
- kept up = maintained / continued at the same level

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the questions: "Normal science, the activity in which most scientists inevitably spend almost all their time, is based on the assumption that the scientific community knows what the world is like. Scientists take great pains to defend that assumption, often restricting their vision to the phenomena that the existing paradigm has defined as relevant. When research proceeds in this fashion, findings tend to be incremental, reinforcing the established framework rather than challenging it. Yet, over time, anomalies-empirical observations that cannot be explained within the current paradigm-accumulate. Initially, these anomalies are dismissed as errors or as problems to be solved within the existing theoretical structure. However, as these anomalies grow in number and significance, they begin to erode confidence in the prevailing paradigm. The resolution of such crises is not a straightforward process of falsification, as Popper might suggest, but rather a transformation in the very way scientists see the world. Scientific revolutions occur when a new paradigm emerges-one that is not merely an extension of the old but a fundamental reconceptualization of reality. This shift is not purely logical or empirical; it involves a radical change in perspective, akin to a gestalt switch. The Copernican Revolution, for example, did not merely adjust astronomical calculations; it redefined the very framework through which celestial motion was understood. Similarly, Einstein's theory of relativity did not just modify Newtonian mechanics but replaced its foundational assumptions about space and time. Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The marketing campaign was so vague that its message failed to ___ with the target audience.

questionsEn.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please switch ___ the lights.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'off'.

Key Points

• The verb "switch off" is commonly used to indicate turning off an electrical device, such as lights.

• The other options do not fit the context of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Complete Sentence: "Please switch off the lights."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "down" is incorrect because it does not indicate the action of turning off lights.

• Option 2: "up" is incorrect because it typically refers to turning something on or increasing brightness, not turning off.

• Option 3: "over" is incorrect because it does not fit the context of switching off lights.

questionsEn.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The witness was reluctant to part ____ vital information.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'with'.

Key Points

• The preposition "with" is used when referring to the act of parting or separating from something.

• In the context of the sentence, the witness was hesitant to part with vital information, indicating reluctance in sharing or giving up something.

• Options 1, 2, and 4 are grammatically incorrect and do not fit the context.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Complete Sentence: "The witness was reluctant to part with vital information."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "by" is incorrect because "part by" does not convey the intended meaning in this context.

• Option 2: "of" is incorrect because "part of" implies belonging to something, which does not fit the sentence.

• Option 4: "from" is incorrect because "part from" is not appropriate when referring to reluctance in sharing information.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option The director's remarks did not ______ well with the board members, leading to immediate backlash.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'go over'.

Key Points

• The phrasal verb "go over" means to be received or accepted in a particular way by others.

• In the given sentence, the director's remarks were not well received by the board members, leading to a backlash, so "go over" is the most appropriate choice.

• Options 1, 2, and 4 are incorrect because they do not convey the intended meaning in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Complete Sentence: "The director's remarks did not go over well with the board members, leading to immediate backlash."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "go out" is incorrect because it means to leave a place or to stop functioning, which does not fit the context.

• Option 2: "go in" is incorrect because it implies entering a place, which is irrelevant here.

• Option 4: "go off" is incorrect because it typically means to explode or to stop working, which does not make sense in this context.

questionsEn.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The thief broke _______ the house.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'into'.

Key Points

• The preposition "into" is used to indicate movement towards the interior of a place or object.

• In this context, the thief "broke into" the house, which is the correct usage.

• Options 1, 3, and 4 are grammatically incorrect in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Complete Sentence: "The thief broke into the house."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "by" is incorrect because "by" indicates proximity or method, not entry.

• Option 3: "in" is incorrect because "broke in" is incomplete without "into" for this context.

• Option 4: "at" is incorrect because "at" indicates location, not movement.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct option that replaces the underline word/phrase in the following sentence: Sujata put in the best dress for the party
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is Option 3.

Key Points

• The phrasal verb "put in" is incorrectly used in this sentence.

• The correct phrasal verb to indicate wearing something is "put on."

• Phrasal verbs have specific meanings, and using the wrong one can change the intended meaning of the sentence.

• Thus, the phrase "put in" must be replaced with "put on" to ensure the sentence is grammatically correct and meaningful.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Correct Sentence: "Sujata put on the best dress for the party."

Additional Information

• Put off - Means to postpone or delay something. This does not fit the context of the sentence.

• Put across - Means to communicate or explain something clearly. This is not relevant to the sentence.

• Put out - Means to extinguish something (like a fire) or to inconvenience someone. This does not suit the sentence context.

questionsEn.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She was brought ________ by her grandmother.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'up'.

Key Points

• The phrasal verb "brought up" means to raise or nurture someone, especially a child.

• In this context, the sentence is referring to the action of raising the subject by her grandmother, so "up" is the correct choice.

• Options 1, 2, and 4 are incorrect, as they do not fit the meaning conveyed by the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Complete Sentence: "She was brought up by her grandmother."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "out" is incorrect as "brought out" usually means to produce or reveal something, not to raise someone.

• Option 2: "off" is incorrect as "brought off" means to succeed in doing something difficult, which does not apply in this context.

• Option 4: "in" is incorrect as "brought in" means to introduce or include something or someone, which does not fit here.

questionsEn.q: Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence: The **dessert** is a dry piece of land.
questionsEn.s: The correct word for a dry piece of land is "desert". "Dessert" means a sweet course after a meal. The other options are incorrect spellings or unrelated forms.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct word. She decided to ______ down and rest for a while.
questionsEn.s: The correct phrase is **lie down**, where **lie** means to recline. **Lay** usually takes an object, as in “lay the book down.”

questionsEn.q: Choose the sentence with correct usage of "less" and "fewer".
o: She has less books than I do.
There are fewer sugar in the jar.
We need fewer volunteers this time.
He has fewer money than his brother.
questionsEn.s: "Fewer" is used with countable nouns, and "volunteers" is countable. The other options incorrectly use "less" or "fewer" with the wrong noun type.

questionsEn.q: Which sentence correctly uses confirm?
o: Please confirm your attendance before Friday.
They conform the package before delivery.
He couldn’t confirm to the crowd's pressure.
She confirmed with the regulations strictly.
questionsEn.s: "Confirm" means verify or state with assurance. Only option (a) uses it correctly. Option (b) confuses it with "conform."

questionsEn.q: Which sentence uses "borne" correctly?
o: The cost was borne by the company.
He has borne arms for years.
The queen has born two sons.
questionsEn.s: "Borne" is the past participle of "bear" in the sense of carried or endured. Thus "The cost was borne by the company" is correct. "Born" is used for birth.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence. He will ___ the award at the ceremony tomorrow.
questionsEn.s:
Correct option (b)

The correct answer is 'accept'.

Key Points

• The word "accept" means to agree to receive or take something, which fits the context of receiving the award.

• The word "except" means to exclude and does not fit the sentence contextually.

• "Access" refers to the ability to approach or enter a place, which is unrelated to receiving an award.

• "Aspect" means a feature or part of something and is not relevant to the given sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Complete Sentence: "He will accept the award at the ceremony tomorrow."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "except" is incorrect because it means to exclude and does not align with the context of receiving an award.

• Option 3: "access" is incorrect because it refers to entering or approaching a place and has no relevance here.

• Option 4: "aspect" is incorrect because it refers to a feature or part of something, which is unrelated to the context.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence. He was asked to ________ the meeting.
questionsEn.s:
Correct option (b)

The correct answer is 'proceed'.

Key Points

• The word "proceed" means to continue or begin an action, especially after a pause or interruption.

• In the context of the sentence, "He was asked to proceed the meeting", it is grammatically correct as it refers to starting or continuing the meeting.

• Options 1, 3, and 4 are incorrect because:

• Option 1: "precede" means to come before something, which does not fit the context.

• Option 3: "preseed" is not a valid word in English.

• Option 4: "process" refers to a series of steps to achieve a result, which does not fit the meaning intended in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Complete Sentence: "He was asked to proceed the meeting."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "precede" is incorrect because it means to come before something in time or order, which does not align with the context.

• Option 3: "preseed" is invalid as it is not a recognized English word.

• Option 4: "process" is incorrect because it refers to a series of steps or actions, not the act of continuing or starting a meeting.

questionsEn.q: Which word matches the clue "to praise"?
questionsEn.s:
Correct option (a)

The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Compliment.

Key Points

• The word "Compliment" means to express praise, admiration, or approval for someone or something. (प्रशंसा करना)

• Example: She received a lot of compliments on her beautiful dress.

• The correct word here is "Compliment" because the question asks for a word that matches the clue "to praise". (प्रशंसा करना)

• Example: He complimented the chef for the delicious meal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Compliment.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

• Complement (पूरक): Something that completes or goes well with something else.

• Example: The blue curtains complement the yellow walls beautifully.

• Complimentary (निःशुल्क): Something given for free or expressing praise.

• Example: The hotel offered complimentary breakfast to all its guests.

• Complyment (invalid word): This is a misspelling and does not exist in English vocabulary.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.** The writer often used clever ______ to hint at deeper meanings.
questionsEn.s: “Allusions” are indirect references that hint at something (literature, history, ideas), fitting the context of deeper meanings. “Illusions” are false perceptions; “delusions” are fixed false beliefs; “elusions” is not the intended word here (rare/incorrect in this context). Learning points: allusion ≠ illusion (reference vs false appearance); “to allude to” = to refer indirectly; writers use allusions to add layers of meaning; context clue “hint” strongly signals “allusions”; build vocabulary by common pairs (affect/effect, allusion/illusion).

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.** The thief tried to ______ the police by hiding in the forest.
questionsEn.s: “Elude” means to evade/escape capture, which fits the context of avoiding the police. “Allude” means to refer indirectly; “illusion” is a false perception; “allusion” is an indirect reference. Learning points: (1) Elude (verb) = evade. (2) Allude (verb) = hint/mention indirectly. (3) Allusion (noun) = indirect reference. (4) Illusion (noun) = deceptive appearance. (5) In vocabulary questions, identify part of speech needed by the sentence.

questionsEn.q: Which sentence has the correct usage?
o: He is a man of high council.
He is a man of high counsel.
He is a man of high cancel.
He is a man of high consul.
questionsEn.s: “Counsel” means advice or a legal adviser; “a man of high counsel” implies a person of great wisdom/advice. “Council” is an assembly/committee; “cancel” is a verb; “consul” is a diplomatic officer. Learning points: council (group) vs counsel (advice/lawyer); sound-alike errors are common; check part of speech; meaning must fit the sentence.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.** The school will _____ the new rules from next Monday.
questionsEn.s: “Adopt” means to accept and start using/implementing something (rules/policy), so it is correct. “Adept” is an adjective meaning skilled. “Addict” is generally a noun/verb related to dependency. “Adapt” means to adjust/modify to suit conditions, not to formally implement rules. Learning points: (1) adopt = accept/implement; (2) adapt = adjust/change; (3) adept = skilled; (4) common exam trap: adopt vs adapt; (5) collocation: “adopt rules/policy/measure”.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence. The teacher advised him to _____ his mistakes instead of hiding them.
questionsEn.s:
“Admit” means to acknowledge or confess, which fits the context: admit mistakes. “Admet” is incorrect spelling. “Omit” means leave out/skip, which doesn’t fit. “Admin” is a noun/short form and not appropriate here.
Learning points: (1) Correct collocation: admit a mistake. (2) Grammar: “to + base verb” → “to admit.” (3) Avoid near-looking words: omit vs admit. (4) Spelling trap: admet. (5) Meaning-based completion is safer than guessing.

questionsEn.s: Correct option (a) advise, advice

test.title: Sentences Completion

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: Nothing short of a paradigm shift will ____ the entrenched bureaucratic inertia.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. dislodge .

Key Points

• The given sentence talks about the need for a paradigm shift to counteract entrenched bureaucratic inertia, implying a strong and forceful action is required.

• The verb “dislodge” means to remove or force out from a position or state, which fits perfectly in the context of overcoming entrenched inertia.

• Other options like “persuade” and “disillusion” do not convey the idea of forceful removal, while “dissuasion” is a noun and does not fit grammatically.

Correct sentence: Nothing short of a paradigm shift will dislodge the entrenched bureaucratic inertia.

Additional Information

• Entrenched: Refers to something deeply established or fixed.

• Inertia: A tendency to resist change or remain unchanged.

• Dislodge: To forcibly remove something or someone from a position.

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: The reforms, while ostensibly motivated by economic exigencies, were in effect a veiled attempt to ____ dissent under the guise of austerity.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'quell'.

Key Points

• The verb "quell" means to suppress or subdue something, especially by force.

• The sentence context indicates that the reforms were designed to suppress (or "quell") dissent.

• Options 2, 3, and 4 do not fit the sentence context:

• Option 2 (swell): "Swell" means to increase in size or number, which is the opposite of suppression.

• Option 3 (rebut): "Rebut" means to argue or refute something, which does not fit the meaning of suppressing dissent.

• Option 4 (impugn): "Impugn" means to challenge or question something, which is unrelated to the act of suppression.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Complete Sentence: "The reforms, while ostensibly motivated by economic exigencies, were in effect a veiled attempt to quell dissent under the guise of austerity."

Additional Information

• Option 2 (swell): Does not match the context, as it implies growth or increase, which is contradictory to the intended meaning.

• Option 3 (rebut): Incorrect because rebut refers to arguing against something, not suppressing it.

• Option 4 (impugn): Incorrect because impugn refers to questioning or challenging something, not quelling dissent.

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: Her rebuttal, though eloquent, failed to ____ the central issue raised by the opposition.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'address'.

Key Points

• The word "address" means to deal with or discuss a particular issue or topic.

• The sentence suggests that although the rebuttal was eloquent, it failed to directly deal with the central issue raised by the opposition.

• Options 2, 3, and 4 are incorrect as they imply deviating from or avoiding the issue, which is contrary to the intended meaning of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Complete Sentence: "Her rebuttal, though eloquent, failed to address the central issue raised by the opposition."

Additional Information

• Option 2: "digress" is incorrect because it means to stray away from the topic, which doesn’t fit the context.

• Option 3: "circumvent" is incorrect as it means to avoid dealing with something, which is not the intended meaning.

• Option 4: "elude" is incorrect because it means to escape or avoid, which doesn’t align with the context of addressing the issue.

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: Her argument was compelling; ___, it was based on outdated data.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. nevertheless .

Key Points

• The sentence conveys a contrast between the compelling nature of the argument and the fact that it is based on outdated data.

• The word "nevertheless" is used to introduce a contrasting idea while maintaining coherence in the statement.

• The other options do not fit the context as they fail to provide a logical contrast:

• Option 1: "otherwise" suggests an alternative condition, which is not relevant here.

• Option 2: "conversely" indicates a reversal of a situation, which is not applicable.

• Option 4: "subsequently" refers to time sequence, which is irrelevant to the contrast being presented.

Correct sentence: Her argument was compelling; nevertheless, it was based on outdated data.

Additional Information

• Usage of Nevertheless:

• Definition: "Nevertheless" is used to introduce a contrasting idea despite the previous statement.

• Example: The weather was cold; nevertheless, they went for a walk.

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: Had it not been for her timely intervention, the discussion might well have ____ into an acrimonious stalemate.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. devolved .

Key Points

• The sentence uses the construction "Had it not been for...", which is a way of expressing a hypothetical past situation.

• The word "devolved" is appropriate here because it means to "degenerate" or "deteriorate" into a worse state, which fits the context of the discussion potentially becoming acrimonious and reaching a stalemate.

• The other options don't fit the context:

• evolved: Implies a positive or neutral progression, which is contrary to the negative tone implied in the sentence.

• emerged: Refers to coming into existence or becoming visible, which doesn't align with the idea of deterioration.

• absorbed: Refers to soaking up or integrating, which is irrelevant to the context.

Correct sentence: Had it not been for her timely intervention, the discussion might well have devolved into an acrimonious stalemate.

Additional Information

• Understanding "Had it not been for...":

• This phrase is used to express that something would have happened if it weren't for a specific action or event.

• It often sets up a hypothetical situation in the past.

• Usage of "devolved":

• Devolved is commonly used in contexts where there is a decline or regression to a worse state.

• Example: The meeting devolved into chaos after the heated argument.

questionsEn.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The government's new policies sought to _________ economic growth, not stifle it.
questionsEn.s: Ans: (C) stimulate

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: The philosopher's stance was diametrically ____ to the prevailing orthodoxy.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'opposed'.

Key Points

• The word "opposed" means being in direct conflict or contrast with something.

• The sentence indicates that the philosopher's stance was completely contrary to the prevailing orthodoxy, which aligns with the meaning of "opposed."

• Options 1, 2, and 3 do not fit the context. "Adverse" and "averse" have different meanings, and "converse" does not describe direct opposition.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Complete Sentence: "The philosopher's stance was diametrically opposed to the prevailing orthodoxy."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "adverse" refers to something harmful or unfavorable, which does not fit the context here.

• Option 2: "averse" refers to a strong dislike, not a direct opposition.

• Option 3: "converse" means something reversed in position or order, which does not convey the intended meaning.

questionsEn.q: Although the experiment had been meticulously designed, unforeseen variables ____ the reliability of its conclusions.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'undermined'.

Key Points

• The verb "undermined" means to weaken or reduce the effectiveness, power, or ability of something, which fits the context of the sentence.

• The sentence indicates that unforeseen variables negatively impacted the reliability of the experiment's conclusions, making "undermined" the appropriate choice.

• Options 2, 3, and 4 do not align with the intended meaning of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Complete Sentence: "Although the experiment had been meticulously designed, unforeseen variables undermined the reliability of its conclusions."

Additional Information

• Option 2: "bolstered" is incorrect because it means to support or strengthen, which is the opposite of the intended meaning.

• Option 3: "ratified" is incorrect because it means to formally approve or confirm, which does not fit the context.

• Option 4: "exacerbated" is incorrect because it means to make something worse, which does not align with the idea of impacting reliability.

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: The artifact was notable not merely for its age but also for the ____ with which it was preserved.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. meticulousness .

Key Points

• The given sentence discusses two aspects of the artifact: its age and the way it was preserved.

• The missing word must describe the quality or manner in which the artifact was preserved.

• Out of the provided options:

• Meticulousness: Refers to extreme care or attention to detail, which fits perfectly in the context of how the artifact was preserved.

• Velocity: Refers to speed, which is irrelevant here.

• Brevity: Refers to shortness, particularly in speech or writing, and does not suit the context.

• Severity: Refers to harshness, which is also unrelated to the preservation of the artifact.

Correct sentence: The artifact was notable not merely for its age but also for the meticulousness with which it was preserved.

Additional Information

• This question tests vocabulary and the ability to choose a word that fits the context of the sentence.

• When solving such questions:

• Understand the context of the sentence.

• Eliminate options that do not fit the meaning or tone of the sentence.

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: Only after years of archival research did the historian manage to ____ the contradictory accounts of the regime's collapse.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'reconcile'.

Key Points

• The verb "reconcile" means to bring together or make consistent conflicting ideas, accounts, or facts.

• In this sentence, the historian had to resolve or harmonize the contradictory accounts of the regime's collapse, which aligns with the meaning of "reconcile."

• Options 1, 2, and 4 are incorrect because they do not convey the meaning of resolving or harmonizing contradictions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Complete Sentence: "Only after years of archival research did the historian manage to reconcile the contradictory accounts of the regime's collapse."

Additional Information

• Option 1: "retract" is incorrect because it means to withdraw or take back something, which does not fit the context.

• Option 2: "revise" is incorrect because it means to change or modify something, but it does not convey the idea of harmonizing contradictions.

• Option 4: "reverberate" is incorrect because it means to echo or resound, which is unrelated to the context.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct option: The anthropologist's findings were considered so controversial that they were initially ______.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'disregarded'.

Key Points

• The anthropologist's findings were considered controversial, which suggests that they were not immediately accepted.

• The word "disregarded" fits this context as it means "ignored" or "not given importance."

• Options 2 ("celebrated"), 3 ("acclaimed"), and 4 ("adopted") imply positive reception, which contradicts the idea of controversy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Complete Sentence: "The anthropologist's findings were considered so controversial that they were initially disregarded."

Additional Information

• Option 2: "celebrated" is incorrect because controversial findings are unlikely to be celebrated immediately.

• Option 3: "acclaimed" is incorrect because acclaim typically follows widespread acceptance, not controversy.

• Option 4: "adopted" is incorrect because adopting something implies approval, which contradicts the initial controversy.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct semantic fit: The intervention was seen as a ____ to escalating tensions.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. deterrent.

Key Points

• The sentence indicates that the intervention aimed to prevent or reduce escalating tensions. The word 'deterrent' fits best in this context as it refers to something that discourages or prevents a particular action.

• The other options do not fit semantically. For example:

• 'Detention' refers to confining someone or keeping someone in custody, which does not suit the context.

• 'Detraction' refers to diminishing someone's reputation, irrelevant to this sentence.

• 'Derision' means mockery or ridicule, which does not align with the meaning.

Correct sentence: The intervention was seen as a deterrent to escalating tensions.

Additional Information

• A 'deterrent' is often used in situations to describe actions, interventions, or measures intended to discourage undesirable behavior or outcomes.

• It is commonly used in contexts like policy-making, conflict resolution, and crime prevention.

questionsEn.q: Select the correct option: Far from being a liability, his dissenting views often served as a ____ to complacency within the group.
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is 'counterweight'.

Key Points

• The term "counterweight" refers to something that serves to balance or counteract something else.

• In the context of the sentence, the dissenting views provided a balance or a challenge to the complacency within the group.

• Options 2, 3, and 4 do not fit the context of the sentence:

• Option 2: detriment suggests harm or damage, which does not align with the positive contribution of dissenting views.

• Option 3: digression suggests a departure from the main topic, which is unrelated to the sentence's meaning.

• Option 4: repudiation suggests rejection or denial, which does not fit the context of serving as a balance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Complete Sentence: "Far from being a liability, his dissenting views often served as a counterweight to complacency within the group."

Additional Information

• Option 2: detriment refers to harm or damage, which is not the intended meaning in the context.

• Option 3: digression means a departure from the main subject, which is irrelevant here.

• Option 4: repudiation means rejection or denial, which does not align with the idea of balancing complacency.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate verb: She _____ her position on the matter only after repeated questioning by the press.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The legislation was passed with ______ support, uniting parties across the political spectrum.
questionsEn.s: **Unanimous support** means everyone agreed. That best fits the idea of parties across the political spectrum uniting. “Partisan” means biased toward one side, which is the opposite.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The professor’s remarks were so ______ that even seasoned scholars found them difficult to decipher.
questionsEn.s: **Enigmatic** means mysterious or difficult to understand. Since the remarks were difficult to decipher, this is the most appropriate word.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The philosopher's ideas were so ______ that they challenged conventional understanding of time and existence.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The ambassador’s tone was _____, balancing diplomacy with quiet authority.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The legislation was passed with _____ support, uniting parties across the political spectrum.
questionsEn.s: "Unanimous support" means everyone supported it, which matches "uniting parties across the political spectrum." The other options do not fit the context.

questionsEn.q: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option: The CEO’s sudden resignation sent _____ through the corporate world.
questionsEn.s: The idiomatic expression is “sent tremors through,” meaning caused shock or disturbance. The other options do not fit the context.

questionsEn.q: Choose the correct option to fill in the blank in the sentence given. When filling out admission forms, it is ______ to fill up our complete names and date of birth.
questionsEn.s: The context of filling out official papers like admission forms requires compulsory information such as full name and date of birth, making **mandatory** the logically correct choice.

questionsEn.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks: If you plant hard work, you will reap ------------.
questionsEn.s: The metaphor "plant hard work, reap ____" follows the proverbial structure similar to "you reap what you sow." The most logical and appropriate completion is "success," as hard work typically leads to success.

questionsEn.q: Read the passage and answer the questions: "Normal science, the activity in which most scientists inevitably spend almost all their time, is based on the assumption that the scientific community knows what the world is like. Scientists take great pains to defend that assumption, often restricting their vision to the phenomena that the existing paradigm has defined as relevant. When research proceeds in this fashion, findings tend to be incremental, reinforcing the established framework rather than challenging it. Yet, over time, anomalies-empirical observations that cannot be explained within the current paradigm-accumulate. Initially, these anomalies are dismissed as errors or as problems to be solved within the existing theoretical structure. However, as these anomalies grow in number and significance, they begin to erode confidence in the prevailing paradigm. The resolution of such crises is not a straightforward process of falsification, as Popper might suggest, but rather a transformation in the very way scientists see the world. Scientific revolutions occur when a new paradigm emerges-one that is not merely an extension of the old but a fundamental reconceptualization of reality. This shift is not purely logical or empirical; it involves a radical change in perspective, akin to a gestalt switch. The Copernican Revolution, for example, did not merely adjust astronomical calculations; it redefined the very framework through which celestial motion was understood. Similarly, Einstein's theory of relativity did not just modify Newtonian mechanics but replaced its foundational assumptions about space and time. What type of clause is used in the sentence: "Yet, over time, anomalies that cannot be explained within the current paradigm accumulate."
questionsEn.s: Correct option (c) Relative clause
questionsEn.source: Selection Post Phase XIII (Graduate), 29 Jul 2025, Shift 3

questionsEn.q: Which of the following is an example of onomatopoeia?
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is: Murmur.

Key Points

• The word "Murmur" is an example of onomatopoeia, which refers to words that imitate or resemble the sound they describe. (मर्मराहट)

• Example: The gentle murmur of the stream was soothing to the ears.

• Onomatopoeia helps create a vivid sensory experience by mimicking actual sounds. (ध्वनि अनुकरण)

• Example: Words like "buzz," "splash," and "whisper" are other examples of onomatopoeia.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Murmur.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

• Silence (चुप्पी): The absence of sound or noise.

• Example: The room was filled with an eerie silence after the announcement.

• Balloon (गुब्बारा): An inflatable object typically made of rubber.

• Example: The children played joyfully with colorful balloons at the party.

• Horrible (भयानक): Something extremely unpleasant or shocking.

• Example: The horrible storm caused widespread destruction in the town.

Q: Which of the following is an example of onomatopoeia?

The correct answer is: Murmur.

questionsEn.q: Which figure of speech is used in "The old lady wept a river of tears"?
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is Option 2.

Key Points

• The sentence "The old lady wept a river of tears" uses an exaggerated expression to emphasize the extent of her sadness.

• This is an example of Hyperbole, a figure of speech that uses deliberate and obvious exaggeration for dramatic effect.

• Hyperbole is often used to evoke strong feelings or create a vivid mental image.

• In this case, the expression "a river of tears" is not literal but exaggerates the old lady’s intense emotions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

The sentence does not employ euphemism, alliteration, or anticlimax, as these figures of speech serve different purposes. Instead, the vivid exaggeration aligns with hyperbole.

Additional Information

• Euphemism: A mild or indirect word/expression used to substitute something harsh or blunt (e.g., "passed away" for "died").

• Alliteration: The repetition of the same initial consonant sound in closely connected words (e.g., "She sells seashells by the seashore").

• Anticlimax: A sudden transition from a significant idea to a trivial one for humorous or ironic effect.

• Hyperbole: An exaggerated statement not meant to be taken literally, often used for emphasis or effect.

questionsEn.q: The figure of speech used in "I wandered lonely as a cloud..."?
questionsEn.s:
The correct answer is Option 2.

Key Points

• The line "I wandered lonely as a cloud" is an example of a simile.

• A simile is a figure of speech that compares two different things using "like" or "as."

• In this case, the poet compares his wandering to a lonely cloud, emphasizing the sense of isolation and movement.

• This line is from William Wordsworth's poem "Daffodils," which explores themes of nature, beauty, and reflection.

• Wordsworth often used vivid imagery and figures of speech to evoke emotions and connect readers to the natural world.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Hyperbole: An exaggerated statement or claim not meant to be taken literally.

• Metaphor: A figure of speech that directly compares two unlike things without using "like" or "as."

• Personification: Assigning human traits or qualities to non-human entities or objects.

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Puissant
questionsEn.s:
Puissant - शक्तिशाली (Having great power or influence)
Feeble - कमज़ोर (Lacking physical strength or character)
Robust - मज़बूत (Strong and healthy in constitution)
Powerful - ताकतवर (Having great power or influence)
Strong - बलवान (Possessing physical power)


Hence, 'Feeble' is the most suitable antonym for 'Puissant'.
oa:
This term describes a person or thing that lacks physical strength, energy, or effectiveness. It stands as the direct opposite of being powerful or influential, thus fulfilling the antonym requirement for the given word.
Synonyms: Weak (कमज़ोर), Fragile (नाज़ुक), Infirm (अशक्त).
Antonyms: Robust (मज़बूत), Powerful (शक्तिशाली), Vigorous (जोशपूर्ण).

This word refers to someone who is strong, healthy, and vigorous in constitution. Since it conveys a sense of great power and durability, it acts more as a synonym than an opposite to the given word.
Synonyms: Sturdy (हट्टा-कट्टा), Healthy (स्वस्थ), Resilient (लचीला/मज़बूत).
Antonyms: Frail (दुर्बल), Weak (कमज़ोर), Delicate (नाज़ुक).

This word signifies having great power, prestige, or influence. It is a direct synonym of the question word and describes the same quality of being mighty or potent.
Synonyms: Mighty (बलवान), Potent (असरदार), Dominant (प्रभावी).
Antonyms: Powerless (शक्तिहीन), Weak (निर्बल), Impotent (अक्षम).

This describes having the power to move heavy weights or perform other physically demanding tasks. It focuses on physical capability and serves as a synonymous idea rather than a contrasting one.
Synonyms: Tough (कठोर), Muscular (मांसपेशीयुक्त), Solid (ठोस).
Antonyms: Feeble (शक्तिहीन), Tiny (छोटा), Fragile (कमज़ोर).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Erudite
questionsEn.s:
Erudite - विद्वान (Having or showing great knowledge or learning)
Scholarly - पंडित (Involving or relating to serious academic study)
Uninformed - अज्ञानी (Lacking knowledge or awareness)
Learned - ज्ञानी (Having acquired much knowledge through study)
Intellectual - बौद्धिक (Possessing a high capacity for self-conscious thought)


Hence, 'Uninformed' is the most suitable antonym for 'Erudite'.
oa:
This word relates to a person who is devoted to study and possesses deep academic knowledge. It reflects a similar meaning to the given word and cannot be considered an antonym.
Synonyms: Academic (शैक्षिक), Learned (शिक्षित), Intellectual (बौद्धिक).
Antonyms: Ignorant (अनपढ़), Illiterate (निरक्षर), Uneducated (अशिक्षित).

This word describes a person who lacks knowledge, awareness, or information about specific facts or subjects. It is the most appropriate opposite for a word that signifies being deeply learned and knowledgeable.
Synonyms: Ignorant (अज्ञानी), Unaware (अनभिज्ञ), Oblivious (बेखबर).
Antonyms: Enlightened (प्रबुद्ध), Knowledgeable (जानकार), Educated (शिक्षित).

This refers to someone who has acquired much knowledge through study and experience. As it is a direct synonym for the given word, it does not fit the requirement of an opposite.
Synonyms: Erudite (विद्वान), Wise (बुद्धिमान), Lettered (साक्षर).
Antonyms: Foolish (मूर्ख), Unlearned (अशिक्षित), Ignorant (अज्ञानी).

This relates to a person's ability to think in a logical way and understand difficult ideas. It describes a quality of the mind similar to being erudite and thus acts as a synonym.
Synonyms: Rational (तार्किक), Cerebral (दिमागी), Thoughtful (विचारशील).
Antonyms: Stupid (मूर्ख), Brainless (बुद्धिहीन), Irrational (अतार्किक).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Encomium
questionsEn.s:
Encomium - गुणगान (A speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly)
Panegyric - प्रशंसात्मक (A public speech or text in high praise of someone)
Praise - सराहना (Expression of approval or admiration)
Castigation - कड़ी आलोचना (Severe criticism or punishment)
Tribute - श्रद्धांजलि (An act or statement showing respect or gratitude)


Hence, 'Castigation' is the most suitable antonym for 'Encomium'.
oa:
This word refers to a public speech or published text delivered in high praise of someone or something. It shares the same positive connotation as the given word and is therefore a synonym.
Synonyms: Eulogy (प्रशंसा भाषण), Accolade (सम्मान), Paean (विजय गीत).
Antonyms: Criticism (आलोचना), Condemnation (निंदा), Tirade (कड़ी निंदा).

This is a common term for the expression of approval or admiration for someone's achievements or qualities. Since it is the core meaning of the given word, it cannot be the antonym.
Synonyms: Admiration (प्रशंसा), Commendation (सराहना), Applause (वाहवाही).
Antonyms: Insult (अपमान), Blame (दोष), Scolding (डांट).

This word refers to the act of rebuking or criticizing someone severely. It represents a harsh negative judgment, making it the direct opposite of a formal expression of high praise.
Synonyms: Reprimand (फटकार), Censure (निंदा), Berating (डांटना).
Antonyms: Approval (स्वीकृति), Praise (तारीफ़), Compliment (प्रशंसा).

This is an act, statement, or gift that is intended to show gratitude, respect, or admiration. It is a form of praise, which means it aligns with the meaning of the given word rather than opposing it.
Synonyms: Respect (सम्मान), Homage (श्रद्धांजलि), Recognition (मान्यता).
Antonyms: Disrespect (अनादर), Contempt (तिरस्कार), Criticism (आलोचना).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Evanescent
questionsEn.s:
Evanescent - क्षणभंगुर (Passing out of sight, memory, or existence quickly)
Ephemeral - अल्पकालिक (Lasting for a very short time)
Transient - अस्थायी (Lasting only for a short time)
Enduring - टिकाऊ (Lasting over a period of time; durable)
Fleeting - क्षणिक (Lasting for a very short time)


Hence, 'Enduring' is the most suitable antonym for 'Evanescent'.
oa:
This word describes something that lasts for a very short time. Since it perfectly matches the meaning of the given word, it serves as a synonym and not an antonym.
Synonyms: Transitory (क्षणिक), Short-lived (अल्पकालिक), Brief (संक्षिप्त).
Antonyms: Permanent (स्थायी), Eternal (अनंत), Everlasting (शाश्वत).

This refers to staying or lasting for only a short time before passing away. It captures the essence of being evanescent, making it a synonym.
Synonyms: Passing (गुज़रता हुआ), Temporary (अस्थायी), Fugitive (क्षणभंगुर).
Antonyms: Constant (निरंतर), Persistent (दृढ़), Enduring (चिरस्थायी).

This word describes something that lasts for a long time or remains in existence without fading. It is the direct opposite of being short-lived or vanishing quickly.
Synonyms: Lasting (टिकाऊ), Permanent (स्थायी), Abiding (अटल).
Antonyms: Fleeting (क्षणिक), Temporary (अस्थायी), Short-lived (अल्पकालिक).

This refers to something that passes very quickly or is of very short duration. It is contextually identical to being evanescent and therefore acts as a synonym.
Synonyms: Momentary (क्षणिक), Vanishing (गायब होता हुआ), Brief (लघु).
Antonyms: Perpetual (लगातार), Long-term (दीर्घकालिक), Infinite (असीम).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Lachrymose
questionsEn.s:
Lachrymose - अश्रुपूर्ण (Inducing tears; tearful)
Tearful - रोने वाला (Crying or inclined to cry)
Mournful - शोकाकुल (Feeling or expressing sadness, regret, or grief)
Weepy - रोनी सूरत (Inclined to weep; tearful)
Jovial - उल्लासपूर्ण (Cheerful and friendly)


Hence, 'Jovial' is the most suitable antonym for 'Lachrymose'.
oa:
This word describes a person who is crying or inclined to cry easily. It is the primary characteristic of being lachrymose and serves as a direct synonym.
Synonyms: Weepy (रोने वाला), Sobbing (सिसकते हुए), Crying (रोता हुआ).
Antonyms: Happy (खुश), Cheerful (हंसमुख), Joyful (आनंदित).

This refers to expressing or feeling deep sadness, usually associated with grief or loss. It aligns with the sorrowful nature of the given word and is thus a synonym.
Synonyms: Sorrowful (शोकाकुल), Melancholy (उदास), Doleful (दुखद).
Antonyms: Jubilant (प्रफुल्लित), Excited (उत्साहित), Bright (प्रसन्न).

This is an informal term for someone who is inclined to weep or is showing signs of having cried. It is essentially a synonym for the given word.
Synonyms: Emotional (भावुक), Sad (दुखी), Teary (अश्रुपूर्ण).
Antonyms: Unmoved (अविचलित), Stoic (उदासीन), Hearty (प्रसन्न).

This word describes a person who is very cheerful, friendly, and full of high spirits. It is the perfect opposite of being tearful or mournful.
Synonyms: Jolly (हंसमुख), Merry (खुशहाल), Mirthful (आनंदपूर्ण).
Antonyms: Gloomy (उदासीन), Depressed (उदास), Miserable (अति दुखी).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Cacophony
questionsEn.s:
Cacophony - कोलाहल (A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds)
Noise - शोर (A sound, especially one that is loud or unpleasant)
Harmony - सामंजस्य (A pleasing arrangement or combination of sounds)
Dissonance - बेसुरापन (Lack of harmony among musical notes)
Clamor - हंगामा (A loud and confused noise)


Hence, 'Harmony' is the most suitable antonym for 'Cacophony'.
oa:
This refers to a sound, especially one that is loud, unpleasant, or that causes disturbance. It describes the very essence of the given word and is therefore a synonym.
Synonyms: Racket (शोर-शराबा), Din (कोलाहल), Hubbub (हल्ला).
Antonyms: Silence (शांति), Quiet (शांति), Stillness (सन्नाटा).

This word refers to the quality of forming a pleasing and consistent whole, especially in terms of sound or music. It is the direct opposite of a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds.
Synonyms: Accord (तालमेल), Euphony (मधुर ध्वनि), Agreement (सहमति).
Antonyms: Discord (कलह), Conflict (विवाद), Dissonance (असंगति).

This word refers to a lack of harmony among musical notes or a tension between elements. It is functionally synonymous with the given word as it implies unpleasant sound.
Synonyms: Discordance (बेसुरापन), Conflict (मतभेद), Harshness (कर्कशता).
Antonyms: Consonance (अनुरूपता), Agreement (समझौता), Melodiousness (मधुरता).

This refers to a loud and confused noise, especially that of people shouting vehemently. It reinforces the idea of loud, unorganized sound, making it a synonym.
Synonyms: Outcry (चिल्लाहट), Uproar (हंगामा), Commotion (हलचल).
Antonyms: Peace (शांति), Calm (स्थिरता), Silence (चुप्पी).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Subterfuge
questionsEn.s:
Subterfuge - छल (Deceit used in order to achieve one's goal)
Chicanery - वाक्छल (The use of trickery to achieve a purpose)
Candor - स्पष्टवादिता (The quality of being open and honest; frankness)
Trickery - धोखेबाज़ी (The practice of deception)
Deception - छल (The act of deceiving someone)


Hence, 'Candor' is the most suitable antonym for 'Subterfuge'.
oa:
This word refers to the use of trickery or sophistry to achieve a political, financial, or legal purpose. It is a synonym that emphasizes deceitful behavior.
Synonyms: Deception (धोखा), Duplicity (छल-कपट), Guile (धूर्तता).
Antonyms: Honesty (ईमानदारी), Integrity (अखंडता), Truthfulness (सच्चाई).

This word refers to the quality of being open, honest, and sincere in expression. It is the direct opposite of using tricks or deceit to achieve a goal.
Synonyms: Frankness (स्पष्टवादिता), Openness (खुलापन), Sincerity (सच्चाई).
Antonyms: Deceit (छल), Evasion (टाल-मटोल), Guile (धूर्तता).

This is the practice of using deceptive methods to cheat or outwit someone. Since the given word involves deceit, this word acts as a near-perfect synonym.
Synonyms: Artifice (चालाकी), Fraud (ज़ालसाजी), Cunning (चतुराई).
Antonyms: Fairness (निष्पक्षता), Honesty (ईमानदारी), Directness (सीधापन).

This refers to the act of causing someone to believe something that is not true, typically to gain some advantage. It is a synonym for the deceptive nature of subterfuge.
Synonyms: Bluff (धोखा), Treachery (विश्वासघात), Hoax (छलावा).
Antonyms: Reality (वास्तविकता), Truth (सत्य), Authenticity (प्रमाणिकता).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Taciturn
questionsEn.s:
Taciturn - अल्पभाषी (Reserved or uncommunicative in speech)
Reserved - संकोची (Slow to reveal emotions or opinions)
Loquacious - बातूनी (Tending to talk a great deal; talkative)
Quiet - शांत (Making little or no noise)
Uncommunicative - मौनी (Not inclined to talk or give information)


Hence, 'Loquacious' is the most suitable antonym for 'Taciturn'.
oa:
This word describes a person who does not reveal their thoughts or feelings readily. It is very close in meaning to being taciturn and thus serves as a synonym.
Synonyms: Reticent (अल्पभाषी), Shy (शर्मीला), Uncommunicative (मितभाषी).
Antonyms: Outgoing (मिलनसार), Sociable (सामाजिक), Extroverted (बहिर्मुखी).

This word describes someone who tends to talk a great deal or is very talkative. It is the perfect antonym for someone who habitually says very little.
Synonyms: Garrulous (बातूनी), Voluble (वाचाल), Chatty (गप्पी).
Antonyms: Silent (मौन), Quiet (शांत), Reticent (कम बोलने वाला).

This refers to someone who makes little or no noise or someone who speaks very little. It is a synonymous concept to the given word and doesn't provide an opposite relationship.
Synonyms: Still (स्थिर), Soft (धीमा), Peaceful (शांत).
Antonyms: Loud (ज़ोरदार), Noisy (शोर वाला), Rowdy (उपद्रवी).

This describes a person who is unwilling to talk or provide information. It is a direct synonym for the behavior of a taciturn individual.
Synonyms: Secretive (गुप्त), Tight-lipped (मौन), Silent (खामोश).
Antonyms: Frank (स्पष्ट), Open (खुला), Communicative (मिलनसार).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Extirpate
questionsEn.s:
Extirpate - समूल नष्ट करना (Root out and destroy completely)
Exterminate - जड़ से मिटाना (Destroy completely; kill a large group)
Establish - स्थापित करना (Set up on a firm or permanent basis)
Uproot - उखाड़ फेंकना (Pull up by the roots; displace)
Eradicate - उन्मूलन करना (Destroy completely; put an end to)


Hence, 'Establish' is the most suitable antonym for 'Extirpate'.
oa:
This word refers to the act of destroying completely, usually applied to a whole group of people or animals. It is a synonym as it involves total destruction.
Synonyms: Annihilate (मिटा देना), Eradicate (उन्मूलन), Abolish (समाप्त करना).
Antonyms: Create (बनाना), Preserve (संरक्षित करना), Protect (रक्षा करना).

This word means to set up, create, or initiate something on a firm or permanent basis. It is the direct opposite of completely destroying or uprooting something.
Synonyms: Found (नींव रखना), Institute (संस्थापित करना), Settle (बसाना).
Antonyms: Destroy (नष्ट करना), Uproot (उखाड़ना), Demolish (ध्वस्त करना).

This means to pull something, especially a plant, out of the ground with its roots. It is the literal and figurative meaning of extirpating, making it a synonym.
Synonyms: Displace (विस्थापित करना), Remove (हटाना), Extract (निकालना).
Antonyms: Plant (पौधा लगाना), Embed (स्थापित करना), Settle (बसाना).

This refers to getting rid of something completely or destroying the very root of a problem. It is a strong synonym for the given word.
Synonyms: Eliminate (निकाल देना), Expunge (मिटा देना), Liquidate (समाप्त करना).
Antonyms: Promote (बढ़ावा देना), Support (सहायता करना), Foster (पालना-पोसना).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Placatory
questionsEn.s:
Placatory - शांतिदायक (Intended to make someone less angry; pacifying)
Pacifying - शांत करनेवाला (Bringing peace or calm)
Soothing - सुखदायक (Having a gently calming effect)
Aggravating - उत्तेजक (Making a problem or situation worse)
Conciliatory - मिलाप करानेवाला (Intended to placate or pacify)


Hence, 'Aggravating' is the most suitable antonym for 'Placatory'.
oa:
This word describes an action intended to calm someone down and reduce their anger or excitement. It is a direct synonym for the given word.
Synonyms: Calming (शांत करने वाला), Peacemaking (शांतिदूत), Gentle (कोमल).
Antonyms: Irritating (चिढ़ाने वाला), Provoking (उकसाने वाला), Violent (हिंसक).

This refers to something that has a gently calming effect or reduces pain and discomfort. It carries a similar positive connotation to being placatory.
Synonyms: Relaxing (आरामदायक), Comforting (दिलासा देने वाला), Balmy (सुखद).
Antonyms: Agitating (परेशान करने वाला), Harsh (कठोर), Intense (तीव्र).
