This term refers to being courteous and polite, especially relating to ordinary citizens. It is a synonym for polite and therefore does not satisfy the requirement for an opposite.
Synonyms: Respectful (आदरपूर्ण), Mannerly (शिष्ट), Urbane (सभ्य).
Antonyms: Rude (असभ्य), Uncivil (असभ्य), Barbarian (बर्बर).

This word describes behavior that is socially acceptable, honest, and fair. While positive, it describes a general standard of goodness rather than the specific trait of politeness.
Synonyms: Proper (उचित), Honorable (सम्माननीय), Modest (विनम्र).
Antonyms: Indecent (अश्लील), Immoral (अनैतिक), Dishonest (बेईमान).

This adjective refers to a person who is not affected by alcohol or someone who is serious and sensible. It relates to clarity of mind rather than social manners.
Synonyms: Sensible (समझदार), Grave (गंभीर), Abstemious (संयमी).
Antonyms: Drunk (नशे में), Frivolous (छिछोरा), Excited (उत्तेजित).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Under
questionsEn.s:
Under - नीचे (Below the surface of something)
Over - ऊपर (Above or higher than something)
Sink - डूबना (To go down under a surface)
Behind - पीछे (At the back of something)
Beneath - नीचे / तले (Directly under something)
oa:
This preposition refers to being at a higher level than something or covering it. It is the direct spatial opposite of under, which means below a surface.
Synonyms: Above (ऊपर), Atop (शिखर पर), Overhead (सिर के ऊपर).
Antonyms: Under (नीचे), Below (नीचे), Beneath (तले).

This verb means to go down or submerge below the surface of a liquid. While it involves downward movement, it is an action and not a prepositional opposite.
Synonyms: Submerge (डूबना), Descend (नीचे जाना), Drown (डूब मरना).
Antonyms: Float (तैरना), Rise (उठना), Surface (सतह पर आना).

This term indicates being at the back of something. It describes a different spatial relationship (front/back) rather than the vertical relationship (up/down).
Synonyms: Rear (पीछे), Abaft (पीछे), Following (पीछे).
Antonyms: Front (सामने), Ahead (आगे), Before (सामने).

This word is a preposition meaning below the surface of something. It is a synonym for under and therefore cannot be the required antonym.
Synonyms: Under (नीचे), Below (नीचे), Underneath (तले).
Antonyms: Over (ऊपर), Above (ऊपर), Aloft (ऊपर).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Servile
questionsEn.s:
Servile - दब्बू / चापलूस (Excessively willing to please or obey others)
Arrogant - अहंकारी (Having an exaggerated sense of importance)
Sheepish - लज्जित / संकोची (Showing embarrassment from shame)
Bickering - झगड़ा / तकरार (Engaging in petty arguments)
Cunning - चालाक / धूर्त (Skillful in achieving ends by deceit)
oa:
This word refers to having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities. It stands as the opposite of servile, which describes an excessive willingness to obey others.
Synonyms: Haughty (अहंकारी), Conceited (घमंडी), Proud (अभिमानी).
Antonyms: Servile (दब्बू), Humble (विनम्र), Modest (विनीत).

This term describes a person showing embarrassment from shame or a lack of self-confidence. It aligns more with a lack of assertion rather than being an opposite of servility.
Synonyms: Embarrassed (लज्जित), Ashamed (शर्मिंदा), Timid (डरपोक).
Antonyms: Bold (साहसी), Confident (आत्मविश्वासी), Shameless (बेशर्म).

This word refers to engaging in petty, often prolonged, arguments or quarrels. It describes a type of conflict rather than a personality trait related to obedience.
Synonyms: Quarreling (झगड़ा), Squabbling (तकरार), Arguing (बहस).
Antonyms: Agreeing (सहमत), Harmony (सामंजस्य), Concurring (एकमत).

This adjective describes someone having or showing skill in achieving one's ends by deceit or evasion. It focuses on cleverness and trickery rather than subservience.
Synonyms: Crafty (चालाक), Shrewd (चतुर), Sly (धूर्त).
Antonyms: Naive (भोला), Honest (ईमानदार), Guileless (निष्कपट).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Frugal
questionsEn.s:
Frugal - मितव्ययी (Economical or thrifty with money)
Prices - कीमतें (Amount of money required for purchase)
Accommodation - आवास (A place where someone lives or stays)
Present - वर्तमान (Existing or occurring now)
Extravagant - फिजूलखर्च (Spending money without restraint)
oa:
This noun refers to the amount of money expected, required, or given in payment for something. It does not describe a lifestyle or habit of spending.
Synonyms: Costs (लागत), Rates (दर), Charges (कीमत).
Antonyms: Free (मुफ्त), Discount (छूट), Worthless (बेकार).

This term refers to a room, group of rooms, or building in which someone may live or stay. It focuses on a physical place rather than financial behavior.
Synonyms: Housing (आवास), Lodging (निवास), Shelter (शरण).
Antonyms: Eviction (बेदखली), Homelessness (बेघर), Displacement (विस्थापन).

This word can mean existing or occurring now, or a gift. Neither meaning serves as a direct antonym for being economical with resources.
Synonyms: Current (वर्तमान), Existing (मौजूद), Gift (उपहार).
Antonyms: Past (अतीत), Future (भविष्य), Absent (अनुपस्थित).

This adjective describes someone who spends money without restraint or is wasteful. It is the direct antonym of frugal, which implies being thrifty and economical.
Synonyms: Lavish (फिजूलखर्च), Wasteful (अपव्ययी), Prodigal (अतिव्ययी).
Antonyms: Frugal (मितव्ययी), Thrifty (किफायती), Stingy (कंजूस).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Lonely
questionsEn.s:
Lonely - अकेला / सुनसान (Without company or solitary)
Crowded - भीड़भाड़ वाला (Filled with many people)
Isolated - अलग-थलग (Separated from others)
Empty - खाली (Having nothing inside)
Remote - दूरदराज (Situated far away)
oa:
This word describes a place or area filled with a large number of people or things. It is the direct opposite of lonely, which implies being solitary or without company.
Synonyms: Packed (ठसाठस), Swarming (भीड़ भरा), Congested (संकुल).
Antonyms: Lonely (अकेला), Deserted (वीरान), Empty (खाली).

This term refers to being separated from others or placed alone. It is a synonym for lonely and therefore cannot be the required opposite.
Synonyms: Remote (दूरस्थ), Solitary (एकाकी), Secluded (सुनसान).
Antonyms: Accessible (सुलभ), Central (केंद्रीय), Public (सार्वजनिक).

This adjective describes something containing nothing; not filled or occupied. While it implies lack of presence, it doesn't specifically contrast the "social" aspect of being lonely.
Synonyms: Vacant (खाली), Bare (नग्न), Hollow (खोखला).
Antonyms: Full (भरा हुआ), Occupied (भरा), Crowded (भीड़युक्त).

This word refers to a place situated far from the main centers of population; distant. It focuses on distance rather than the density of people.
Synonyms: Distant (दूर), Faraway (दूरस्थ), Isolated (अलग).
Antonyms: Near (पास), Close (निकट), Nearby (नज़दीक).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Seldom
questionsEn.s:
Seldom - शायद ही कभी (Rarely or not often)
Hardly - मुश्किल से (Almost not)
Rarely - विरले ही (Not often)
Frequently - अक्सर / बार-बार (Happening many times)
Occasionally - कभी-कभी (Happening from time to time)
oa:
This adverb means only just or almost not. It serves as a synonym for seldom and therefore does not satisfy the requirement for an opposite relationship.
Synonyms: Barely (मुश्किल से), Scarcely (कदाचित), Rarely (शायद ही).
Antonyms: Often (अक्सर), Frequently (बार-बार), Always (हमेशा).

This word means not often or infrequently. It is a direct synonym of seldom and cannot be used as its antonym.
Synonyms: Seldom (शायद ही कभी), Scarcely (विरले ही), Occasionally (कभी-कभार).
Antonyms: Regularly (नियमित), Frequently (बार-बार), Usually (आमतौर पर).

This word refers to something happening often or at short intervals. it is the correct antonym for seldom, which characterizes things that happen very rarely.
Synonyms: Often (अक्सर), Regularly (नियमित रूप से), Repeatedly (बार-बार).
Antonyms: Seldom (कदाचित), Rarely (दुर्लभ), Infrequently (कभी-कभार).

This term means happening from time to time or now and then. While more frequent than "never," it does not represent the strong contrast that "frequently" provides.
Synonyms: Sometimes (कभी-कभी), Sporadically (अनियमित रूप से), Periodically (समय-समय पर).
Antonyms: Constantly (निरंतर), Always (हमेशा), Frequently (बार-बार).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Disgrace
questionsEn.s:
Disgrace - अपमान / बदनामी (Loss of reputation or respect)
Suspicion - संदेह (A feeling of doubt or mistrust)
Shame - शर्म (A feeling of humiliation)
Discord - कलह / विवाद (Disagreement between people)
Honour - सम्मान / आदर (High respect or great esteem)
oa:
This noun refers to a feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true, or a feeling of mistrust. It deals with doubt rather than reputation.
Synonyms: Doubt (संदेह), Mistrust (अविश्वास), Skepticism (संशय).
Antonyms: Trust (विश्वास), Certainty (निश्चितता), Faith (आस्था).

This word describes a painful feeling of humiliation caused by the consciousness of wrong behavior. It is a synonym of disgrace and thus not the opposite.
Synonyms: Humiliation (अपमान), Guilt (अपराधबोध), Ignominy (बदनामी).
Antonyms: Pride (गर्व), Honor (सम्मान), Dignity (गरिमा).

This term refers to disagreement or lack of harmony between people or things. It focuses on conflict within a group rather than the standing of an individual.
Synonyms: Strife (कलह), Conflict (विवाद), Friction (अनबन).
Antonyms: Harmony (सामंजस्य), Accord (सहमति), Peace (शांति).

This word means high respect or great esteem. It is the direct opposite of disgrace, which signifies a loss of reputation or respect.
Synonyms: Respect (आदर), Prestige (प्रतिष्ठा), Glory (महिमा).
Antonyms: Disgrace (अपमान), Shame (शर्म), Contempt (तिरस्कार).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Divergence
questionsEn.s:
Divergence - अलगाव / विचलन (The act of moving away or becoming different)
Convergence - मिलन / संगम (The act of coming together)
Existence - अस्तित्व (The state of having objective reality)
Resilience - लचीलापन (The capacity to recover quickly)
Transience - क्षणभंगुरता (The state of lasting for a short time)
oa:
This term refers to the process of coming together from different directions so as eventually to meet. it is the direct opposite of divergence, which means moving away or becoming different.
Synonyms: Merging (मिलन), Union (संगम), Meeting (मिलाप).
Antonyms: Divergence (अलगाव), Separation (विभाजन), Deviation (विचल).

This noun refers to the fact or state of living or having objective reality. It deals with the being of something rather than the direction of its path.
Synonyms: Being (अस्तित्व), Presence (उपस्थिति), Survival (उत्तरजीविता).
Antonyms: Nonexistence (गैर-अस्तित्व), Death (मृत्यु), Absence (अनुपस्थिति).

This word describes the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness. It refers to the ability to bounce back rather than a spatial or conceptual split.
Synonyms: Flexibility (लचीलापन), Toughness (कठोरता), Durability (स्थायित्व).
Antonyms: Fragility (भंगुरता), Weakness (कमज़ोरी), Rigidity (कठोरता).

This term refers to the state or fact of lasting only for a short time; impermanence. It deals with duration rather than the act of branching out.
Synonyms: Ephemerality (क्षणभंगुरता), Impermanence (अस्थिरता), Shortness (अल्पता).
Antonyms: Permanence (स्थायित्व), Longevity (दीर्घायु), Eternity (अनंतकाल).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Blooming
questionsEn.s:
Blooming - खिलना / प्रफुल्लित (Developing successful qualities)
Flourishing - फलना-फूलना (Developing in a healthy way)
Sprouting - अंकुरित होना (Beginning to grow)
Growing - बढ़ना (Increasing in size or complexity)
Fading - मुरझाना / फीका पड़ना (Losing brightness or strength)
oa:
This word means growing or developing in a healthy or vigorous way. It serves as a synonym for blooming and therefore is not an opposite.
Synonyms: Thriving (फलना-फूलना), Prospering (समृद्ध), Burgeoning (बढ़ना).
Antonyms: Withered (मुरझाया), Failing (असफल), Declining (गिरता हुआ).

This term refers to starting to grow or developing. It describes the early stages of a life cycle, much like blooming, rather than its decline.
Synonyms: Germinating (अंकुरित), Budding (पल्लवित), Emerging (उभरता).
Antonyms: Dying (मरना), Shrinking (सिकुड़ना), Decaying (सड़ना).

This is a general term for increasing in size or developing. As blooming is a form of growth, this word cannot be the required antonym.
Synonyms: Developing (विकासशील), Increasing (बढ़ता हुआ), Expanding (फैलता).
Antonyms: Shrinking (सिकुड़ना), Diminishing (घटता), Waning (क्षीण).

This term refers to losing brightness, color, or strength. It acts as the direct opposite of blooming, which describes something reaching its peak or developing successful qualities.
Synonyms: Withering (मुरझाना), Declining (ढलना), Dimming (धुंधला होना).
Antonyms: Blooming (खिलना), Shining (चमकना), Flourishing (पनपना).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Heavy
questionsEn.s:
Heavy - भारी (Having great weight)
Big - बड़ा (Large in size or extent)
Massive - विशाल / भारी (Large and heavy)
Light - हल्का (Having little weight)
Large - बड़ा (Of considerable size)
oa:
This adjective refers to something that is large in size or extent. While large things can be heavy, "big" focuses on dimension rather than weight.
Synonyms: Large (बड़ा), Huge (विशाल), Massive (विराट).
Antonyms: Small (छोटा), Little (नन्हा), Tiny (सूक्ष्म).

This word describes something that is exceptionally large and heavy. Since it includes the idea of being heavy, it is a synonym rather than an opposite.
Synonyms: Gigantic (विशालकाय), Colossal (प्रचंड), Immense (अत्यधिक).
Antonyms: Light (हल्का), Tiny (छोटा), Minute (सूक्ष्म).

This word refers to something having little weight or being easy to lift. It is the direct and most accurate antonym for the word heavy.
Synonyms: Weightless (भारहीन), Airy (हल्का), Featherweight (बहुत हल्का).
Antonyms: Heavy (भारी), Weighty (वजनी), Hefty (भारी-भरकम).

This term describes something of considerable size or capacity. Like "big," it addresses physical dimensions rather than the mass or gravity of an object.
Synonyms: Great (महान), Sizable (काफी बड़ा), Extensive (विस्तृत).
Antonyms: Small (छोटा), Meager (अल्प), Petty (तुच्छ).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Plight
questionsEn.s:
Plight - दुर्दशा / कठिन अवस्था (A difficult or unfortunate situation)
Predicament - कठिन परिस्थिति (A difficult or embarrassing situation)
Dilemma - दुविधा (A difficult choice between two options)
Quandary - व्याकुलता (A state of uncertainty in a difficult situation)
Advantage - फायदा / लाभ (A favorable or beneficial circumstance)
oa:
This word describes a difficult, unpleasant, or embarrassing situation. It is a direct synonym for plight and therefore does not provide an opposite meaning.
Synonyms: Dilemma (दुविधा), Quagmire (दलदल), Crisis (संकट).
Antonyms: Resolution (समाधान), Ease (आराम), Comfort (सुकून).

This term refers to a situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives. It characterizes a difficult state, similar to plight.
Synonyms: Quandary (व्याकुलता), Conflict (संघर्ष), Perplexity (उलझन).
Antonyms: Solution (समाधान), Certainty (निश्चितता), Agreement (सहमति).

This word describes a state of perplexity or uncertainty over what to do in a difficult situation. It is synonymous with the distress implied by plight.
Synonyms: Confusion (भ्रम), Muddle (अव्यवस्था), Predicament (कठिन परिस्थिति).
Antonyms: Clarity (स्पष्टता), Decision (निर्णय), Confidence (विश्वास).

This noun refers to a favorable or beneficial circumstance or a condition that puts one in a superior position. It is the opposite of the unfortunate state defined by plight.
Synonyms: Benefit (लाभ), Boon (वरदान), Privilege (विशेषाधिकार).
Antonyms: Plight (दुर्दशा), Disadvantage (हानि), Handicap (बाधा).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Calm down
questionsEn.s:
Calm down - शांत होना (To become quiet or peaceful)
Understand - समझना (To perceive the meaning of)
Agitate - परेशान / उत्तेजित करना (To make someone feel anxious or troubled)
Question - प्रश्न करना (To ask for information)
Dissipate - गायब होना / बिखेरना (To disperse or disappear)
oa:
This verb means to perceive the intended meaning of something. It is a cognitive process that bears no relationship to the emotional state of being calm or agitated.
Synonyms: Comprehend (समझना), Grasp (पकड़ना), Perceive (महसूस करना).
Antonyms: Misinterpret (गलत समझना), Confuse (भ्रमित), Ignore (उपेक्षा).

This word means to make someone feel anxious, troubled, or nervous. it is the direct opposite of calming someone down, which involves restoring peace and quiet.
Synonyms: Disturb (परेशान करना), Incite (उकसाना), Provoke (उकसाना).
Antonyms: Calm (शांत), Soothe (शांत करना), Pacify (तसल्ली देना).

This term refers to the act of asking for information or expressing doubt. It does not describe an emotional state and thus cannot be the opposite of calm down.
Synonyms: Query (पूछना), Inquire (पूछताछ), Challenge (चुनौती).
Antonyms: Answer (उत्तर), Accept (स्वीकार), Believe (विश्वास).

This verb means to disperse or disappear, often used in the context of energy or feelings. While it can mean a feeling goes away, it is not a direct behavioral opposite to calming.
Synonyms: Disperse (बिखेरना), Scatter (छितराना), Vanish (गायब होना).
Antonyms: Accumulate (जमा करना), Gather (इकट्ठा), Collect (संग्रह).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Delegate
questionsEn.s:
Delegate - प्रतिनिधि नियुक्त करना (To entrust tasks to others)
Retain - बरकरार रखना (To keep or continue to have)
Appoint - नियुक्त करना (To assign a job to someone)
Nominate - नामांकित करना (To formally suggest for a position)
Depute - प्रतिनिधि बनाना (To authorize as a substitute)
oa:
This verb means to keep or continue to have something. In the context of workload and duties, it is the direct opposite of delegating, which involves entrusting tasks to others.
Synonyms: Keep (बनाए रखना), Maintain (बनाए रखना), Reserve (आरक्षित).
Antonyms: Delegate (प्रतिनिधि नियुक्त), Relinquish (त्यागना), Release (छोड़ना).

This term refers to the act of assigning a job or position to someone. While it involves authority, it does not express the opposite of handing over tasks.
Synonyms: Nominate (नामित), Designate (निर्धारित), Choose (चुनना).
Antonyms: Dismiss (बर्खास्त), Reject (अस्वीकार), Remove (हटाना).

This verb means to formally suggest someone for a position or an award. It characterizes the selection process rather than the act of holding onto responsibilities.
Synonyms: Propose (प्रस्तावित), Suggest (सुझाव देना), Present (प्रस्तुत करना).
Antonyms: Reject (अस्वीकार), Withdraw (वापस लेना), Ignore (उपेक्षा).

This word means to appoint or authorize someone as a representative or substitute. It is a synonym for delegate rather than being its opposite.
Synonyms: Delegate (सौंपना), Authorize (अधिकृत), Assign (सौंपना).
Antonyms: Retain (रखना), Hold (थामना), Withdraw (वापस लेना).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Innate
questionsEn.s:
Innate - जन्मजात (Existing from birth; natural)
Learned - सीखा हुआ (Acquired by study or experience)
Aquatic - जलीय (Relating to water)
Natural - प्राकृतिक (Existing in nature)
Replete - पूर्ण / भरपूर (Filled or well-supplied)
oa:
This word refers to qualities or skills acquired through study, experience, or being taught. It is the perfect antonym for innate, which describes things existing from birth.
Synonyms: Acquired (अर्जित), Developed (विकसित), Cultivated (संवर्धित).
Antonyms: Innate (जन्मजात), Inborn (सहज), Natural (प्राकृतिक).

This adjective describes something relating to water or living in water. It identifies a physical habitat rather than the origin of an ability or trait.
Synonyms: Marine (जलीय), Watery (जलयुक्त), Oceanic (सामुद्रिक).
Antonyms: Terrestrial (स्थलीय), Land (भूमिगत), Dry (सूखा).

This term describes qualities that exist in or are derived from nature; it often means inborn. Therefore, it is a synonym for innate and not the required opposite.
Synonyms: Native (देशी), Inherent (अंतर्निहित), Instinctive (सहज).
Antonyms: Artificial (कृत्रिम), Unnatural (अप्राकृतिक), Acquired (अर्जित).

This word means filled or well-supplied with something. It describes the fullness of a container or state rather than the origin of a characteristic.
Synonyms: Full (पूर्ण), Abundant (प्रचुर), Loaded (भरा हुआ).
Antonyms: Empty (खाली), Drained (सूखा), Deficient (अपूर्ण).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Transient
questionsEn.s:
Transient - क्षणिक / अस्थायी (Not permanent or lasting)
Boring - उबाऊ (Lacking interest or excitement)
Permanent - स्थायी (Enduring or lasting forever)
Toxic - विषैला (Harmful or poisonous)
Fleeting - क्षणभंगुर (Lasting for a very short time)
oa:
This adjective describes something that lacks interest or excitement. It focuses on the quality of engagement rather than the duration of existence.
Synonyms: Dull (नीरस), Tedious (थकाऊ), Monotonous (एकरस).
Antonyms: Exciting (रोमांचक), Interesting (दिलचस्प), Engaging (मोहक).

This word means lasting or intended to last or remain unchanged indefinitely. It serves as the direct opposite of transient, which refers to things that are short-lived.
Synonyms: Lasting (चिरस्थायी), Eternal (अनंत), Enduring (अडिग).
Antonyms: Transient (क्षणिक), Temporary (अस्थायी), Fleeting (क्षणभंगुर).

This term describes something that is poisonous or harmful. It refers to the physical or emotional danger of a substance rather than its lifespan.
Synonyms: Poisonous (विषैला), Lethal (घातक), Venonous (विषैला).
Antonyms: Harmless (अहानिकर), Safe (सुरक्षित), Healthy (स्वस्थ).

This word describes something that lasts for a very short time. It is a direct synonym for transient and therefore cannot be the required opposite.
Synonyms: Ephemeral (क्षणभंगुर), Brief (संक्षिप्त), Momentary (क्षणिक).
Antonyms: Permanent (स्थायी), Constant (निरंतर), Lasting (टिकाऊ).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Clandestine
questionsEn.s:
Clandestine - गुप्त (Kept secret or done secretively)
Known - ज्ञात (Recognized or familiar)
Private - निजी (Not public or open)
Sneaky - धूर्त (Secretive or dishonest)
Illicit - अवैध (Forbidden by law or rules)
oa:
This word refers to something that is recognized, familiar, or within the scope of public knowledge. It serves as the direct opposite of clandestine, which implies secrecy.
Synonyms: Obvious (स्पष्ट), Public (सार्वजनिक), Familiar (परिचित).
Antonyms: Clandestine (गुप्त), Secret (गुप्त), Hidden (छिपा हुआ).

This adjective describes things intended for or restricted to the use of a particular person or group. It is similar in meaning to clandestine rather than opposite.
Synonyms: Personal (व्यक्तिगत), Confidential (गोपनीय), Exclusive (विशिष्ट).
Antonyms: Public (सार्वजनिक), Open (खुला), Common (साधारण).

This term describes behavior that is secretive or dishonest in a stealthy way. It aligns with the idea of being clandestine rather than providing a contrast.
Synonyms: Sly (धूर्त), Furtive (गुप्त), Underhand (छलपूर्ण).
Antonyms: Honest (ईमानदार), Candid (स्पष्टवादी), Forthright (सीधा).

This word refers to something forbidden by law, rules, or custom. While often associated with secret activities, it describes the legality rather than the visibility of an act.
Synonyms: Illegal (अवैध), Unlawful (गैरकानूनी), Forbidden (वर्जित).
Antonyms: Legal (कानूनी), Lawful (वैध), Allowed (अनुमत).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Absurd
questionsEn.s:
Absurd - बेतुका (Wildly unreasonable or illogical)
Ordinary - साधारण (With no special features)
Odd - विचित्र (Strange or unexpected)
Eerie - डरावना (Strange and frightening)
Realistic - यथार्थवादी (Sensible and practical)
oa:
This word refers to something that is normal or has no special features. While it contrasts with "extraordinary," it doesn't specifically address the "illogical" nature of the word absurd.
Synonyms: Normal (साधारण), Common (सामान्य), Usual (साधारण).
Antonyms: Extraordinary (असाधारण), Unique (अद्वितीय), Rare (दुर्लभ).

This adjective describes something that is different from what is expected; strange. It is often used interchangeably with absurd in certain contexts, so it is not an opposite.
Synonyms: Peculiar (विचित्र), Weird (अजीब), Unusual (असामान्य).
Antonyms: Regular (नियमित), Typical (विशिष्ट), Normal (साधारण).

This term describes something strange and frightening, suggesting a supernatural quality. It characterizes a mood of fear rather than a state of logical reasoning.
Synonyms: Spooky (डरावना), Creepy (भयावह), Sinister (अशुभ).
Antonyms: Comforting (सांत्वना देने वाला), Natural (स्वाभाविक), Familiar (परिचित).

This word means having or showing a sensible and practical idea of what can be achieved. it is the direct opposite of absurd, which implies being wildly unreasonable.
Synonyms: Practical (व्यावहारिक), Rational (तर्कसंगत), Sensible (समझदार).
Antonyms: Absurd (बेतुका), Unrealistic (अवास्तविक), Fanciful (काल्पनिक).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Randomly
questionsEn.s:
Randomly - बेतरतीब ढंग से (Without method or conscious decision)
Casually - बेपरवाही से (In a relaxed or informal manner)
Unwillingly - अनिच्छा पूर्वक (Without wanting to do something)
Systematically - व्यवस्थित ढंग से (Done according to a fixed plan)
Incidentally - संयोग से (By chance or as a minor accompaniment)
oa:
This adverb refers to doing something in a relaxed or unhurried manner without much thought. It aligns with the haphazard nature of randomness rather than opposing it.
Synonyms: Nonchalantly (बेपरवाही से), Informally (अनौपचारिक रूप से), Unintentionally (अनजाने में).
Antonyms: Seriously (गंभीरता से), Formally (औपचारिक रूप से), Meticulously (सावधानीपूर्वक).

This word means doing something without wanting to or with reluctance. it describes a person's desire or motivation rather than the order or method of an action.
Synonyms: Reluctantly (अनिच्छा से), Grudgingly (अनिच्छा से), Loathly (घृणा से).
Antonyms: Willingly (स्वेच्छा से), Eagerly (उत्सुकता से), Gladly (खुशी-खुशी).

This term means doing something in a planned, orderly, or methodical manner. It is the direct opposite of randomly, which implies a lack of method or sequence.
Synonyms: Methodically (व्यवस्थित ढंग से), Orderly (क्रमबद्ध), Regularly (नियमित रूप से).
Antonyms: Randomly (बेतरतीब ढंग से), Haphazardly (यदा-कदा), Chaotically (अराजकतापूर्ण).

This word means as a by-product or by chance. It characterizes an event that happens along with something else, which is conceptually similar to a random occurrence.
Synonyms: Parenthetically (संयोगवश), Casually (इत्तफाक से), Accidentally (अचानक).
Antonyms: Deliberately (जानबूझकर), Intentionally (जानबूझकर), Purposely (सप्रयोजन).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Brisk
questionsEn.s:
Brisk - फुरतीला / तेज़ (Quick and energetic)
Slow - धीमा / मंद (Moving without much speed)
Late night - देर रात (Happening late in the night)
Quick - तेज़ (Done with speed)
Dusky - धुंधला / सांवला (Dim or having little light)
oa:
This word means moving, doing something, or happening without much speed. It is the direct opposite of brisk, which refers to being quick, energetic, and active.
Synonyms: Sluggish (सुस्त), Leisured (धीमा), Gradual (मंद).
Antonyms: Brisk (फुरतीला), Fast (तेज़), Rapid (द्रुत).

This phrase refers to a specific time of day rather than the pace or energy level of an action. It identifies when something happens, not how it happens.
Synonyms: Midnight (आधी रात), After-hours (देर रात), Dark (अंधेरा).
Antonyms: Daytime (दिन का समय), Morning (सुबह), Early (जल्दी).

This adjective refers to doing something with speed or taking a short time. It is a synonym for brisk and therefore cannot be the required opposite.
Synonyms: Fast (तेज़), Swift (द्रुत), Speedy (शीघ्र).
Antonyms: Slow (धीमा), Tardy (विलंबित), Laggard (पिछड़ा).

This term describes something that is dim or has little light; it often refers to a dark or muted color. It relates to visibility and shade rather than speed.
Synonyms: Dim (मंद), Shadowy (छायादार), Darkish (धुंधला).
Antonyms: Bright (उज्ज्वल), Radiant (चमकीला), Luminous (प्रकाशमान).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Partial
questionsEn.s:
Partial - पक्षपाती (Showing favoritism or bias)
Unjust - अनुचित (Not morally right or fair)
Prejudiced - पूर्वाग्रहग्रस्‍त (Having a preconceived bias)
Doubtful - अनिश्चित (Uncertain or not sure)
Unbiased - निष्पक्ष (Showing no prejudice)
oa:
This adjective describes something that is unfair or not morally right. It is often a result of being partial, making it a related term rather than an opposite.
Synonyms: Unfair (अनुचित), Biased (पक्षपाती), Prejudiced (पूर्वाग्रहग्रस्‍त).
Antonyms: Just (न्यायपूर्ण), Fair (निष्पक्ष), Equitable (न्यायसंगत).

This word refers to having a preconceived opinion about someone based on their background. It is a synonym for partial and does not satisfy the requirement.
Synonyms: Biased (पक्षपाती), Bigoted (कट्टर), Opinionated (दुराग्रही).
Antonyms: Impartial (निष्पक्ष), Neutral (तटस्थ), Unbiased (पूर्वाग्रहहीन).

This term describes being uncertain or not sure about something. It relates to the degree of certainty in one's mind rather than the fairness of a judgment.
Synonyms: Uncertain (अनिश्चित), Dubious (संदिग्‍ध), Skeptical (संशयवादी).
Antonyms: Certain (निश्चित), Sure (पक्का), Confident (आत्मविश्वासी).

This word refers to showing no prejudice for or against something; it implies being impartial and fair. it is the direct opposite of being partial or biased.
Synonyms: Impartial (निष्पक्ष), Fair (न्यायपूर्ण), Objective (तटस्थ).
Antonyms: Partial (पक्षपाती), Biased (सपक्ष), Prejudiced (पूर्वाग्रही).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Trivial
questionsEn.s:
Trivial - मामूली / तुच्छ (Unimportant or insignificant)
Fierce - उग्र / बर्बर (Aggressive or violent)
Hopeful - आशावान (Feeling optimistic)
Significant - महत्वपूर्ण (Important or meaningful)
Common - सामान्य (Ordinary or usual)
oa:
This adjective describes someone or something that is aggressive, violent, or intense. It characterizes the nature of energy or behavior rather than the importance of a task.
Synonyms: Aggressive (आक्रामक), Ferocious (बर्बर), Intense (प्रबल).
Antonyms: Gentle (सौम्य), Mild (हल्का), Tame (पालतू).

This word refers to feeling or inspiring optimism about a future event. It describes an emotional outlook rather than the weight or significance of an issue.
Synonyms: Optimistic (आशावान), Sanguine (आशामय), Confident (विश्वासी).
Antonyms: Pessimistic (निराशावादी), Desperate (निराश), Gloomy (उदास).

This term means large or important enough to be worthy of attention. It stands as the direct opposite of trivial, which refers to things that are unimportant or minor.
Synonyms: Important (महत्वपूर्ण), Weighty (गंभीर), Substantial (काफ़ी बड़ा).
Antonyms: Trivial (मामूली), Petty (तुच्छ), Negligible (नगण्य).

This word describes something that is ordinary or found often. While common things are sometimes minor, the word itself refers to frequency rather than importance.
Synonyms: Usual (सामान्य), Ordinary (साधारण), Standard (मानक).
Antonyms: Rare (दुर्लभ), Unique (अद्वितीय), Unusual (असामान्य).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Abate
questionsEn.s:
Abate - कम करना / धीमा होना (To lessen or reduce in intensity)
Lessen - घटाना (To make something less)
Sustain - सहारा देना / बनाए रखना (To keep alive or healthy)
Increase - बढ़ाना (To make larger in number or degree)
Subside - शांत होना / मंद पड़ना (To become less intense)
oa:
This verb means to become less or to make something less in degree or amount. It is a synonym for abate and therefore cannot be the required opposite.
Synonyms: Reduce (घटाना), Diminish (कम करना), Decrease (घटाना).
Antonyms: Increase (बढ़ाना), Boost (बढ़ाना), Amplify (विस्तारित करना).

This word means to keep someone or something alive, healthy, or in existence. It refers to maintaining a state rather than changing its intensity in an upward direction.
Synonyms: Maintain (बनाए रखना), Support (सहारा देना), Nourish (पोषण करना).
Antonyms: Abandon (त्यागना), End (समाप्त), Weaken (कमज़ोर करना).

This verb means to become or to make something larger in number, amount, or intensity. It is the direct opposite of abate, which involves decreasing or lessening.
Synonyms: Boost (बढ़ाना), Escalate (तीव्र करना), Augment (वृद्धि करना).
Antonyms: Abate (कम करना), Decline (घटना), Lessen (घटाना).

This term refers to something becoming less intense, severe, or active. It is synonymous with the idea of abating and therefore does not satisfy the requirement.
Synonyms: Decline (कम होना), Recede (पीछे हटना), Ebb (कम होना).
Antonyms: Rise (उठना), Surge (उछाल), Increase (बढ़ना).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Nefarious
questionsEn.s:
Nefarious - अधर्मी / जघन्य (Wicked or criminal)
Pious - धर्मपरायण / पवित्र (Devoutly religious or righteous)
Traitorous - विश्वासघाती (Disloyal or treacherous)
Envious - ईर्ष्यालु (Jealous or covetous)
Perfidious - धोखेबाज (Deceitful or untrustworthy)
oa:
This adjective describes someone who is devoutly religious or righteous in character. it is the correct antonym for nefarious, which describes wicked or criminal intentions.
Synonyms: Devout (भक्त), Righteous (धर्मी), Virtuous (सदाचारी).
Antonyms: Nefarious (अधर्मी), Wicked (दुष्ट), Sinful (पापी).

This word refers to someone who is disloyal or has betrayed their country or friends. It describes a type of wicked behavior similar to being nefarious rather than opposing it.
Synonyms: Treacherous (विश्वासघाती), Faithless (बेवफा), Disloyal (राजद्रोही).
Antonyms: Loyal (वफादार), Faithful (निष्ठावान), Devoted (समर्पित).

This term describes being jealous or covetous of someone else's possessions or luck. It refers to a specific negative emotion rather than a general criminal nature.
Synonyms: Jealous (ईर्ष्यालु), Covetous (लोभी), Resentful (द्वेषपूर्ण).
Antonyms: Contented (संतुष्ट), Generous (उदार), Satisfied (तृप्त).

This adjective describes someone who is deceitful and untrustworthy. Like "traitorous," it characterizes a negative trait and functions as a near-synonym for nefarious behavior.
Synonyms: Deceitful (धोखेबाज), Dishonest (बेईमान), Insidious (कपटी).
Antonyms: Honest (ईमानदार), Reliable (विश्वसनीय), Trustworthy (भरोसेमंद).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Accepted
questionsEn.s:
Accepted - स्वीकार किया (To agree to or approve)
Trusted - विश्वास किया (To have confidence in someone)
Rejected - अस्वीकार किया (To refuse or deny)
Agreed - सहमत होना (To have the same opinion)
Believed - मान लिया (To have faith in something)
oa:
This verb means to have confidence in someone's honesty or reliability. It describes an internal belief rather than the formal act of agreeing to an excuse.
Synonyms: Believed (विश्वास किया), Relied (भरोसा किया), Confided (भरोसा किया).
Antonyms: Distrusted (अविश्वास किया), Doubted (संदेह किया), Suspected (शक किया).

This word means to refuse to accept, consider, or agree with something. It stands as the direct behavioral and contextual opposite of accepted.
Synonyms: Refused (अस्वीकार), Declined (नामंजूर), Denied (नकारा).
Antonyms: Accepted (स्वीकार), Approved (मंजूर), Agreed (सहमत).

This term refers to having the same opinion or consenting to a proposal. It is a synonym for accepted in this context and therefore is not an opposite.
Synonyms: Concurred (सहमति दी), Assented (स्वीकृति दी), Complied (पालन किया).
Antonyms: Disagreed (असहमत), Differed (भिन्न होना), Objected (आपत्ति की).

This word means to accept something as true or real. While related to acceptance, it focuses on conviction rather than the decision to approve an excuse.
Synonyms: Accepted (मान लिया), Credited (विश्वास किया), Trusted (भरोसा किया).
Antonyms: Disbelieved (अविश्वास किया), Doubted (संदेह किया), Questioned (प्रश्न किया).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Encouraged
questionsEn.s:
Encouraged - प्रोत्साहित किया (To give support or hope)
Motivated - प्रेरित किया (To provide incentive to act)
Supported - समर्थित किया (To give assistance or approval)
Cheered - हर्षोल्लास किया (To shout in support)
Discouraged - निरुत्साहित किया (To dissuade or reduce confidence)
oa:
This verb means to provide someone with a reason or incentive to act. It serves as a synonym for encouraged and does not provide the required opposite.
Synonyms: Inspired (प्रेरित), Stimulated (प्रोत्साहित), Driven (उत्तेजित).
Antonyms: Discouraged (निरुत्साहित), Deterred (रोका), Depressed (हतोत्साहित).

This term refers to giving assistance, approval, or financial help to someone. It aligns with the act of encouraging rather than opposing it.
Synonyms: Backed (समर्थित), Aided (सहायता दी), Upheld (बनाए रखा).
Antonyms: Opposed (विरोध), Hindered (बाधा), Blocked (अवरुद्ध).

This word means to shout in support or to express joy and approval. It is a more vocal and emotional form of encouragement rather than an antonym.
Synonyms: Applauded (सराहा), Hailed (जयकार), Praised (प्रशंसा की).
Antonyms: Booed (हूटिंग की), Jeered (उपहास किया), Mocked (मज़ाक उड़ाया).

This term means to dissuade or persuade someone not to do something by making them lose confidence. It is the direct opposite of encouraged.
Synonyms: Dissuaded (रोका), Disheartened (हतोत्साहित), Deterred (निवारित).
Antonyms: Encouraged (प्रोत्साहित), Persuaded (मनाया), Inspired (प्रेरित).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Above
questionsEn.s:
Above - ऊपर (Higher in position or rank)
Over - ऊपर (Above and covering)
After - बाद में (Following in time or order)
Upward - ऊपर की ओर (Moving toward a higher position)
Below - नीचे (At a lower level or position)
oa:
This preposition means being at a higher level or covering something. It is essentially a synonym for above and therefore cannot be its opposite.
Synonyms: Overhead (ऊपर), Atop (ऊपर), Beyond (परे).
Antonyms: Under (नीचे), Below (नीचे), Beneath (तले).

This term refers to something following in time or order. It identifies a sequence (first/last) rather than a vertical position (up/down).
Synonyms: Following (पश्‍चात), Later (बाद में), Subsequent (आगामी).
Antonyms: Before (पहले), Prior (पूर्व), Earlier (पहले).

This word means moving or directed towards a higher position. While it relates to being high, it is a direction of movement rather than a relative position.
Synonyms: Ascending (ऊर्ध्व), Rising (उठता हुआ), Aloft (ऊपर).
Antonyms: Downward (नीचे की ओर), Descending (अवरोही), Falling (गिरता हुआ).

This preposition means being at a lower level or position than something else. It stands as the direct spatial opposite of above.
Synonyms: Under (नीचे), Beneath (तले), Underneath (नीचे).
Antonyms: Above (ऊपर), Over (ऊपर), Aloft (ऊपर).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Meticulous
questionsEn.s:
Meticulous - अति सावधान / सूक्ष्म (Showing great attention to detail)
Accurate - यथार्थ / सही (Exact and without mistakes)
Precise - सुस्पष्ट (Clear and accurate)
Careless - लापरवाह / असावधान (Not giving sufficient attention)
Concise - संक्षिप्त (Giving information in few words)
oa:
This adjective describes something that is exact, correct, and without mistakes. It functions as a synonym for being meticulous rather than an antonym.
Synonyms: Precise (यथार्थ), Correct (सही), Exact (त्रुटिहीन).
Antonyms: Inaccurate (अशुद्ध), Wrong (गलत), Faulty (दोषपूर्ण).

This term means clear and accurate. It aligns with the careful attention to detail implied by meticulous and does not satisfy the opposite relationship.
Synonyms: Meticulous (अति सावधान), Specific (विशिष्ट), Detailed (विस्तृत).
Antonyms: Vague (अस्पष्ट), Rough (मोटा-मोटा), Indefinite (अनिश्चित).

This word means not giving sufficient attention or thought to avoid harm or errors. It is the direct opposite of meticulous, which involves being extremely careful.
Synonyms: Negligent (लापरवाह), Heedless (असावधान), Remiss (बेपरवाह).
Antonyms: Meticulous (सूक्ष्म), Careful (सावधान), Thorough (संपूर्ण).

This adjective describes giving a lot of information in a few words; brief. It refers to the length and density of information rather than the care taken in its preparation.
Synonyms: Brief (संक्षिप्त), Succinct (चुस्त), Short (छोटा).
Antonyms: Wordy (शब्दाडंबरपूर्ण), Lengthy (लंबा), Verbose (वाचाल).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Violent
questionsEn.s:
Violent - हिंसक (Using physical force to harm)
Crazy - पागल / सनकी (Mentally unstable or foolish)
Aggressive - आक्रामक (Forceful and ready to attack)
Gentle - सौम्य / कोमल (Kind and mild in nature)
Savage - बर्बर / निर्दयी (Cruel and brutal)
oa:
This word describes someone who is mentally unstable or behaving in an extremely foolish way. It refers to mental state rather than the physical force associated with violence.
Synonyms: Insane (पागल), Mad (सनकी), Absurd (मूर्ख).
Antonyms: Sane (समझदार), Rational (तर्कसंगत), Balanced (संतुलित).

This adjective describes being forceful and assertive, often ready to attack. It is a synonym for the behavioral aspect of being violent and not an opposite.
Synonyms: Hostile (शत्रुतापूर्ण), Belligerent (लड़ाकू), Pugnacious (झगड़ालू).
Antonyms: Submissive (दब्बू), Passive (निष्क्रिय), Peaceful (शांतिपूर्ण).

This word means being kind, mild, and calm in nature, avoiding the use of force. It is the direct and most appropriate antonym for violent behavior.
Synonyms: Mild (सौम्य), Kind (दयालु), Tender (कोमल).
Antonyms: Violent (हिंसक), Harsh (कठोर), Rough (उग्र).

This term describes someone who is extremely cruel, brutal, or uncivilized. It serves as a strong synonym for being violent rather than providing a contrast.
Synonyms: Brutal (बर्बर), Ferocious (क्रूर), Vicious (निर्दयी).
Antonyms: Civilized (सभ्य), Cultured (सुसंस्कृत), Gentle (सौम्य).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Sluggish
questionsEn.s:
Sluggish - सुस्त / ढीला-ढाला (Slow and lacking energy)
Active - सक्रिय / चुस्त (Lively and full of energy)
Distorted - विकृत (Twisted or deformed)
Eye catching - आकर्षक (Attractive or noticeable)
Comfortable - आरामदेह (Providing physical ease)
oa:
This word describes someone who is lively, energetic, and constantly engaged in action. It serves as the direct opposite of sluggish, which means being slow and lacking energy.
Synonyms: Energetic (ऊर्जावान), Lively (जीवंत), Brisk (फुरतीला).
Antonyms: Sluggish (सुस्त), Passive (निष्क्रिय), Idle (बेकार).

This term refers to something being twisted out of shape or misrepresented. It describes the physical or conceptual form of an object rather than its speed.
Synonyms: Deformed (विकृत), Twisted (बिगाड़ा हुआ), Misrepresented (भ्रामक).
Antonyms: Accurate (सटीक), Perfect (संपूर्ण), Normal (साधारण).

This adjective describes something that is very attractive or noticeable. It focuses on the visual appeal of an object rather than the pace of its movement.
Synonyms: Striking (प्रभावशाली), Attractive (आकर्षक), Appealing (मनोहारी).
Antonyms: Unnoticeable (अप्रत्यक्ष), Dull (फीका), Plain (सादा).

This word describes being in a state of physical ease or relaxed. While being comfortable can sometimes lead to being slow, it is not a direct opposite to sluggishness.
Synonyms: Cozy (आरामदेह), Pleasant (सुखद), Relaxed (निश्चिंत).
Antonyms: Uncomfortable (असुविधाजनक), Painful (दर्दनाक), Stiff (कठोर).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Compelled
questionsEn.s:
Compelled - मजबूर (Forced or pressured to do something)
Demur - आपत्ति (To object or hesitate)
Obscured - अस्पष्ट करना (To make unclear)
Confessed - स्वीकार करना (To admit wrongdoing)
Dissuaded - रोकना / निरुत्साहित करना (Persuaded not to do something)
oa:
This verb means to raise objections or show reluctance to do something. While it involves a reaction to being forced, it is an objection rather than the direct removal of pressure.
Synonyms: Object (आपत्ति), Hesitate (झिझकना), Protest (विरोध).
Antonyms: Accept (स्वीकार), Consent (सहमति), Agree (सहमत).

This term means to make something unclear or difficult to understand. It deals with clarity and visibility rather than the force applied to a person's decision.
Synonyms: Hidden (छिपा हुआ), Blurred (धुंधला), Veiled (अस्पष्ट).
Antonyms: Revealed (प्रकट), Clarified (स्पष्ट), Exposed (उजागर).

This verb refers to admitting or acknowledging a wrongdoing or a secret. It describes an act of honesty rather than the opposite of being forced into an action.
Synonyms: Admitted (स्वीकार किया), Disclosed (प्रकट किया), Owned (माना).
Antonyms: Denied (इनकार किया), Concealed (छिपाया), Refuted (खंडन किया).

This term refers to being persuaded not to take a particular course of action. In the context of being influenced or urged, it serves as the most appropriate opposite for being compelled.
Synonyms: Discouraged (निरुत्साहित), Deterred (रोका), Prevented (निवारित).
Antonyms: Compelled (मजबूर), Persuaded (मनाया), Urged (प्रेरित).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Adage
questionsEn.s:
Adage - कहावत / सत्य (A saying expressing a general truth)
Misconstruction - गलतफहमी (A false interpretation)
Rebuke - फटकार (To scold or criticize)
Dare - हिम्मत / चुनौती (To challenge someone to do something)
Addiction - लत (Strong dependence on a substance)
oa:
This noun refers to a false or wrong interpretation of something. it functions as an antonym for adage because an adage is a widely accepted, settled truth.
Synonyms: Misinterpretation (गलतफहमी), Error (चूक), Delusion (भ्रम).
Antonyms: Adage (कहावत), Truth (सच्चाई), Fact (तथ्य).

This word refers to a sharp disapproval or a scolding. It focuses on criticism of a person's behavior rather than the validity of a traditional saying.
Synonyms: Scolding (फटकार), Reprimand (निंदा), Censure (भर्त्सना).
Antonyms: Praise (प्रशंसा), Compliment (तारीफ), Commend (सराहना).

This term means to have the courage to do something or to challenge someone. It focuses on bravery and risk rather than a general or accepted truth.
Synonyms: Challenge (चुनौती), Defy (अवहेलना), Venture (साहस).
Antonyms: Avoid (बचना), Fear (डरना), Dodge (टालना).

This noun refers to a strong physical or mental dependence on a substance or activity. It identifies a medical or behavioral condition unrelated to proverbs.
Synonyms: Dependence (लत), Habit (आदत), Obsession (जुनून).
Antonyms: Dislike (नापसंद), Avoidance (परहेज), Detachment (वैराग्य).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Callous
questionsEn.s:
Callous - निर्दयी / कठोर (Showing no concern for others' suffering)
Rationalistic - तर्कवादी (Believing in the use of reason)
Unsympathetic - सहानुभूतिहीन (Not showing sympathy)
Sympathetic - सहानुभूतिपूर्ण (Showing compassion or understanding)
Nondiplomatic - अकुशल (Lacking tact or diplomacy)
oa:
This adjective describes a belief in using reason and logic to understand the world. It deals with intellectual processes rather than the capacity for emotional sympathy.
Synonyms: Logical (तर्कसंगत), Analytical (विश्लेषणात्मक), Scientific (वैज्ञानिक).
Antonyms: Emotional (भावनात्मक), Intuitive (सहज), Irrational (अतार्किक).

This word describes someone who is not showing or feeling sympathy. It is a direct synonym for callous and therefore cannot be used as its antonym.
Synonyms: Callous (निर्दयी), Cold (भावहीन), Indifferent (उदासीन).
Antonyms: Sympathetic (सहानुभूतिपूर्ण), Kind (दयालु), Caring (देखभाल करने वाला).

This term means showing compassion or understanding for others' feelings. It is the direct opposite of being callous, which implies an insensitive disregard for others.
Synonyms: Compassionate (दयालु), Kind (सदय), Empathetic (सहानुभूतिपूर्ण).
Antonyms: Callous (कठोर), Unkind (निष्ठुर), Heartless (निर्दयी).

This word refers to a lack of tact or skill in dealing with people. While it might describe a rude person, it does not specifically address the lack of pity associated with callousness.
Synonyms: Tactless (अकुशल), Blunt (स्पष्टवादी), Abrupt (रूखा).
Antonyms: Diplomatic (कूटनीतिक), Tactful (विनम्र), Courteous (शिष्ट).

test.instructions: Standard CBT Pattern Exam. Positive Marks: +1, Negative Marks: -0.25. Total Questions: 50.

test.title: Set - 15

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Optimistic
questionsEn.s:
Optimistic - आशावादी (Expecting good things to happen)
Stay - ठहरना (To remain in a place)
Incident - घटना (An event or occurrence)
Positive - सकारात्मक (Hopeful and confident)
Gloomy - निराशावादी / उदास (Lacking hope or feeling sad)
oa:
This verb means to remain in a particular place or condition. It is a neutral term identifying a state of presence rather than an emotional or mental outlook.
Synonyms: Remain (ठहरना), Reside (बसना), Wait (प्रतीक्षा करना).
Antonyms: Leave (छोड़ना), Depart (प्रस्थान), Exit (निकलना).

This noun refers to an event or occurrence, especially one that is unusual or unpleasant. It identifies a happening rather than a person's expectation of the future.
Synonyms: Event (घटना), Occasion (अवसर), Episode (प्रसंग).
Antonyms: Routine (नियम), Nothing (कुछ नहीं), Plan (योजना).

This word refers to being hopeful or confident. It is a direct synonym for optimistic and therefore cannot be used as the required opposite.
Synonyms: Confident (आत्मविश्वासी), Sanguine (आशावादी), Bright (उज्ज्वल).
Antonyms: Negative (नकारात्मक), Pessimistic (निराशावादी), Gloomy (उदास).

This adjective refers to a sense of sadness, pessimism, and lack of hope. it serves as the correct antonym for optimistic, which involves expecting good results.
Synonyms: Pessimistic (निराशावादी), Dismal (निराशाजनक), Sad (उदास).
Antonyms: Optimistic (आशावादी), Cheerful (हंसमुख), Bright (उज्ज्वल).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Evident
questionsEn.s:
Evident - स्पष्ट / प्रत्यक्ष (Clearly visible or noticeable)
Hidden - छिपा हुआ (Not easily noticed or seen)
Profuse - प्रचुर (Abundant or excessive)
Visible - दृश्य (Able to be seen)
oa:
This adjective describes something that is kept out of sight or not easily noticed. It serves as the direct opposite of evident, which means clearly visible or noticeable.
Synonyms: Concealed (छिपा हुआ), Obscure (धुंधला), Masked (ढका हुआ).
Antonyms: Evident (स्पष्ट), Visible (प्रत्यक्ष), Obvious (साफ).

This word refers to something that is produced in large amounts or is excessive. It deals with the quantity of a substance rather than its clarity or visibility.
Synonyms: Abundant (प्रचुर), Copious (भरपूर), Lavish (अत्यधिक).
Antonyms: Scanty (अल्प), Meager (थोड़ा), Scarce (दुर्लभ).

This adjective describes something that is free from error and in accordance with fact or truth. It focuses on accuracy rather than how easily something can be seen.
Synonyms: Accurate (सही), Right (शुद्ध), Valid (वैध).
Antonyms: Incorrect (गलत), Faulty (दोषपूर्ण), Erroneous (अशुद्ध).

This word means able to be seen. It is a direct synonym for evident and therefore does not satisfy the requirement for an opposite.
Synonyms: Apparent (प्रत्यक्ष), Clear (स्पष्ट), Noticeable (प्रत्यक्ष).
Antonyms: Invisible (अदृश्य), Hidden (गुप्त), Imperceptible (अगोचर).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Nervous
questionsEn.s:
Nervous - घबराया हुआ / व्यग्र (Feeling anxious or apprehensive)
Hesitant - हिचकिचाने वाला (Tentative or unsure)
Shaky - कांपता हुआ (Trembling or unsteady)
Casual - अनौपचारिक (Relaxed and unconcerned)
Courageous - साहसी (Not deterred by danger or pain; brave)
oa:
This adjective describes someone who is tentative, unsure, or slow in acting. It aligns with the uncertainty of being nervous rather than opposing it.
Synonyms: Tentative (अनिश्चित), Uncertain (द्विधा में), Dithering (हिचकिचाने वाला).
Antonyms: Decisive (निर्णायक), Confident (आत्मविश्वासी), Resolute (दृढ़).

This term describes something trembling or unsteady. It is often a physical symptom of being nervous and acts as a synonym in many contexts.
Synonyms: Trembling (कांपता हुआ), Unsteady (अस्थिर), Tottering (डगमगाता).
Antonyms: Steady (स्थिर), Stable (मजबूत), Firm (दृढ़).

This word refers to being relaxed and unconcerned or happening by chance. While it implies a lack of anxiety, it doesn't provide the strong thematic contrast required.
Synonyms: Relaxed (निश्चिंत), Informal (अनौपचारिक), Easy-going (लापरवाह).
Antonyms: Formal (औपचारिक), Serious (गंभीर), Anxious (चिंतित).

This term describes someone who is not deterred by danger or pain; brave. it is the most appropriate opposite for nervous, as it implies boldness and lack of fear.
Synonyms: Brave (बहादुर), Bold (साहसी), Intrepid (निडर).
Antonyms: Nervous (घबराया हुआ), Cowardly (कायर), Timid (डरपोक).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Meticulous
questionsEn.s:
Meticulous - सूक्ष्म / सावधानीपूर्वक (Showing great attention to detail)
Heedful - सावधान (Paying careful attention)
Careful - सावधान (Avoiding danger or harm)
Careless - लापरवाह (Not giving sufficient attention)
Untidy - अव्यवस्थित (Not arranged neatly)
oa:
This adjective describes someone who is paying careful attention to something. It is a synonym for being meticulous and therefore is not an opposite.
Synonyms: Attentive (सावधान), Vigilant (सतर्क), Observant (चौकस).
Antonyms: Heedless (असावधान), Careless (लापरवाह), Negligent (बेपरवाह).

This term refers to making sure to avoid potential danger, mishap, or harm. Like meticulous, it describes an attitude of caution rather than a lack of detail.
Synonyms: Wary (सतर्क), Prudent (विवेकपूर्ण), Meticulous (सूक्ष्म).
Antonyms: Rash (जल्दबाज), Reckless (लापरवाह), Careless (असावधान).

This word means not giving sufficient attention or thought to avoiding harm or errors. It is the direct opposite of meticulous, which signifies great attention to detail.
Synonyms: Negligent (लापरवाह), Slapdash (अव्यवस्थित), Remiss (बेपरवाह).
Antonyms: Meticulous (सावधानीपूर्वक), Thorough (संपूर्ण), Careful (सावधान).

This adjective describes something that is not arranged neatly or is in disorder. While related to a lack of care, it focuses on physical mess rather than the mental process of detail.
Synonyms: Messy (गंदा), Disorganized (अव्यवस्थित), Cluttered (अस्त-व्यस्त).
Antonyms: Tidy (साफ-सुथरा), Neat (सुव्यवस्थित), Ordered (क्रमबद्ध).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Hinder
questionsEn.s:
Hinder - बाधा डालना (To create difficulties or delay)
Monitor - निगरानी करना (To observe and check progress)
Aid - सहायता करना (To help or support)
Domesticate - पालतू बनाना (To tame an animal)
Force - बल (Strength or physical energy)
oa:
This verb refers to observing and checking the progress of something over time. It describes a process of oversight rather than the act of blocking or helping movement.
Synonyms: Observe (निगरानी करना), Track (नज़र रखना), Supervise (निरीक्षण).
Antonyms: Ignore (नज़रअंदाज़), Neglect (उपेक्षा), Overlook (अनदेखा).

This term refers to help or support, typically of a practical nature. it is the direct opposite of hinder, which means to create difficulties that result in delay or obstruction.
Synonyms: Assist (सहायता), Support (सहयोग), Help (मदद).
Antonyms: Hinder (बाधा डालना), Obstruct (अवरोध), Block (रोकना).

This verb means to tame an animal and keep it as a pet or on a farm. It relates to the taming of nature and has no connection with blocking or helping an action.
Synonyms: Tame (पालतू बनाना), Train (सिखाना), Gentle (कोमल बनाना).
Antonyms: Wild (जंगली), Free (आज़ाद), Release (छोड़ना).

This word refers to strength or energy as an attribute of physical action. It focuses on the exertion of power rather than the facilitation or obstruction of progress.
Synonyms: Compel (विवश करना), Coerce (मजबूर करना), Exert (प्रयास करना).
Antonyms: Persuade (मनाना), Allow (अनुमति), Free (मुक्त).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Perseverance
questionsEn.s:
Perseverance - दृढ़ता (Persistence in doing something despite difficulty)
Irresolution - दुविधा / अनिर्णय (Hesitancy or uncertainty)
Obstacy - हठ (Stubborn refusal to change)
Readiness - तत्परता (State of being fully prepared)
Eloquence - वाक्‌चातुर्य (Fluent or persuasive speaking)
oa:
This noun refers to hesitancy or uncertainty in a course of action. It serves as the direct opposite of perseverance, which involves persistence despite difficulty.
Synonyms: Indecision (दुविधा), Hesitancy (झिझक), Vacillation (डगमगाहट).
Antonyms: Perseverance (दृढ़ता), Determination (संकल्प), Resolution (निर्णय).

This term refers to the quality of being stubborn or refusing to change one's opinion. It is a synonym for a stubborn form of perseverance and thus not an opposite.
Synonyms: Stubbornness (हठ), Doggedness (ज़िद्दीपन), Tenacity (दृढ़ता).
Antonyms: Compliance (अनुपालन), Flexibility (लचीलापन), Docility (विनम्रता).

This word describes the state of being fully prepared for something. It focuses on the timing and willingness to act rather than the long-term persistence in a task.
Synonyms: Preparedness (तत्परता), Promptness (मुस्तैदी), Alacrity (उत्सुकता).
Antonyms: Unpreparedness (अतैयारी), Hesitance (संकोच), Delay (विलंब).

This term refers to fluent or persuasive speaking or writing. It describes communication skills and has no relationship to the concept of persistence or uncertainty.
Synonyms: Fluency (वाक्‌चातुर्य), Oratory (भाषणकला), Rhetoric (वाकपटुता).
Antonyms: Inarticulacy (अस्पष्टता), Muteness (मूकता), Dullness (नीरसता).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Arrival
questionsEn.s:
Arrival - आगमन / पहुँच (Reaching the place of travel)
Timing - समय-निर्धारण (The time when something happens)
Entrance - प्रवेश (Coming into a place)
Departure - प्रस्थान / रवानगी (Leaving or going away)
Appearance - रूप-रंग / उपस्थिति (The way someone looks or becomes visible)
oa:
This noun refers to the time when something is planned to happen or the skill of doing something at the right moment. It deals with scheduling rather than movement.
Synonyms: Scheduling (समय-निर्धारण), Punctuality (समयपालन), Sequence (अनुक्रम).
Antonyms: Tardiness (विलंब), Miscalculation (गलत गणना), Delay (देर).

This word refers to a door, gate, or the act of coming into a place. It describes the beginning of presence and is a synonym for arrival in many contexts.
Synonyms: Admission (प्रवेश), Ingress (प्रवेश), Access (पहुँच).
Antonyms: Exit (निकास), Departure (प्रस्थान), Withdrawal (वापसी).

This term means the act of leaving or going away from a place. It acts as the direct and most accurate antonym for arrival, which means reaching a destination.
Synonyms: Leaving (रवानगी), Exit (निकास), Withdrawal (वापसी).
Antonyms: Arrival (आगमन), Entrance (प्रवेश), Ingress (प्रवेश).

This term refers to the way that someone looks or the act of becoming visible. It characterizes visibility rather than the completion of a journey.
Synonyms: Presence (उपस्थिति), Aspect (रूप), Look (शक-सूरत).
Antonyms: Disappearance (गायब होना), Vanishing (विलुप्ति), Absence (अनुपस्थिति).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Unsure
questionsEn.s:
Unsure - अनिश्चित (Uncertain or having doubts)
Certain - निश्चित / पक्का (Confident or having no doubt)
Date - तिथि (A particular day or time)
Customised - अनुकूलित (Modified to suit an individual)
Handicrafts - हस्तशिल्प (Items made by hand with skill)
oa:
This noun refers to a particular day of the month or year. It is a factual reference to time and bears no logical relationship of opposition to the state of being unsure.
Synonyms: Day (तिथि), Time (दिनांक), Appointment (मुलाकात).
Antonyms: Eternity (अनंत), Void (शून्यता), Period (अवधि).

This word describes being completely confident or having no doubt about something. It is the direct opposite of unsure, which implies uncertainty or having doubts.
Synonyms: Sure (निश्चित), Confident (पक्का), Definite (सुस्पष्ट).
Antonyms: Unsure (अनिश्चित), Doubtful (संदिग्ध), Hesitant (दुविधा में).

This term means modified or made to suit a particular individual or task. It describes the tailoring of a product rather than the level of certainty in a person's mind.
Synonyms: Personalized (स्वनिर्धारित), Tailored (विशिष्ट), Bespoke (अनुकूलित).
Antonyms: Standardized (मानक), Mass-produced (बड़े पैमाने पर निर्मित), Generic (सामान्य).

This word refers to activities that need skill with the hands or the products made from such skills. It identifies a category of items and not a state of doubt.
Synonyms: Artisanry (हस्तशिल्प), Craftsmanship (कौशल), Artifacts (शिल्प).
Antonyms: Industrial (औद्योगिक), Automated (स्वचालित), Mass-market (व्यावसायिक).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Acquitted
questionsEn.s:
Acquitted - बरी किया / दोषमुक्त (Formally stated as not guilty)
Conformed - अनुपालन किया (Obeyed a rule or law)
Discharged - मुक्त किया (Sent something out or allowed to leave)
Praised - प्रशंसा की (Expressing admiration for something)
Convicted - दोषी ठहराया (Officially declared guilty in court)
oa:
This verb means to obey a rule, law, or custom. It describes the act of following standards rather than a formal verdict given in a court of law.
Synonyms: Complied (अनुपालन किया), Followed (अनुसरण किया), Obeyed (आज्ञा मानी).
Antonyms: Defied (अवहेलना), Rebelled (विद्रोह), Violated (उल्लंघन किया).

This term means to tell someone officially that they can leave, often after a period of duty. While it implies being set free, it lacks the specific context of innocence.
Synonyms: Released (मुक्त किया), Dismissed (बर्खास्त), Freed (आज़ाद).
Antonyms: Detained (हिरासत), Enlisted (भरती), Retained (बनाए रखा).

This word means to express approval or admiration for something or someone. It is a social or verbal acknowledgment rather than a legal declaration of guilt or innocence.
Synonyms: Commended (सराहना), Extolled (प्रशंसा की), Lauded (सराहा).
Antonyms: Criticized (आलोचना), Rebuked (फटकारा), Condemned (निंदा की).

This term means to say officially in a court of law that someone is guilty of a crime. It is the direct legal opposite of being acquitted or found not guilty.
Synonyms: Sentenced (दोषी ठहराया), Condemned (दोषी), Found guilty (अपराधी पाया).
Antonyms: Acquitted (बरी किया), Exonerated (दोषमुक्त), Cleared (दोषमुक्त).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Modest
questionsEn.s:
Modest - विनम्र / विनीत (Not talking too much about one's abilities)
Distant - दूर / अलग-थलग (A long way away or unfriendly)
Unpresuming - विनम्र (Unassuming or modest)
Conceited - अहंकारी / घमंडी (Excessively proud of oneself)
Obvious - स्पष्ट (Easily seen or understood)
oa:
This adjective refers to being a long way away in space or time, or being cold and unfriendly. It focuses on proximity and social warmth rather than pride.
Synonyms: Remote (दूरस्थ), Faraway (दूर), Aloof (अलग-थलग).
Antonyms: Near (पास), Close (नज़दीक), Friendly (मिलनसार).

This word describes someone who is modest or unassuming. It acts as a synonym for the given word and therefore does not satisfy the required relationship.
Synonyms: Humble (विनम्र), Modest (विनीत), Meek (नम्र).
Antonyms: Arrogant (घमंडी), Proud (अभिमानी), Conceited (अहंकारी).

This word means excessively proud of oneself; vain. It is the direct and most accurate antonym for modest, which describes being humble about one's abilities.
Synonyms: Arrogant (अहंकारी), Haughty (घमंडी), Vain (अभिमानी).
Antonyms: Modest (विनम्र), Humble (विनीत), Unpresuming (निःसंदेह).

This adjective refers to something easily seen or understood; clear. It relates to the visibility of a fact rather than the personality trait of a person.
Synonyms: Clear (स्पष्ट), Evident (प्रत्यक्ष), Manifest (साफ).
Antonyms: Obscure (धुंधला), Vague (अस्पष्ट), Hidden (छिपा हुआ).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Messy
questionsEn.s:
Messy - गंदा / अव्यवस्थित (Untidy or disorganized)
Untidy - मैला-कुचैला (Not neat or well arranged)
Chaotic - अराजक (In a state of complete confusion)
Disordered - अव्यवस्थित (Lacking order or arrangement)
Organised - व्यवस्थित (Everything in order and well arranged)
oa:
This word means not neat or well arranged. It functions as a direct synonym for messy and therefore does not satisfy the requirement for an opposite.
Synonyms: Messy (गंदा), Slapdash (अव्यवस्थित), Cluttered (अस्त-व्यस्त).
Antonyms: Tidy (साफ-सुथरा), Neat (सुव्यवस्थित), Clean (निर्मल).

This term describes being in a state of complete confusion and disorder. It is a higher-intensity synonym for messy rather than being its opposite.
Synonyms: Disorganized (अव्यवस्थित), Turmoil (उथल-पुथल), Muddled (उलझा हुआ).
Antonyms: Orderly (क्रमबद्ध), Systematic (व्यवस्थित), Calm (शांत).

This adjective refers to lacking order or regular arrangement. It characterizes the same negative state as being messy and does not function as an antonym.
Synonyms: Untidy (मैला), Unsystematic (अव्यवस्थित), Random (बेतरतीब).
Antonyms: Ordered (क्रमबद्ध), Organized (व्यवस्थित), Neat (सुथरा).

This word means arranged in a systematic manner or having everything in order. It is the direct and most suitable antonym for being messy.
Synonyms: Systematic (व्यवस्थित), Orderly (क्रमबद्ध), Structured (संरचित).
Antonyms: Messy (गंदा), Chaotic (अराजक), Disordered (अव्यवस्थित).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Definite
questionsEn.s:
Definite - निश्चित / स्पष्ट (Unmistakable and well-defined)
Monotonous - नीरस (Lack of change; boring)
Hazy - धुंधला (Not well-defined; blurred)
Subtle - सूक्ष्म (Not easily noticeable; delicate)
Vague - अस्पष्ट / अनिश्चित (Lack of clarity or precision)
oa:
This adjective describes a lack of change or variety, often leading to boredom. It refers to the interest level of a pattern rather than the clarity of an arrangement.
Synonyms: Boring (नीरस), Tedious (उबाऊ), Repetitive (बार-बार होने वाला).
Antonyms: Exciting (रोमांचक), Varied (विविध), Diverse (विविध).

This word refers to a visual or mental state where details are not well-defined or appear blurred. While it implies lack of clarity, it's often more about sight than definition.
Synonyms: Blurred (धुंधला), Foggy (धुंधला), Misty (कुहासा भरा).
Antonyms: Clear (स्पष्ट), Lucid (सुस्पष्ट), Bright (चमकीला).

This term refers to qualities or details that are not easily noticeable and require careful thought to be understood. It describes delicacy rather than lack of certainty.
Synonyms: Fine (सूक्ष्म), Precise (बारीक), Understated (कोमल).
Antonyms: Obvious (स्पष्ट), Crude (अपरिष्कृत), Blatant (खुल्लमखुल्ला).

This word describes situations where there is a lack of clarity, precision, or specificity. It serves as the direct antonym for definite, which implies being unmistakably clear.
Synonyms: Unclear (अस्पष्ट), Indefinite (अनिश्चित), Ambiguous (अनेकार्थी).
Antonyms: Definite (निश्चित), Precise (सटीक), Specific (विशिष्ट).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Rowdy
questionsEn.s:
Rowdy - उपद्रवी / उधमी (Loud, disorderly, and rough)
Compliant - आज्ञाकारी (Well-behaved and following rules)
Chattering - बड़बड़ाहट (Talking a lot)
Disorderly - अव्यवस्थित (Chaotic or untidy)
Noisy - शोरगुल वाला (Filled with loud sounds)
oa:
This adjective describes someone or a group that is well-behaved and follows rules or orders. It acts as the best antonym for rowdy, which implies noisy disorder.
Synonyms: Obedient (आज्ञाकारी), Submissive (दब्बू), Docile (विनम्र).
Antonyms: Rowdy (उपद्रवी), Rebellious (विद्रोही), Defiant (अवज्ञाकारी).

This term refers to talking rapidly or incessantly, often about trivial matters. While it involves noise, it describes the act of talking rather than general misbehavior.
Synonyms: Talkative (बातूनी), Babbling (बड़बड़ाना), Garrulous (वाचाल).
Antonyms: Silent (मौन), Quiet (शांत), Reticent (अल्पभाषी).

This word means not controlled by rules or a system; it describes a situation that is chaotic. It is a direct synonym for rowdy and cannot be an opposite.
Synonyms: Chaotic (अराजक), Untidy (अव्यवस्थित), Messy (गंदा).
Antonyms: Orderly (क्रमबद्ध), Disciplined (अनुशासित), Systematic (व्यवस्थित).

This adjective describes something full of loud and often disruptive sounds. It is a synonym for the acoustic aspect of being rowdy rather than providing a contrast.
Synonyms: Clamorous (कोलाहलपूर्ण), Loud (जोरदार), Boisterous (उधमी).
Antonyms: Quiet (शांत), Silent (चुप), Peaceful (शांतिपूर्ण).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Probably
questionsEn.s:
Probably - शायद (Suggested uncertainty or likelihood)
Definitely - निश्चित रूप से (Without doubt or certainly)
Perhaps - शायद / कदाचित (Maybe or possibly)
Apparently - प्रतीत होता है (Based on appearances)
Possibly - संभवतः (Maybe or potentially)
oa:
This adverb means without doubt or certainly. It serves as the direct opposite of probably, which suggests a degree of uncertainty or likelihood rather than absolute truth.
Synonyms: Certainly (निश्चित रूप से), Surely (पक्का), Absolutely (पूरी तरह).
Antonyms: Probably (शायद), Possibly (संभवतः), Perhaps (कदाचित).

This term means maybe or possibly. It functions as a synonym for probably in contexts involving uncertainty and therefore is not an opposite.
Synonyms: Possibly (संभवतः), Maybe (शायद), Peradventure (संयोगवश).
Antonyms: Definitely (निश्चित रूप से), Certainly (पक्का), Surely (जरूर).

This word means seemingly or based on appearances. It describes how something looks regardless of the actual facts and does not specifically address the degree of probability.
Synonyms: Seemingly (प्रतीत होता है), Ostensibly (जाहिर तौर पर), Evident (प्रत्यक्ष).
Antonyms: Hiddenly (गुप्त रूप से), Improbably (असंभवतः), Unlikely (शायद ही).

This adverb refers to something that may happen or be the case; it signifies potential. Since it implies the same lack of certainty as probably, it is a synonym.
Synonyms: Maybe (शायद), Perhaps (कदाचित), Potentially (संभवतः).
Antonyms: Impossible (असंभव), Definitely (निश्चित रूप से), certainly (पक्का).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Expensive
questionsEn.s:
Expensive - महंगा / खर्चीला (Costing a lot of money)
Cheap - सस्ता (Low in price or costing little)
Costly - कीमती (Costing much; expensive)
Premium - प्रीमियम / अतिरिक्त (High quality or additional cost)
Precious - बहुमूल्य (Of great value or rare)
oa:
This adjective refers to things that are low in price or cost little money. It is the direct and most accurate antonym for expensive, which means costing a lot.
Synonyms: Inexpensive (सस्ता), Affordable (किफायती), Low-priced (कम कीमत).
Antonyms: Expensive (महंगा), Costly (कीमती), Priceless (अमूल्य).

This term means costing a lot of money or being expensive. It is a synonym for the given word and therefore does not satisfy the requirement for an opposite.
Synonyms: Dear (कीमती), High-priced (महंगा), Sumptuous (आलीशान).
Antonyms: Cheap (सस्ता), Inexpensive (सस्ता), Budget (किफायती).

This word refers to a high quality or a higher price paid for a specific benefit. While related to price, it describes a superior category rather than a lack of expense.
Synonyms: Superior (श्रेष्ठ), Choice (उत्कृष्ट), Deluxe (भव्य).
Antonyms: Basic (बुनियादी), Standard (सामान्य), Cheap (सस्ता).

This adjective describes something of great value, often because it is rare or difficult to find. It focuses on the worth or sentimental value rather than the simple market price.
Synonyms: Valuable (बहुमूल्य), Cherished (प्यारा), Rare (दुर्लभ).
Antonyms: Worthless (बेकार), Common (सामान्य), Trashy (तुच्छ).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Lament
questionsEn.s:
Lament - विलाप / शोक (Expressing grief or sorrow)
Deplore - दुःखी होना / निंदा करना (Expressing strong disapproval)
Decry - निंदा करना (To publicly denounce)
Celebrate - जश्न मनाना (Marking an occasion with joy)
Regret - पछताना (Feeling sad about a past event)
oa:
This verb means to feel or express strong disapproval of something. It involves a negative emotional judgment similar to lamenting and therefore is not an opposite.
Synonyms: Condemn (निंदा करना), Regret (पछताना), Mourn (शोक करना).
Antonyms: Applaud (प्रशंसा), Approve (मंजूरी), Celebrate (उत्सव मनाना).

This word means to publicly denounce or express strong disapproval of something. Like deplore, it is a negative response to an event or situation.
Synonyms: Denounce (निंदा करना), Criticize (आलोचना), Vilify (गाली देना).
Antonyms: Praise (प्रशंसा), Commend (सराहना), Extol (बखान करना).

This word means to mark an event or achievement with joy and festivity. It is the direct and most appropriate antonym for lamenting, which involves expressing grief.
Synonyms: Rejoice (आनंद मनाना), Commemorate (उत्सव मनाना), Revel (मौज-मस्ती).
Antonyms: Lament (विलाप), Mourn (शोक), Regret (पछताना).

This term refers to feeling sad, repentant, or disappointed about something that has happened. It is a component of lamenting and acts as a synonym.
Synonyms: Rue (पछताना), Repent (पश्चाताप), Sorrow (दुःख).
Antonyms: Rejoice (खुश होना), Satisfied (संतुष्ट), Proud (गर्वित).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Yell
questionsEn.s:
Yell - चिल्लाना (To shout loudly or raise voice)
Notify - सूचित करना (To inform or give notice)
Indemnify - मुआवज़ा देना (To compensate for loss)
Whisper - फुसफुसाना (To speak in a soft, low voice)
Terrorise - आतंकित करना (To intimidate or create fear)
oa:
This verb means to inform or give official notice to someone about something. it describes a formal process of communication rather than a volume level of speech.
Synonyms: Inform (सूचित करना), Apprise (बताना), Announce (घोषित करना).
Antonyms: Hide (छिपाना), Conceal (गुप्त रखना), Ignore (उपेक्षा).

This legal term means to compensate someone for harm or loss. It deals with financial or legal protection and has no relationship to the act of shouting.
Synonyms: Compensate (मुआवज़ा देना), Recompense (क्षतिपूर्ति), Repay (चुकाना).
Antonyms: Penalize (दंडित), Charge (आरोप), Fine (जुर्माना).

This term signifies speaking in a very soft, low voice, often to maintain privacy. it is the direct opposite of yelling, which involves shouting loudly and forcefully.
Synonyms: Murmur (फुसफुसाना), Mutter (बुदबुदाना), Mumble (अस्पष्ट बोलना).
Antonyms: Yell (चिल्लाना), Shout (चिल्लाना), Scream (चीखना).

This verb means to use violence and intimidation to create fear, especially for political purposes. It focuses on the intent to frighten rather than the volume of sound.
Synonyms: Intimidate (आतंकित करना), Frighten (डराना), Bully (धमकाना).
Antonyms: Comfort (सांत्वना), Reassure (आश्वस्त), Protect (रक्षा).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Clear
questionsEn.s:
Clear - स्पष्ट / साफ (Pure or easy to see through)
Clean - साफ / निर्मल (Not dirty or contaminated)
Opaque - अपारदर्शी (Not letting light through)
Mess - गंदगी / अव्यवस्था (A state of being untidy)
Untidy - मैला-कुचैला (Not well arranged)
oa:
This adjective describes something that is not dirty, soiled, or contaminated. While clear things are often clean, this word focuses on hygiene and purity rather than transparency.
Synonyms: Pure (निर्मल), Spotless (स्वच्छ), Unsoiled (साफ).
Antonyms: Dirty (गंदा), Filthy (मैला), Soiled (गंदा).

This term refers to something that does not let light pass through and is not transparent. it serves as the direct physical opposite for clear when describing substances.
Synonyms: Murky (धुंधला), Cloudy (अस्पष्ट), Turbid (मैला).
Antonyms: Clear (साफ), Transparent (पारदर्शी), Lucid (सुस्पष्ट).

This noun refers to a state of being dirty, untidy, or disorganized. It describes a situation or a pile of objects rather than the visual quality of transparency or understanding.
Synonyms: Chaos (गंदगी), Clutter (अव्यवस्था), Jumble (गड़बड़).
Antonyms: Order (व्यवस्था), Neatness (सफाई), System (प्रणाली).

This word means not neat or well arranged; it is used to describe a room or a person's appearance. It relates to organization rather than clarity or transparency.
Synonyms: Messy (मैला-कुचैला), Slapdash (अव्यवस्थित), Sloppy (लापरवाह).
Antonyms: Tidy (सुव्यवस्थित), Neat (सुथरा), Ordered (क्रमबद्ध).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Waned
questionsEn.s:
Waned - क्षीण होना / कम होना (To become gradually weaker)
Declined - ह्रास होना (To become weaker or smaller)
Dimmed - धुंधला होना (To become less bright)
Abated - धीमा होना (To become less strong)
Grew - बढ़ना / विकसित होना (To increase in size or strength)
oa:
This verb means to become weaker, smaller, or less good. it is a direct synonym for waned and therefore cannot satisfy the requirement for an opposite.
Synonyms: Diminished (क्षीण हुआ), Ebbed (घटा), Decreased (कम हुआ).
Antonyms: Increased (बढ़ा), Grew (विकसित हुआ), Rose (उठा).

This term refers to something becoming less bright or clear. It focuses on the intensity of light or understanding, functioning similarly to the idea of waning.
Synonyms: Faded (धुंधला हुआ), Obscured (अस्पष्ट), Pale (फीका).
Antonyms: Brightened (चमका), Lighted (प्रकाशित), Clarified (स्पष्ट किया).

This word means to become less strong or to lessen the intensity of something. It is a synonym for waned in the context of energy or impact.
Synonyms: Subsided (शांत हुआ), Lessened (कम हुआ), Moderated (धीमा हुआ).
Antonyms: Intensified (तीव्र हुआ), Heightened (बढ़ा), Increased (बढ़ा).

This verb refers to increasing in size, number, or strength. It serves as the direct opposite of waned, which involves becoming gradually weaker or less important.
Synonyms: Increased (बढ़ा), Expanded (फैलना), Developed (विकसित हुआ).
Antonyms: Waned (क्षीण हुआ), Shrank (सिकुड़ा), Declined (घटा).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Veteran
questionsEn.s:
Veteran - अनुभवी (A person of long experience in a skill)
Renowned - प्रसिद्ध (Known by many people; famous)
Creviced - दरारयुक्त (Having narrow openings or cracks)
Conditioned - अनुकूलित (Affecting the way someone behaves)
Novice - नौसिखिया (A person new to a job or experience)
oa:
This adjective describes someone who is known or talked about by many people; famous. It focuses on reputation rather than the length of experience in a field.
Synonyms: Famous (प्रसिद्ध), Celebrated (प्रख्यात), Noted (विख्यात).
Antonyms: Anonymous (अज्ञात), Unknown (अनजान), Obscure (अस्पष्ट).

This term refers to something having narrow openings caused by splits or cracks. It describes a physical texture and has no logical connection to human experience.
Synonyms: Cracked (दरारयुक्त), Fissured (दरार भरा), Split (फटा हुआ).
Antonyms: Smooth (चिकना), Solid (ठोस), Unbroken (अखंड).

This verb means to affect or control the way that someone behaves or to adapt them to certain environments. It relates to behaviorism, not the lack of experience.
Synonyms: Trained (अनुकूलित), Adapted (अभ्यस्त), Regulated (नियंत्रित).
Antonyms: Unprepared (अतैयार), Natural (प्राकृतिक), Raw (कच्चा).

This word refers to a person who is new and without experience in a certain job or situation. it is the direct opposite of a veteran, who has long experience.
Synonyms: Beginner (नौसिखिया), Rookie (नया खिलाड़ी), Learner (शिक्षार्थी).
Antonyms: Veteran (अनुभवी), Expert (विशेषज्ञ), Master (उस्ताद).

questionsEn.q: Select the word opposite in meaning to: Fetish
questionsEn.s:
Fetish - मनोग्रस्‍तता (An unreasonable obsession with something)
Indifference - उदासीनता (Lack of interest or feeling)
Fixed - निश्चित (Already decided or firm)
Problems - समस्या (Things difficult to deal with)
Obsession - जुनून (State of thinking only about one thing)
oa:
This noun refers to a lack of interest, concern, or feeling towards something. It serves as the direct opposite of a fetish, which implies an unreasonable obsession or obsession.
Synonyms: Apathy (उदासीनता), Disregard (उपेक्षा), Neutrality (तटस्थता).
Antonyms: Fetish (मनोग्रस्‍तता), Obsession (जुनून), Interest (रुचि).

This term means something that is already decided or securely placed. It describes the state of a decision or object rather than the emotional intensity of an interest.
Synonyms: Decided (निश्चित), Settled (स्थिर), Firm (नियत).
Antonyms: Changeable (परिवर्तनशील), Flexible (लचीला), Variable (अस्थिर).

This plural noun refers to things that are difficult to deal with or understand. It identifies hurdles or issues rather than the psychological fixation implied by fetish.
Synonyms: Issues (समस्या), Hurdles (अड़चन), Difficulties (कठिनाई).
Antonyms: Solutions (समाधान), Benefits (लाभ), Advantages (फायदा).
